jobs.title: Wetland Biologist
jobs.description:
Matrix New World Engineering, a part of True Environmental and its partner firms, have united their strengths to establish the nation's premier environmental and engineering services consulting firm. This powerhouse organization offers an extensive range of services aimed at revolutionizing the built environment and preserving the natural one. Its diverse expertise encompasses environmental remediation, urban planning, engineering iconic coastal and marine structures, developing sustainable energy sources, and pioneering resource extraction methods. **Matrix New World** is seeking an experienced **Wetland Biologist** who desires a challenging career to join our well-established team of Environmental Scientists, GIS Analysts, and Land Surveying professionals to participate in projects throughout the Gulf Coast.

The successful candidate will also use GIS (ArcGIS Pro) and mobile data collection tools (ArcGIS Field Maps, Survey123, sub-meter GPS) to collect, review, and QA/QC field data, and will prepare basic maps and figures for wetland delineation reports and permit submittals.

* Working knowledge of ArcGIS Pro and core geoprocessing tools

* Strong attention to detail and data QA/QC habits
* Ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team with limited direction and oversight

* Excellent technical writing and oral communication skills
* Attention to detail along with strong organizational skills
* Strong problem-solving abilities and aptitude

jobs.title: WFH Remote Drone Supervisor
jobs.description:
Are you an FAA Part 107 Certified drone pilot looking to earn money remotely, all from the comfort of your home?

Fliteworks is expanding our team of remote drone supervisors to support our growing nationwide flight operations. We're looking for dependable pilots interested in full-time, part-time, or weekend opportunities.

We need pilots to log on when scheduled to fly and oversee its preflight checklist and flight. The process is very standardized, and the role of the pilot is to monitor the flight and step in if needed.

**Scheduling & Availability**

We offer flexible scheduling and work with pilots to coordinate missions based on their availability and our operational needs. We're currently looking for pilots interested in the following schedules:

* **Full-Time Availability:** Consistent weekday availability to support daily flight operations and multiple scheduled missions.
* **Part-Time Availability:** Flexible weekday availability for pilots looking to supplement their existing schedules.
* **Weekend Availability:** Pilots available on Saturday and Sunday to provide consistent weekend coverage. This can be alternating weekends.

Pilots can supervise individual missions lasting around 30 minutes or work multiple consecutive missions, depending on availability and operational demand.

**Please Note:** Flight operations are weather-dependent and subject to site conditions, equipment availability, and operational requirements. Scheduled missions may be delayed, rescheduled, or canceled, sometimes with limited advance notice. Pilots are compensated based on the time spent supervising missions. Actual working hours may vary from week to week.

**Responsibilities:**

* Work with us to schedule shifts, and log-in on time for the shifts you’ve scheduled.
* Look at video feeds, weather forecasts, and dashboard readouts to complete a preflight checklist and make sure the conditions are safe for the drone to fly.
* Monitor live video feed and dashboard while the drone is in flight to make sure it is flying safely.
* If necessary, control the drone or abort the mission using the dashboard.

**Job Requirements:**

* FAA Part 107 Certification
* Basic knowledge of drone operations and FAA regulations.
* Ability to assess weather conditions, airspace restrictions, and potential flight hazards
* Familiarity with drone flight systems and remote monitoring software
* A reliable internet connection
* A desktop or laptop computer
* A phone to reach you in emergencies

**Company Overview:**

Fliteworks is building a nationwide network of unmanned aircraft to keep watch over critical infrastructure, from highways, to pipelines, to power plants. We have FAA approval to deploy drones that don’t require on-site supervision, and we’re using this to bring visibility to even the most remote assets. Our mission is to transform infrastructure monitoring from a time-consuming, backlogged task into a continuous, mass-scale resource that prevents disasters and enables our society to build more than ever before.

Job Type: Contract

Pay: From $20.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Application Question(s):

* What is your availability (full-time, part-time, or weekends)?

License/Certification:

* FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certification (Required)

Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Environmental Law & Policy
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Environmental Law & Policy Instructor

**Classification:** Faculty, Online May Session

**Duration:** Three weeks (May 17 – June 4, 2027); one-session appointment

**Applications:** Review begins immediately; open until filled

**Location:** Online / Remote

**About Au Sable**

At Au Sable, we believe Christians should be leading the way in solving the earth’s toughest environmental challenges. Through hands-on learning in the outdoors, engaging professors who integrate faith into their instruction, and a supportive community of friends, we inspire and educate students to serve, protect and restore God’s earth. Our university-level courses emphasize scientific rigor, professional preparation, and Christian stewardship through field-based and online instruction.

**Environmental Law & Policy Faculty Position**

We seek applicants to teach ENVST 310: Environmental Law & Policy during the online May Session (May 17 - June 4, 2027). This three-credit course (75 equivalent contact hours) examines environmental policymaking at local, national, and international scales, with attention to climate and energy, resource management, relationships between scientific evidence and policy, environmental ethics, justice, and advocacy. Environmental Law & Policy is the required Category 1 course for Au Sable’s Environmental Policy & GIS Practitioner Certificate and may also be taken by students as an elective requirement for the Forest & Land Management Practitioner Certificate.

The course has an established, primarily asynchronous online structure with recorded lectures, assigned readings, frequent low-stakes quizzes, substantive discussion-board participation, and a small number of scheduled live meetings. Its major assessments have included analysis of a current policy, a policy proposal, and reflection on a Christian framework for environmental policymaking. The selected instructor will be expected to preserve course learning outcomes, provide regular substantive instructor-student interaction and timely feedback, and facilitate respectful analysis of politically-contested policy questions. Course delivery and grading are managed in Populi, with administrative and technical support available from Institute staff.

Because this is a short-term appointment in an established course, the faculty member will coordinate with the Institute to ensure continuity in the syllabus, materials, assessment design, and student learning expectations. The instructor will implement the Institute’s designated signature-assignment process, review course evaluations, and submit a short faculty assessment/reflection following the session. The ability to communicate Christian principles of creation care while engaging diverse perspectives with academic rigor and intellectual hospitality is essential.

**Course Description (2026–2027 Academic Catalog):** EnvSt 310 Environmental Law & Policy. 3 cr; 75 equivalent contact hrs. Analysis of the policy making process at local, national, and international scales with examination of environmental policy challenges including climate change, resource management and energy development. Students will interact with policy-makers, researchers, and land managers to consider linkages between policy and science and ways for science to inform the policy-making process. Environmental ethics, environmental justice, and environmental advocacy will also be considered. Interdisciplinary.

**Online Setting**

The course is offered entirely online through Au Sable’s learning-management system, Populi. Institute staff provide course-administration and technical support. The instructor is responsible for regular student engagement, instructional delivery, assessment, and coordination of access to course-specific learning resources.

**Faculty Qualifications**

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Relevant graduate degree (Master’s, JD, PhD, or equivalent; ABD considered where appropriate) in environmental law, public/environmental policy, political science, environmental studies, public administration, or a closely related field, with demonstrable subject expertise.

* Experience teaching university students and substantive knowledge of U.S. environmental policy and law, including the policy development process and its scientific context.

* Documented training in online teaching (or commitment to complete approved preparation before the course begins), and ability to provide regular instructor-student interaction, feedback, and effective use of a learning-management system.

* Ability to integrate Christian stewardship and ethics into instruction while facilitating respectful engagement with contrasting policy perspectives.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* University-level teaching in environmental law, policymaking, environmental justice, sustainability, or related interdisciplinary coursework.

* Professional policy or regulatory experience with agencies, advocacy organizations, consulting, or policy development.

* Documented online-teaching training, course design experience, and assessment of online student learning; experience using Populi or a comparable learning-management system.

**Diversity, Equity and Inclusion**

Au Sable Institute is committed to combating racism, sexism, and other systems of oppression. We strongly encourage applications from people of color, women, persons with disabilities, and all individuals who will contribute to the excellence of the Institute. Au Sable Institute does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or status as a veteran in any of its policies, practices, or procedures.

**Salary and Benefits**

Stipend is $4,050 for a 3-credit course (prorated from $5,400 for a 4-credit course). The appointment is fully remote; housing and travel are not required.

**Application Process**

Review of applications begins immediately and continues until the position is filled. Interested applicants should email heath.gar

jobs.title: Geospatial and Digital Innovation Development Leader
jobs.description:
Matrix New World Engineering, a part of True Environmental and its partner firms, have united their strengths to establish the nation's premier environmental and engineering services consulting firm. This powerhouse organization offers an extensive range of services aimed at revolutionizing the built environment and preserving the natural one. Its diverse expertise encompasses environmental remediation, urban planning, engineering iconic coastal and marine structures, developing sustainable energy sources, and pioneering resource extraction methods. Explore further at www.MWNE.com and True-Environmental.com to discover the full scope of our capabilities.

True Environmental is seeking a hands-on technical leader to drive geospatial, digital, and AI innovation into everything we do. Working directly with engineers, scientists, GIS staff, and project managers across our six practice groups (Natural Resources and Regulatory Services, Mining, Environmental, Engineering, Water Resources, and Federal) you will learn how each team delivers its work and build the tools, platforms, and workflows that make that work faster, more accurate, and more valuable to clients in the Transportation and Infrastructure, Water, Energy, Power and Utilities, Mining, Industrial, Environmental, and Natural Resources markets.

You will be the firm’s U.S.-based technical authority for enterprise GIS, geomatics, and digital solutions across all practices, and the person who turns emerging technology into everyday practice. You will design the geodatabases, write the scripts, build the applications, integrate the data feeds, and apply AI in a manner that improves how we compile data, detect change, and deliver results. Just as importantly, you will train project teams to use what you create, so innovation reaches every project. Alongside our technical leadership, you will represent the firm in front of clients and present at industry conferences, and you will coordinate with digital technology leaders in Canada to identify, develop, and leverage tools across True. The position reports to the Chief Operating Officer and works in a matrixed relationship with practice leads across the firm.

### **What You Will Do**

**Cross-Practice Technical Leadership**

* Act as the U.S. technical lead for geospatial and digital solutions, supporting all six practice groups: Natural Resources and Regulatory Services, Mining, Environmental, Engineering, Water Resources, and Federal.
* Partner with each practice to map current workflows, identify where spatial data and automation can remove manual effort or improve decision quality, and prioritize a development backlog.
* Establish firm-wide standards for geodatabase design, metadata, data governance, QA/QC, and deliverable formats so geospatial output is consistent regardless of practice or office.
* Coordinate with digital technology leaders in Canada to identify, develop, and leverage tools across True, aligning platforms and avoiding duplicated development.
* Serve as technical reviewer for geospatial deliverables and provide expert input on proposals when practices need a defined digital scope.

**Product and Platform Development**

* Design and build enterprise geodatabases, web-mapping applications, custom dashboards, and digital-twin platforms that integrate 2D/3D mapping, asset inventories, document repositories, point clouds, BIM/Revit models, and inspection and monitoring records.
* Develop repeatable analytical tools and workflows for recurring project needs, for example: cut/fill and dredging analysis, discharge and runout modeling, routing and constraint analysis, contaminant plume and exceedance visualization, impervious surface and flood-exposure analysis, and automated regulatory reporting (figures, tables, EDDs).
* Build and maintain field data collection applications (Survey123, Field Maps, Fulcrum, or custom) and the pipelines that move field data into enterprise databases and client deliverables.
* Integrate real-time and external data sources (IoT sensors, AIS, weather and environmental feeds, bathymetric and LiDAR scans) into living data products.
* Automate with Python, SQL, JavaScript, ModelBuilder, and FME; convert legacy CAD/MicroStation, Access, Excel, and PDF data into spatially enabled databases.

**Innovation and Technology Evaluation**

* Evaluate and pilot emerging capabilities, including GeoAI and LLM-assisted data compilation and metadata generation, automated defect and change detection from imagery and point clouds, open-source geospatial stacks, cloud deployment, and immersive/XR visualization, and establish practical, governed paths to adoption.
* Direct reality-capture programs in coordination with field teams: terrestrial and bathymetric LiDAR, sonar, UAS photogrammetry and inspection.
* Identify project-built tools that can be hardened into reusable firm assets or client-facing products.

**Client Representation, Enablement, and Training**

* Together with technical leadership, represent the firm in front of clients and present at industry conferences, user groups, and professional associations.
* Develop SOPs, written and video tutorials, and training programs so practice staff can use and maintain the tools you build.
* Mentor GIS analysts and developers across practices on development practices, database design, and scripting; you will influence and guide, not line-manage, these staff.

### **Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geography, Geospatial Science, Environmental Science/Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
* Authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.
* 20+ years of progressive geospatial and application-development experience, with substantial time as technical lead on multidisciplinary projects in an environmental, engineering, AEC, or public-sector setting.
* GISP certification (or ability to obtain within 12 months).
* Deep expertise in the Esri platform: ArcGIS Pro,

jobs.title: Research Environmental Scientist - Hydrometeorology
jobs.description:
Why RTI:

RTI International is an independent, scientific research institute dedicated to improving the human condition. Our vision is to address the world's most critical problems with technical and science-based solutions in pursuit of a better future. Clients rely on us to answer questions that demand an objective and multidisciplinary approach—one that integrates expertise across social, statistical, data, and laboratory sciences, engineering, and other technical disciplines to solve the world’s most challenging problems.  
  
We believe in the promise of science and technical solutions, and we push ourselves every day to deliver on that promise for the good of people, communities, and businesses in the US and around the world. If you are looking for the opportunity to make a real difference, RTI is the place for you.

About the Hiring Group:

Are you passionate about water resources and environmental science? RTI’s Water, Agriculture, Natural Resources, and Energy Solutions (WARES) Group is seeking a motivated Research Environmental Scientist to join our hydromet and flood risk team. We develop innovative tools and analytical methods that support hydropower owners, dam safety programs, and the broader water resources community.

Our team is recognized for expertise in precipitation frequency analysis and probable flood hazard assessments (PFHA). As a nonprofit research institute, RTI also supports internal R&D to drive innovation and create real-world impact.

As part of the team, you will contribute to a broad range of meteorological frequency analyses and extreme storm analyses. Candidates should be able to demonstrate experience or exposure in several of the areas listed below (not all are required).

**Why Join Us?**

* Work on impactful domestic and international water resources projects.
* Apply state-of-the-art computational tools to complex water management challenges.
* Help advance modeling technologies and analytical methods.
* Collaborate with leading experts in a supportive, multidisciplinary environment.
* This position can be either based in RTI’s U.S. office in Research Triangle Park, NC, or it can be fully remote. Teleworking is permitted within the United States only.

What You'll Do:

You will support project teams requiring meteorological expertise to support hydrologic hazards, flood forecasting, and other analyses. You will work daily using scripts, tools, and techniques to efficiently prepare and analyze meteorological data including addressing climate change impacts using GCM data. You will also support project management and grow project portfolios.

**Essential Duties:**

* Collaborate with the Hydromet team to implement and enhance RTI’s hydrometeorological analysis tools.
* Perform data processing, quality control, and automation using scripts and tools.
* Collect, process, quality control, and statistically analyze large datasets of meteorological information.
* Develop code to improve existing hydrometeorological analysis tools and link to other existing hydrologic modeling or forecasting tools.
* Contribute to precipitation frequency and probable maximum precipitation analyses in support of dam safety projects.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
We're seeking a part-time GIS analyst to apply spatial analysis and remote sensing to our ecological planning work.

You'll work alongside our ecologists and designers to map habitat, tree canopy, and land cover; screen sites and portfolios using desktop data; and produce maps and spatial datasets to inform goal-setting, site design, and monitoring. Projects range from single urban sites in the San Francisco Bay Area to multi-site portfolios across the US and Europe. You'll also help us organize our GIS data and build workflows that make analyses repeatable from one project to the next.

The ideal candidate is experienced in ArcGIS and remote sensing and has worked with landscape and ecological datasets such as land cover, vegetation and habitat maps, and species occurrence records.

This is a part-time, hourly position with a flexible schedule where hours will vary depending on project needs.

**Minimum qualifications**

* BS in GIS, geography, ecology, environmental science, or a related field
* Expertise in ArcGIS Pro, including spatial analysis, geoprocessing, and cartography
* Expertise in remote sensing, including classification and analysis of aerial, satellite, or lidar data
* Experience working with landscape and ecological datasets, such as land cover, vegetation and habitat maps, tree canopy, and species occurrence data
* Availability for part-time, hourly work on a flexible, project-based schedule

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Spatial analysis and remote sensing**

* Map existing land cover, habitat types, tree canopy, and impervious surfaces from aerial and satellite imagery, lidar, and land-use classification data
* Conduct desktop baseline assessments and regional context evaluations for individual sites and multi-site portfolios, including review of historical imagery
* Conduct spatial analyses to understand spatial patterns and processes and summarize spatial information.
* Compile and analyze species occurrence data from sources such as GBIF, iNaturalist, and eBird to characterize species and habitat value
* Evaluate landscape context, including habitat connectivity and proximity to sensitive habitats, waterways, and protected areas
* Quantify outcomes such as habitat area and condition, canopy cover, and heat island and carbon benefits to support biodiversity metrics and sustainability reporting

**Data management and workflows**

* Help organize, document, and maintain our GIS data library, project files, and metadata
* Help establish standard, repeatable workflows so desktop screenings and habitat analyses can be applied consistently across projects and portfolios
* Integrate field data from our ecologists, such as habitat maps, vegetation condition assessments, and survey points, with desktop datasets
* Set up and maintain field data collection tools such as ArcGIS Field Maps
* Check spatial data for accuracy and completeness before it goes into analyses and deliverables

**Products**

* Produce clear, well-designed maps and graphics for slide decks, reports, and client presentations
* Deliver GIS files and spreadsheet summaries of spatial results to clients and design teams

**Working style**

* Attention to detail and a commitment to accurate, well-documented data
* Clear written and verbal communication with teammates and clients
* Ability to work independently and as part of a distributed team
* Work closely with ecologists, designers, and partner landscape architects and engineers to translate spatial findings into design and strategy recommendations

**PREFERRED SKILLS**

**GIS workflows**

* Ability to help organize GIS data and establish standardized, well-documented workflows for a small team
* Experience automating repeatable analyses with Python (ArcPy) or ModelBuilder
* Familiarity with ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Field Maps

**Technical**

* Experience with Google Earth Engine and R for spatial analysis
* Familiarity with biodiversity assessment frameworks, such as habitat condition scoring or biodiversity net gain metrics

\*\*\*\*

Second Nature Ecology + Design provides innovative biodiversity services to create ecological and social impact. Collaborating with leading corporations, creative firms, and high-impact NGOs, we apply state-of-the-art science and tailored support to bring the essential benefits of nature to diverse settings. Drawing on our team of ecologists and designers, we develop award-winning nature strategies that catalyze biodiversity, climate resilience, and human well-being. Our distributed team has locations across the US and Europe, with our core location in the SF Bay Area.

* Strong written communication skills in English.

We are seeking a highly experienced Strategic Advisor specializing in Environmental Due Diligence (Phase I ESA and PCA) to guide the development of Inspectli’s AI-driven software platform. In this advisory role, you will not be conducting field investigations or writing reports. Instead, you will act as the bridge between ground truth industry expertise and our engineering team. Your insights will shape how our software automates data extraction, ensures regulatory compliance, and meets the rigorous risk-tolerance standards of commercial lenders and engineering firms.

**Responsibilities**

* Review and pressure-test automated Phase I ESA and PCA outputs generated by our software to ensure they meet or exceed industry expectations.
* Advise our engineering team on the practical nuances of ASTM E1527 and E2018 compliance, identifying potential real-world pitfalls in automated data extraction (e.g., EDR data, historical city directories).
* Provide strategic insight into the commercial lender perspective, defining exactly what risk officers care about when reviewing due diligence reports.
* Help prioritize our product roadmap by identifying the most significant workflow bottlenecks and manual pain points in traditional report writing.
* Act as a sounding board for new feature development, effectively translating environmental risk concepts into actionable guidance for software engineers.

**Requirements**

jobs.description:
Job Description
  
  
Senior Geospatial Data Analyst / Geospatial Data Remediation SME
  
**Company:** Silverthorne Advisory Group
  
**Location:** Fully Remote
  
**Clearance:** Active Secret Clearance Required
  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time, Salaried
  
**Experience Level:** Journeyman, Senior, or Subject Matter Expert (SME)
  
**Education:** Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree
  
  
Position Overview
  
Silverthorne Advisory Group is seeking a skilled Geospatial Data Analyst / Geospatial Data Remediation Specialist to support U.S. Air Force real property and geospatial data quality initiatives. This role focuses on identifying, analyzing, and remediating complex spatial and attribute data discrepancies across enterprise geospatial datasets and real property management systems.
  
The ideal candidate will have extensive experience with enterprise Geographic Information Systems (GIS), spatial data validation, photogrammetry, engineering drawings, aerial imagery interpretation, and data remediation. The successful candidate will work with Geospatial Integration Offices (GIO), Real Property personnel, and other stakeholders to improve data accuracy, resolve discrepancies, support audit readiness, and strengthen the integrity of Air Force geospatial and infrastructure data.
  
  
Photogrammetry experience is highly preferred, particularly experience interpreting aerial imagery and extracting or validating geospatial information. Silverthorne is especially interested in candidates who can operate at the Subject Matter Expert (SME) level, bringing deep technical expertise, independent problem-solving capabilities, and the ability to lead complex data remediation efforts.
  
This is a fully remote position, with targeted site visits as needed to support field validation activities.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
Geospatial Analysis and Data Remediation
  
Identify, investigate, and remediate complex spatial and attribute data discrepancies across Air Force geospatial datasets.
  
Analyze linear asset geometry, segmentation, length, and classification discrepancies between GIS layers and real property management systems, including NexGen IT and TRIRIGA.
  
Perform advanced spatial quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) to identify missing, obsolete, duplicated, fragmented, or inaccurate geospatial data.
  
Diagnose root causes of data discrepancies, including topology errors, schema misalignments, and broken linear networks.
  
Develop and implement systematic remediation plans to improve data accuracy, consistency, and reliability.
  
Validate corrected datasets and document remediation activities, outcomes, and remaining data gaps.
  
Interpret aerial imagery and other geospatial sources to support spatial analysis, asset identification, and data validation.
  
  
Technical Assistance and Field Validation
  
Lead virtual technical assistance sessions with base-level Geospatial Integration Offices (GIO) and Real Property personnel to troubleshoot complex mapping and data quality issues.
  
Provide technical guidance on geospatial data standards, validation methodologies, and remediation best practices.
  
Conduct targeted site visits and field validation activities when desktop analysis and existing records are insufficient.
  
Utilize field collection technologies, including high-accuracy GNSS/GPS equipment, mobile LiDAR, and rangefinders, as appropriate.
  
Establish clear validation boundaries for underground utilities and linear assets, translating data uncertainty into defined engineering and surveying requirements.
  
Coordinate with stakeholders to resolve discrepancies between mapped assets, engineering records, field observations, and property management systems.
  
  
Reporting and Data Visualization
  
Translate complex geospatial findings, data remediation results, and audit progress into clear technical documentation, corrective action reports, and executive summaries.
  
Develop dashboards and reporting tools to monitor data quality, remediation progress, and post-remediation performance.
  
Leverage data visualization tools, including Power BI, to communicate trends, identify recurring issues, and support data-driven decision-making.
  
Track key performance indicators and document improvements in data completeness, accuracy, and consistency.
  
  
Experience Levels and Compensation
  
Compensation is based on experience, education, technical expertise, and overall qualifications.

**About the Organization**

Now is a great time to join Redhorse Corporation. We are a solution-driven company delivering data insights and technology solutions to customers with missions critical to U.S. national interests. We’re looking for thoughtful, skilled professionals who thrive as trusted partners building technology-agnostic solutions and want to apply their talents supporting customers with difficult and important mission sets.

**About the Role**

Redhorse transforms the way government uses data and technology. To support this mission, we are seeking a motivated Junior GIS Analyst to serve as a Common Installation Picture (CIP) Helpdesk and SDSFIE Specialist on a long-term engagement supporting the Army National Guard (ARNG).

This is a work-from-home position that **requires the candidate to be local to the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area** to support periodic local stakeholder coordination and meetings. You will perform as part of an integrated, mission-driven team dedicated to developing, maintaining, and reporting critical geospatial data layers depicting the built and natural environments across all ARNG States and Territories. Your work will directly empower ARNG leadership with real-time Situational Awareness (SA) over real property and environmental assets, maintaining strict data integrity through DoD and Army Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) standards.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* **Data Aggregation & QA/QC:** Implement structured workflows for Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) and enterprise aggregation of ARNG State and Territory geospatial data and metadata.
* **CIP Quality Reporting:** Conduct data quality analyses and generate discrepancy reports utilizing Python-based validation tools to assess geodatabase geometry, schema, and attribution.
* **Tool Maintenance & Optimization:** Identify, recommend, and execute modifications to existing CIP tools and Python scripts to optimize validation and reporting capabilities.
* **Application Support:** Support and update the Geospatial Layer and Attribute Database (GLAD) application to meet evolving program specifications.
* **Helpdesk Support & Troubleshooting:** Serve as a frontline technical resource to field questions, resolve user issues, and ensure efficient, compliant submission of CIP data from field installations.
* **Standards Migration & Training:** Support the enterprise migration and compliance of Spatial Data Standards for Facilities, Infrastructure, and the Environment (SDSFIE), and facilitate user training sessions for stakeholders.

* **Location:** Must be local to the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area (or within direct rail/commuting access) to attend periodic on-site meetings and customer engagements.
* **Education & Experience**: Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 2 years of related professional GIS experience.
* **Programming & Scripting**: Working knowledge of Python, specifically for automating workflows and modifying geospatial validation scripts.
* **GIS Expertise**: Demonstrated knowledge of GIS concepts, cartographic and geospatial production techniques, and digital spatial data formats.
* **Software Proficiency**: Hands-on experience with ArcGIS Pro, SQL, and Microsoft Office Suite.
* **Enterprise Systems**: Experience utilizing Enterprise GIS, Portal for ArcGIS, and ArcGIS Dashboards.
* **Eligibility**: Must be a U.S. Citizen eligible to pass a federal background check/favorable suitability determination to support DoD systems.

* **DoD & Military Familiarity**: Prior experience supporting military customers, with familiarity regarding military command structures, installation workflows, and decision-making processes.
* **Data Standards**: Hands-on familiarity with SDSFIE schema requirements and real property asset management systems.
* **Independent Drive**: Demonstrated ability to work effectively from home in a collaborative, distributed team environment.
* **Adaptability & Communication**: Strong interpersonal communication skills, sharp attention to detail, and the flexibility to adapt to changing mission priorities.

jobs.title: 3D & LiDAR Data Annotation Analyst
jobs.description:
About The Role

We’re building high-quality ground-truth datasets used to train and validate perception models for autonomous and operator-assisted machines working in complex, real-world environments.

As a Data Annotation Analyst, you’ll work with camera imagery, video, and LiDAR point clouds to create precise labels that help perception systems understand objects, people, terrain, and surrounding environments. You’ll work in specialized annotation tools, following detailed specifications while balancing accuracy, consistency, and production volume.

Your Impact

Annotate 2D and 3D objects across images, video, and LiDAR point clouds, including vehicles, machinery, people, signage, and environmental features.
Create and maintain accurate segmentation, object tracking, pose, and keypoint annotations across sequences.
Apply detailed annotation guidelines, including class definitions, occlusion rules, object thresholds, and inclusion/exclusion criteria.
Review your work, respond to QA feedback, and maintain established quality and accuracy standards.
Identify and escalate ambiguous scenes, sensor artifacts, tooling issues, and gaps in specifications rather than making assumptions.
Document data quality and tooling issues with clear details and reproduction steps.
Participate in calibration sessions, guideline reviews, and team standups to maintain consistent interpretations.
Share observations that help improve annotation guidelines, taxonomies, and edge-case documentation.

Success in this role means producing accurate, consistent annotations at the expected volume while helping maintain a reliable, high-quality dataset.

What You Bring

Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy while performing repetitive, visually intensive work for extended periods.
Strong spatial reasoning skills, including the ability to interpret 3D environments and understand object size, position, and orientation.
Ability to learn and navigate complex, purpose-built software and become productive with keyboard shortcuts and other tooling features.
Experience working in a fast-paced, scaled environment with defined productivity, quality, or accuracy targets.
Experience with image annotation GenAI workflows
Reliable high-speed internet, a distraction-free workspace, and the ability to work on a company-provisioned machine within a controlled environment.

Nice to Haves

Associate or bachelor’s degree.
Experience with image, video, LiDAR, or 3D annotation tools.
Experience with subsurface utility engineering (SUE), construction surveying, surveying, GIS, or other work involving spatial interpretation of physical environments.
Experience with AutoCAD or similar type tools
Experience in construction, mining, agriculture, industrial operations, or heavy equipment environments.
Familiarity with point cloud data, sensor fusion, or camera-LiDAR calibration.
Experience working with autonomous vehicles, robotics, or machine perception datasets.

$30 - $32 an hour

Why You’ll Love Working Here

At Appen, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence. We value curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to delivering the highest-quality AI solutions for frontier models.

You’ll work on complex challenges that shape the future of AI across industries and geographies, alongside talented people in a culture that values humility over ego. You’ll have the flexibility to deliver in a way that works for you and your team, supported by tools, resources and development opportunities to continue to build your capability over time.

About Appen

Appen has been a leader in AI training data for over 30 years. We specialise in human generated data to train, fine tune, and evaluate models across generative AI, large language models, computer vision, and speech recognition. Our AI assisted data annotation platform and global crowd of more than 1 million contributors in over 200 countries support model pre-training, supervised fine tuning, evaluation and benchmarking, safety and red teaming, and multilingual global expansion.

Preparing and reviewing documents in compliance with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right-of-way activities
Planning and reviewing work related to evaluation and consideration of cultural and tribal resources
Communicating and delivering project information to Tribal representatives and governments as needed to engage Tribal participation or consultation on Sonoma Water projects and initiatives
Coordinating with Tribal representatives and governments in their review of Sonoma Water projects and environmental documents to facilitate receipt of and responses to Tribal comments
Managing agreements with consultant archeologists and drafting and managing Tribal monitoring agreements
Attending meetings (in the office, virtual, or in the field) with staff and managers from other Sonoma Water divisions
Regularly updating and working with the Environmental Resources Division Manager and Executive Team to develop and implement strategic positions supporting tribal consultations

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess Experience In Natural Resources, Water Resources Planning, And/or Community Liaison Experience, And Many Of The Following

Experience negotiating with Tribal communities and governments, regulatory agencies, and other project stakeholders
Excellent understanding and in-depth knowledge of Native American culture, history, tradition, perspectives and experiences
An understanding of tribal communities and governance in the Russian River watershed and/or San Francisco Bay region
Demonstrated knowledge of government-to-government sovereignty protocols
Demonstrated knowledge of AB 52 and the CEQA environmental review process for Tribal stakeholders
Strong stakeholder relationships with Native American Tribal governments and Tribal communities, demonstrated experience with Tribes, and knowledge and experience with industry best practices.
Experience organizing and facilitating public and stakeholder meetings, responding to concerns and issues from stakeholders, and gaining consensus on projects

Note: This position typically works Monday-Friday during regular business hours but may be required to work evening or weekend shifts to attend public meetings and community events. Work includes in-office (in-person) meetings, video conferencing (telework), travel to regional meetings, conferences and visits to project sites in terrestrial and aquatic environments during variable (sometimes inclement) weather conditions.

About Sonoma Water

Sonoma Water is a special district formed by the California State Legislature in 1949 and is responsible for providing a safe and reliable water supply to its customers in Sonoma and Marin counties. Sonoma Water also maintains 75 miles of flood control channels and provides sanitation services. Employing approximately 250 employees, Sonoma Water consists of four divisions, including Engineering & Resource Planning, Environmental Resources, Business Services & External Affairs, and Water/Wastewater Operations & Maintenance. Sonoma Water supports the concept of environmental sustainability, focusing on renewable power sources, and strives to be a leader in its water use efficiency and fishery restoration programs.

Employees of Sonoma Water are employees of a special district and are not subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance of the County of Sonoma.

What We Offer

Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits* including:

Hybrid Telework - A schedule that meets the needs of our staff, department operations, and the communities we serve may be available depending on the assignment
Salary Advancement - A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
Paid Time Off - Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays, and an additional 8 floating holiday hours per year
County Paid Health Premium Contributions - 100% premium contribution for the majority of employee-only and employee + family health plan options
Post-Retirement Health Reimbursement Arrangement - County contributions to help fund post-retirement health insurance/benefits
Retirement - A pension fully integrated with Social Security
Paid Parental Leave - May be eligible for up to 8 weeks (320 hours) after 12 months of County employment
Additional Benefits - Excellent dental, vision, disability, life insurance, employee assistance program, professional development, and more
Student Loan Debt Relief - County employees may be eligible for Public Service Loan Forgiveness through the U.S. Department of Education
Salary is negotiable within the established range. Benefits described herein do not represent a contract and may be changed without notice. Additional information can be found in the Service Employees International Union Local 1021 Memorandum Of Understanding (SEIU MOU) and our Employee Benefits Directory .

Sonoma Water is currently recruiting to fill a Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist - Tribal Liaison position. This employment list may also be used to fill future full-time, part-time, or extra-help (temporary) positions as they occur during the active status of the list. Qualified County employees who wish to be considered for future positions should consider applying to this recruitment.

Experience & Education:
Any combination of education, training, and experience which would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities listed. Normally, this would include a Bachelor's degree in planning, engineering, water related, physical, and/or biological sciences, environmental studies, environmental law, natural resource or watershed management, or a closely related field; and three years of experience with engineering, environmental impact assessments and permitting, including at least one year at the level of Water Agency Environmental Specialist II, or equivalent.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

analyze and design project reports and determine probable effect on environment; write effectively and to use good judgment in the assembling, evaluation, and use of information; prepare and present various reports on the effect of projects on the environment to advisory boards, commissions, and elected bodies; assist in planning, scheduling, and training of other employees; make mathematical calculations; analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action; establish and maintain effective relationships with other staff members, staff of other agencies, organizations, and the general public; prepare and disseminate information to media and others; prepare a wide range of clear, concise and informative reports, correspondence and brochures; operate office equipment including computers and supporting word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.

Fish and Wildlife

fishery and wildlife management principles and methods; the classification, life histories, ecology, habitats, parasites, and diseases of fresh-water fish and California wildlife; research methodology; wildlife resource management, including watershed, range, forestry, fishery, wildlife and recreation techniques and equipment in making biological investigations of fish and wildlife; materials, equipment, and techniques used in fishery and wildlife habitat improvement; fishery considerations in the design, location, and construction of public works projects relating to streams, lakes, and ecological areas.

vegetation and soil management principles and methods; the classification and morphology of soil, and botanical identification, classification, and life histories of plants; botanical soil research methodology; techniques and equipment in making botanical and soil investigations; materials, equipment, and techniques used in botanical habitat enhancements or soil structure improvements; botanical considerations in the design, location, and construction of public construction projects relating to wetlands, riparian areas and other ecological areas.

Arboricultural/Revegetation

the classification and identification of native plants and ornamental trees; the growth habits, parasites, diseases, habitat, and life histories of native plants and ornamental trees; sources of native plants; soil amendments and fertilizers; irrigation methods, needs, and materials; erosion control methods and materials; planting monitoring and maintenance methods; tree management principles and methods; research methodologies; forestry, woodland and range resource management; techniques used in arboriculture; considerations needed to design, locate, and construct revegetation projects in urban and natural settings and to be compatible with the desired function of flood control, water supply, and sanitation facilities; arboricultural considerations in the design, location, and construction of public projects.

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati

Founded in 1819, the University of Cincinnati ranks among the nation’s best urban public research universities. Home to more than 53,600 students, 12,000 faculty and staff, and over 360,000 living alumni, UC, a Carnegie 1 institution, combines research prowess with a physical setting The New York Times has called “the most ambitious campus design program in the country." UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.

UC is a mission-driven organization where we are committed to student success and positively transforming the community through scholarship and service. We thrive on innovation, making an impact, and fostering an environment where staff and faculty are key contributors to UC’s success.

Job Overview

As one of the oldest medical schools in the country, the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine (COM) has a reputation for training best-in-class health care professionals and developing cutting-edge procedures and research that improves the health and clinical care of patients. In partnership with the UC Health academic healthcare system and Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, College of Medicine’s faculty are transforming the world of medicine every day. The Department of Environmental and Public Health Sciences is a top-tier department with world-renowned faculty and staff.

The Department of Environmental and Public Health Sciences (DEPHS) at the College of Medicine (COM) seeks an outstanding individual to fill a faculty position at the Assistant Professor level to join its fast-growing Public Health Programs.

The successful candidate will serve in a key leadership role supporting the Great Lakes OSHA Training Institute (OTI) Education Center and advancing the University's mission in occupational and environmental health, workforce development, and community engagement. Specific research areas of interest include health policy, health services, health economics, health management, health system/program evaluation, comparison and implementation, and/or health technology and outcome assessments. The appointee can anticipate an opportunity to become a member of several multidisciplinary research/educational centers/institutes including an NIOSH-funded Education and Research Center (ERC); the NIH funded Center for Clinical and Translational Science and Training (CCTST); and UC’s Cancer Institute, Neuroscience Institute and Cardiovascular Institute. He/she can expect routine interaction with faculty at the Cincinnati Children’s Medical Center and the Cincinnati VA Hospital Medical Center, as well as with colleagues at the NIOSH and the US EPA.

Essential Functions

Manage Departmental OSHA continuing education programs, including student portal, payment management, and certification distribution
Teach public health courses at the undergraduate and/or graduate level in the areas of health services, health systems, population health, environmental health, qualitative methods, and policy or other relevant topics as needed
Advise and mentor students in academic development and achievement as well as in applied practical experience/integrated learning experiences
Assist with MPH curriculum development, innovation, and continuous quality improvement as well as program assessment, and involvement with professional societies through service
Collaborate with MPH faculty and leadership to ensure program success, student satisfaction, and alignment with workforce needs
Participate in MPH program meetings, accreditation preparation, strategic planning, and departmental service activities
Establish, implement, and uphold MPH policies to ensure the effective delivery and management of all assigned courses and program activities
Undertake other duties assigned from the MPH Program.

Minimum Requirements

Doctoral degree (e.g., DrPH, PhD, or equivalent) in public health or a related field

Required Experience

Demonstrated excellence in teaching and research evidenced by strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals. Candidates for a tenured appointment should demonstrate intellectual leadership and impact on the field and potential significant contributions to the department, University of Cincinnati, and wider scholarly community.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

Office environment/no specific unusual physical or environmental demands.

Compensation And Benefits

UC offers an exceptional benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and work-life balance. (UC Benefits) Eligibility may vary by position and FTE status. Highlights include:

Comprehensive Tuition Remission

UC provides tuition remission for you and your eligible dependents, covering tuition costs for nearly all undergraduate and graduate programs offered by the university.

As a UC employee, you won’t contribute to Social Security (except Medicare). Instead, you’ll choose between state pension plans (OPERS, STRS) or an Alternative Retirement Plan (ARP), with UC contributing 14–18% of your salary based on position.

UC prioritizes work-life balance with a generous time-off policy, including:

6 weeks of paid parental leave for new parents

jobs.description:
Description

We are looking for an Applications Engineer to join the Fauna Robotics support team. This role is hands-on technical problem-solving combined with operational ownership that helps the team scale. You will be a primary point of contact for customers experiencing issues with Fauna robots in the field, responsible for diagnosing problems that span hardware and software, and driving those issues to resolution with a high degree of independence. You will take active ownership of building and improving support infrastructure: establishing the tools, processes, documentation, and feedback loops that the team needs as our customer fleet grows.

You will work directly with highly technical customers including engineers, scientists, and researchers, conducting troubleshooting across mechanical, electrical, and software systems and driving issues to root cause and resolution.

You will work as part of a cross-functional support team that includes field engineers and technical support staff, collaborating on issue resolution from initial diagnosis through on-site repair.

Key job responsibilities

Serve as a primary technical point of contact for customer-reported issues with Fauna robots, conducting remote troubleshooting and driving problems to root cause and resolution across hardware and software domains.
Develop and maintain support infrastructure including ticketing/case management, knowledge base, troubleshooting playbooks, and corrective action documentation.
Analyze and report on support metrics (response time, resolution time, issue categorization, repeat failure rates) to identify trends, surface insights, and inform product improvements.
Communicate field issues clearly to engineering and software teams through structured reporting, advocating for resolution priority by providing field impact context and detailed reproduction steps.
Refine and improve escalation criteria and handoff processes for issues requiring on-site field support or bench-level repair, identifying gaps and driving process improvements.
Create and maintain customer-facing and internal support documentation including troubleshooting guides, FAQs, known-issue bulletins, and repair procedures.
Collaborate with field engineers by providing diagnostic context and handoff documentation when issues require on-site intervention.
Proactively identify recurring issue patterns, build decision trees, and develop tools or scripts that accelerate troubleshooting and reduce resolution time.

Basic Qualifications

Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
Experience troubleshooting and documenting findings
Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems, or experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities and experience in software development
4 years of experience in a technical support, applications engineering, systems engineering, or field engineering role, or equivalent hands-on experience working with robotic or electromechanical systems.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to technical audiences, both verbally and in writing.
Experience documenting technical processes, writing troubleshooting guides, or building knowledge base content.
Ability to independently manage multiple open issues simultaneously, prioritize based on severity and customer impact, and drive problems to resolution.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with robotic systems in a support, integration, test, or applications role.
Familiarity with hardware troubleshooting including mechanical assemblies, actuators, sensors, and electrical systems.
Experience building or owning support documentation, knowledge bases, or operational processes.
Background supporting highly technical customers (researchers, engineers, scientists).
Experience setting up or administering case management or ticketing systems, not just using them.
Familiarity with ROS, embedded systems, or common robotics middleware.
Exposure to field service operations, spare parts management, or repair workflows.

Job Description

Overview

The Superintendent - Environmental Quality administers, oversees, manages, and monitors all operation activities in Pretreatment, Industrial Monitoring, Liquid Waste, and Special Projects & Outreach or Laboratory within the Pretreatment and Laboratory Services (PALS) Division of the Dallas Water Utilities, or/and oversees Park Conservation and Natural Resources, manages and oversees wildlife habitat efforts, manages Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program and staff, coordinates interdepartmental conservation efforts.

Essential Functions

Manages, directs, and leads all operations and activities of the Pretreatment or Laboratory operations or various departmental initiatives regarding Habitat Management, Natural Resource Conservation, or/and environmental strategic planning through supervisors for compliance with TCEQ's Pretreatment permit and other Federal and State regulatory requirements; ensures that all acceptable operating procedures are followed and that operations are efficient and follow regulatory requirements.
Prepares and presents clear, complete, and concise correspondence and technical reports; coordinates and collaborates with other City departments; interacts, engages, and communicates with TCEQ and EPA regarding current regulations, permit compliance, and other matters regarding wastewater operations or/and wildlife conservation, natural resource conservation, pest management.
Manages the hiring and performance evaluation procedures for the department; approves and enforces discipline, verifies and approves time, manages service contracts, equipment, and technology and facilitates departmental success and adherence to permitting and regulatory standards; hears and resolves grievances and implements disciplinary actions when necessary.
Develops and implements long range plans, programs, and schedules to ensure operational efficiency and compliance; determines goals and objectives needing emphasis; directs and coordinates work through supervisors, staff or/and volunteer groups, and provides coaching, advice, counsel, or technical direction as needed; prioritizes tasks, schedules and assigns various requests, and administers City policies and procedures.
Responds to, engages with, and oversees the handling of customer requests and inquiries; acts as a liaison with TCEQ, EPA, and other organizations to improve customer service and regulatory compliance while ensuring safety and City standards.
Supervises the preparation of Pretreatment or Laboratory or/and other reports and documents; coordinates and facilitates the provision of Pretreatment or Laboratory supplies, or/and equipment maintenance contracts, or/and the oversight of maintenance agreements for Pretreatment or Laboratory software and systems; or/and prepares the Annual Pretreatment or Laboratory Report, and oversees the compliance of other regulatory reporting.
Develops and implements budget for department and operations; inspects work, audits activities, and identifies equipment that needs to be procured; attends meetings with upper management regarding operating budget preparation and approval.
Coaches, advises, counsels and instructs employees; identifies all training needs for employees; interviews and makes selection on candidates for filling positions, recommends terminations, and facilitates promotions; hears and resolves serious complaints or simple grievances from employees and refers serious grievances to higher level managers.
Finds and implements methods to improve production or effectiveness; oversees the inspection of pretreatment or laboratory procedures, or/and maintenance activities, and project implementation; approves employee hours and ensures adherence to all personnel and departmental policies and procedures.
Performs any and all other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge And Skills

Knowledge of departmental management.
Knowledge of Water and Wastewater systems and general equipment, facilities, and plant maintenance or/and Natural Resources/Parks Conservation, Wildlife Habitat Management.
Knowledge of inspection procedures and environmental compliance standards.
Knowledge of local, state, and federal regulations relevant to the operations of the Pretreatment program standards or/and Pesticide Management, Forestry/Natural Resources Management and other regulatory requirements
Ability to prioritize work, provide training, and facilitate efficient service delivery.
Ability to follow and give oral and written instructions and read charts and maintain written records.
Ability to participate in budget development, procurement activities, and inventory management.
Ability to maintain record keeping or work log system.
Communicating effectively verbally and in writing.
Knowledge of Federal, State, local standards that affect park activities.
Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Education

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in a Biology, Chemistry, Engineering or Environmental Science field.

Experience

Five (5) years of experience in environmental/industrial waste control, laboratory operations/management, basic chemical analysis, water/soil/air quality sample collection or wastewater collection/pretreatment discharge monitoring.

AND

Two (2) years of supervisory/management involved working with federal and state environmental regulatory agencies (Environmental Protection Agency-EPA, Texas Commission on Environmental Quality-TCEQ) (This experience may be included in the required experience listed above.)

Equivalency(ies)

An associate degree in any field plus seven (7) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
A bachelor's degree or higher in a non-specified field plus seven (7) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
A master's degree or higher in a specified field plus three (3) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

Salary Range

$89,440.00 - $111,800.00

The salary listed on this job posting is the starting salary range; amount offered will depend upon qualifications.

Chuyển đổi hình ảnh sản phẩm may mặc từ ảnh chụp thành  bản vẽ kỹ thuật 2D dạng flat-lay đối xứng
Đọc và phân tích bảng thông số kích thước để đảm bảo bản vẽ tuân thủ đúng kích thước, tỷ lệ, vị trí artwork và khu vực in.
Xây dựng các layout kỹ thuật thể hiện rõ cấu trúc và hình dạng của sản phẩm, đảm bảo các đường vector sạch, chính xác, đối xứng và phù hợp với yêu cầu kỹ thuật
Kiểm tra và đối chiếu file thiết kế với hình ảnh sản phẩm và thông số kỹ thuật trước khi bàn giao. Các file thiết kế này sẽ được sử dụng như bản thiết kế kỹ thuật (technical blueprint) cho quy trình sản xuất và in ấn 

Quyền lợi:

Mức lương từ 6.900.000 - 7.300.000 VNĐ

2 tháng đầu hưởng 85%, review lần đầu sau 6 tháng.
Thưởng thi đua cuối tháng theo năng lực, thưởng lễ, Tết theo quy định trong từng thời kỳ.
Thưởng, lương tháng 13, xét tăng lương định kỳ hàng năm, tăng lương đột xuất theo năng lực.
Cung cấp đầy đủ trang thiết bị làm việc.
Hỗ trợ vé gửi xe, vé xe bus hàng tháng
Hưởng đầy đủ các chính sách BHXH, BHYT, BHTN theo Luật Lao động của Nhà nước.
Cơ hội phát triển nghề nghiệp, học hỏi trong công việc
Được tham gia các câu lạc bộ có hỗ trợ kinh phí từ Công đoàn: Yoga, cầu lông, đá bóng,...
Tham gia các lớp học tiếng anh miễn phí

Sử dụng tốt Adobe Illustrator: Có kiến thức về Pen Tool, Pathfinder, Compound Paths, quản lý Artboard và các công cụ đo lường chính xác.
Có khả năng sử dụng Astute Graphics (plugin MirrorMe) hoặc các công cụ vector CAD tiêu chuẩn là 1 lợi thế

Chú trọng đến chi tiết: Tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt các yêu cầu ở cấp độ chi tiết như quy tắc đặt tên layer, tỷ lệ đường nét và tiêu chuẩn cấu trúc file.

jobs.title: Senior Wetland and Waterways Permitting Specialist
jobs.description:
What We're Looking For

At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners.

This opportunity entails serving as a technical expert in wetland and waterways permitting for complex infrastructure projects. The role focuses on applying environmental planning strategies, regulatory knowledge, and technical expertise to support permitting, compliance, and mitigation efforts. Responsibilities include conducting wetland delineations, preparing permit applications, coordinating with regulatory agencies, and developing mitigation plans. This position also involves analyzing environmental data, preparing documentation, and creating visuals to communicate findings effectively. You will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams from concept development through project completion, ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations. The position may lead technical production for permitting assignments and occasionally serve as a Project Manager for select medium and large-scale projects.

What You’ll Do

Under minimal direction, performs a variety of more highly complex professional planning, environmental planning, landscape architecture and urban design project responsibilities, and leads technical tasks.
Writes and/or reviews major sections of and leads production of plans, studies, reports, and environmental documents for projects. Coordinates and synthesizes the contributions of others.
Leads, prepares, and reviews graphics, technical reports, work plans, scopes of work, fee proposals, and responses to Request for Proposals for projects. Prepares and reviews budgets, invoicing, and billing.
Leads public and stakeholder engagement and presents information to the community.
Provides guidance and mentors staff.
Leads coordination with clients, sub-consultants, and in-house personnel on a regular basis to complete assigned tasks.
Recommends process and system improvements that result in greater efficiencies, enhanced capacities, and improved service delivery.
Supports department managers and office leadership with strategic planning, staffing/training, and other special projects.
May serve as project manager or task lead.
Performs other duties as assigned.

What You’ll Need

Bachelor’s Degree in Landscape Architecture, Planning, Environmental Planning, Urban Design, Architecture, Engineering, Urban Planning, Geography, or related field and 10 years related experience, or
Master's Degree in Landscape Architecture, Planning, Environmental Planning, Urban Design, Architecture, Engineering, Urban Planning, Geography, or related field and 9 yrs of relevant experience

Preferred Qualifications

What You’ll Bring:

Lead wetland and waterway permitting efforts for transportation and infrastructure projects.
Prepare and review permit applications (e.g. USACE Section 401/404, Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act permits, Chapter 91 license)
Conduct wetland delineations, function and values assessments, and mitigation monitoring.
Develop compensatory mitigation plans in compliance with federal and state guidance.
Familiarity with ArcGIS and GPS technologies for field data collection, spatial analysis, and mapping of wetland and waterways resources.
Coordinate with regulatory agencies and clients to ensure compliance with environmental requirements.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to integrate environmental considerations into project design.
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior staff on permitting and compliance processes.
Stay current with evolving federal, state, and local environmental regulations and guidance.
Oversees the preparation of reports and provides consultation on structure and content, including conducting quality reviews. Presents and defends reports to audiences.
Manages client meetings and oversees preparation of meeting materials without oversight from others.

What We Prefer

Master's degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Planning, or related field.
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS)
New Hampshire Certified Wetland Scientist (CWS)

jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

Arcadis is seeking an Environmental, Health, Safety and Sustainability (EHS&S) System Implementation Specialist Consultant to join our Digital EHS&S Team. This team focuses on advising and assisting our clients with deployment of enterprise EHS&S software solutions. This is a hybrid opportunity with ability to work from a home location or from an Arcadis office location with some travel. This role can be based anywhere within the continental U.S.

In this role, you will work with project teams to gather EHS&S related business requirements, translate them into written specifications and configure, test and roll out EHS&S software and tools. You will support business leaders in the successful configuration, implementation, and deployment EHS&S software tools. This could include developing specifications, system configuration, integration, system testing, training, rollout, support, maintenance, enhancement, and improvements as required to meet overall business objectives of clients.

Role accountabilities:

Work as part of teams that lead our clients through the lifecycle of EHS&S software configuration and deployment. This includes working with clients to understand, refine and document their needs and requirements in a design specification, supporting configuration teams, conducting system testing, creating strategies, and executing system integration and data migration plans and final system preparation for go-live.
Serve in a configuration and deployment role for EHS software systems and tools. Provide strategic advice and direction to clients on best practices for system design and configuration. Work directly with clients when defining and confirming their specific requirements.
Serve as a power user of collaborative technology, and champion new and innovative business solutions within established and emerging technical architectures (i.e., EHS&S software systems).

We are seeking an individual with a strong work ethic and a team player mindset with excellent communication skills to join our team. In this role, you will have the opportunity to collaborate effectively with colleagues and client facing. This position may involve travel of up to 10% to client sites and customer meetings.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Qualifications:

3+ years of experience working within and configuring Environmental, Health, Safety and Sustainability EHS&S) software solutions, emphasis on Cority/Enviance.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainability, Information Technology, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or related, or equivalent work experience preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with some of the following domains: air quality, incident management, safety, management of change, audit, sustainability, environmental, health & safety, compliance data management, enterprise risk management, or occupational health.

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. A leading national energy company is seeking an experienced Environmental Permitting Specialist to support gas pipeline and related infrastructure projects. Demonstrated experience permitting construction projects involving land disturbance and water resource impacts.

Wetlands and waters

Stormwater management

Posted Job Title

Project Data Coordinator, School of Nursing

Job Profile Title

Research Coordinator

Job Description Summary

Job Description

The Project Data Coordinator supports the ADRD Public Health Adoption Accelerator's research infrastructure by managing all data collection, entry, extraction, quality assurance, and reporting functions. Reporting to the Project Director with scientific oversight from Dr. Glanz (Strategy 1 lead), the Coordinator executes the annual environmental scan of BOLD program implementation strategies, manages the Penn REDCap database for performance measures and TA engagement logs, and compiles quantitative data for CDC Annual Performance Reports. This position is the operational hub for the program's evidence base.

Job Responsibilities

Execute and manage the annual environmental scan of BOLD program implementation strategies across ≥30 STLT agencies, Component 1 and 2 activities, peer-reviewed literature and grey literature using the dual-review structured extraction protocol developed with Drs. Glanz and Gitlin; train and supervise Penn RAs in extraction coding procedures.
Build, maintain, and update the Penn REDCap database for all program data streams, including quarterly performance measures (tools/trainings used nationally and by STLT agencies; communications products shared), TA engagement logs, adoption-tier classifications, FRAME-IS adaptation notes, and Launch pad site implementation outcome data using the Proctor et al. framework.
Compile and prepare all quantitative performance measure data for CDC quarterly reporting and Annual Performance Reports; coordinate with Emory external evaluation team on data verification procedures; generate equity-disaggregated reach tracking reports from Year 1.
Manage content entry and annual updates for the Implementation Strategy Registry; coordinate with Dr. Demiris on Registry digital infrastructure; perform quality review of Registry entries for accuracy and completeness against CPSTFCPSTF-modeled rating criteria.
Provide data management support for Launchpad sites in coordination with Gaugler lab RA; conduct data audits, generate site-level reports, and flag data quality issues to Dr. Hirschman and the Project Director.
Provide administrative and logistical support for the annual Expert Advisory Panel convening and Evidence Academy, including materials preparation, rating instrument management, and meeting documentation.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 1 to 2 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience is required. Master's degree preferred. Fields of study: public health, health sciences, information science, or related discipline.
1–3 years of experience in data management, research coordination, or program evaluation. Experience with REDCap, Qualtrics, or equivalent data entry and management systems required. Experience with grant reporting preferred.
Required Skills: REDCap, Microsoft Excel (data entry, extraction, and auditing); quantitative research methods; attention to detail; time management; written communication. Familiarity with ADRD, aging, or public health research preferred.
