Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations.

Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report.

Project Overview

The Cheniere Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL) Project is a Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) export facility located along the Sabine River estuary on the southeastern coast of Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Bulk early work for Stage 1 began at the 1,000+ acre facility in August 2012 and by December 2022, Bechtel had successfully and safely turned over the final phase of Stage 4 to Cheniere. The SPL campus now consists of six operating Trains with an LNG production capacity of approximately 27 million tons per year (MTPA), 3 Jetty superstructures that can accommodate the world’s largest vessels, and dozens of associated buildings and utilities.

Sabine Pass Liquefaction Stage 5 Expansion Project (SPL5) is the newest phase at the SPL facility. It will consist of one liquefaction process train with a production capacity of approximately 5 MTPA; one boil-off gas reliquefaction unit; tie-ins to existing storage tanks, ship-loading facilities, and flare systems; and associated utility support infrastructure. SPL5 will perform this work predominantly on a direct hire basis with support from only a few specialty and service subcontractors.

Job Summary

The Project Environmental Manager is the primary contact for environmental permits, planning, performance, and compliance. This includes technical support and guidance on regulatory requirements and field activities to mitigate risk or harm to environmentally sensitive areas, resources, and communities. The position includes communication, training, interface with regulatory agencies, and data and document management. The overarching responsibility is the development and implementation of an environmental management and compliance program for a large-scale project.

Major Responsibilities

Supervises the Project’s environmental program, in compliance with Bechtel’s ESH Management System, and contract and regulatory requirements.
Ensures that environmental requirements are integrated in planning documents, design criteria, work plans, schedules, training programs, and subcontract documents. Works with other project-level functional leads (e.g., engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning) to integrate environmental aspects in their work activities.
Communicates with internal and external stakeholders on environmental requirements and actions, inclusive of project personnel, subcontractors, and regulatory agencies. Identifies and oversees preparation and submittal of environmental permit applications, reviews and negotiates permit conditions with regulatory agencies, and tracks permit compliance and closeout.
Prepares a project-specific Environmental Management Plan and mitigation plans (e.g., Stormwater Pollution Prevention; Spill Prevention and Control, Waste Management, etc.) Prepares and submits notifications and routine reports to regulatory agencies including reportable releases, chemical inventory reports, and waste reports. Emphasizes and uses risk assessment, data analysis, and Bechtel’s ESH Management System to aid environmental performance, corrective actions, and technical guidance.
Participates in ESH emergency preparedness planning, and investigates and helps resolve environmental incidents.
Prepares and maintains required documentation and conducts inspections, monitoring, and sampling to assess site conditions and compliance with contractual commitments, laws and regulations, environmental permits, and Bechtel requirements.
Delivers training and awareness campaigns on environmental, sustainability, and regulatory compliance to the project’s workforce through various forums. Supervises and guides assigned environmental personnel, and participates in safety and health components of the ESH program.

Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) related to environmental sciences, field biology, or natural resources and 8 -10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience

Required Knowledge And Skills

Prior experience with environmental regulatory requirements, impact assessment, and mitigation practices for large-scale projects. Technical skills, work experience, and knowledge of various environmental sciences applicable to the engineering and construction industry.
Knowledge and experience with ISO 14001 Management System standards. Knowledge and experience with environmental mitigation practices (e.g., habitat protection, waste management, stormwater and erosion control, cultural resources).
Knowledge and experience in environmental permitting and regulatory approvals.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including technical writing and data management.
Able to traverse and work outdoors under various weather and site conditions. Experience managing environmental subcontractors or consultants.
This position has a work scope that includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces.
Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress).
Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e., harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.)

Under general supervision, performs technical tasks in the operation, maintenance and repair of the water and wastewater utility concrete repairs. Ability to embrace and embody the City’s core values of Respect, Integrity, Service, and Excellence (R.I.S.E.).

Ability to produce desired work outcomes, including quality, quantity, and timeliness.
Ability to plan and organize work, time, and resources, and if applicable, that of subordinates.

Ability to operate, maneuver, and/or control the actions of equipment, machinery, tools, and/or materials used in performing essential functions.
Ability to utilize a wide variety of descriptive data and information and equipment operator manuals..
Ability to perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division; ability to calculate decimals and percentages; ability to utilize principles of fractions; ability to interpret graphs.
Ability to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagrammatic form, which involves semi-routine, standardized work with some latitude for independent judgment concerning choices of action.
Ability to exercise the judgment required in situations characterized by repetitive or short cycle operations covered by set procedures or sequences.
Ability to perform coordinated movements, which involve placing and turning motions, such as operating a backhoe, dump truck and trailer, front-end loader, air compressor, gas and electrical pumps, and various hand tools.
Ability to work in a team environment while contributing as a team member and treating co-workers, subordinates, and customers with respect; Ability to build professional relationships with internal staff and customers.
Ability to offer flexibility and adaptability, especially during times of change.
Ability to find, locate and follow McKinney Public Works Standard Operating Procedures
Skill in communicating effectively both orally and in writing.

Required Qualifications

Any work related experience resulting in acceptable proficiency levels in the below Minimum Qualifications may be an acceptable substitute.

Highschool diploma or GED equivalent supplemented by previous experience and/or training involving concrete construction, maintenance and repair type work, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Must possess a valid Class A commercial driver's license or the ability to obtain within twelve (12) months of employment.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Some experience with hand tools and power tools
Some experience with outside elements and manual labor.

Must pass a drug screen and background check.

During storms or natural disasters, staff will be divided into two 12-hour shifts. During storms or natural disasters, staff may be called in while on vacation.

DEMANDS

Tasks involve the ability to exert heavy physical effort in heavy work, with greater emphasis on climbing and balancing, but typically also involving some combination of stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, and the lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling of moderately heavy objects and materials (20-50 pounds); may occasionally involve heavier objects and materials (up to 150 pounds). Some tasks require visual and odor perception and discrimination.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

There is limited exposure to environmental conditions. Tasks may require exposure to strong odors and/or smoke, traffic hazards, extreme heat/cold or extreme weather conditions.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Environmental Technician to support environmental remediation for an industrial client. You will work alongside experienced technicians and field crews to execute field tasks safely and efficiently, maintain high-quality documentation, and support operations, maintenance, and sampling activities. The site is located in Niagara Falls, NY.

This role emphasizes hands-on fieldwork and adherence to safety and quality protocols, with growth opportunities into advanced field responsibilities. The successful candidate will ideally have some experience in general operations, environmental remediation/sampling, and hands-on mechanical experience.

Field Operations & Site Support

Oversee pump-and-treat system operations, including monitoring, troubleshooting, maintenance, and performance optimization.
Sampling groundwater Influent and Effluent from groundwater treatment systems primarily for volatile organic compounds. Preparing chains-of-custody and sample cooler loading in preparation for transport to contracted analytical laboratories.
Gathering and maintaining specified records of scientific data for the technical lead/supervisor, including environmental sampling, operations and maintenance, and inspections at client sites
Assisting with calculations, setting up, and operating equipment (sampling devices and pumps), inspecting equipment and installations for compliance with specifications and maintaining proper project documentation.
Driving AECOM-leased site vehicles.
Mechanical aptitude to make basic repairs to treatment equipment.
Overseeing and working in collaboration with client mechanical, electrical, and industrial contractors.

Health & Safety Participation

Follow AECOM safety policies and Site-Specific Health and Safety Plans (SSHPs); participate in JHAs/tailgates and stop work if unsafe conditions arise.
Use required PPE correctly, report incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions immediately.
Maintain compliance with OSHA and applicable state requirements during all phases of work.

Documentation & QA/QC

Maintain complete and accurate field logs, daily reports, equipment logs, photo documentation, and chain-of-custody records.
Perform basic data entry and QA/QC checks for measurements and sampling results.

Coordination & Communication

Coordinate day-to-day needs with the site supervisor, project manager, subcontractors, and client representatives as directed.
Communicate field status, issues, and material/equipment needs promptly and professionally.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Must possess a High School Diploma (or GED).
U.S. citizenship (due to project requirements)
In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background, medical and drug screening requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
Ability to travel to various client sites locations using a AECOM provided Vehicle to conduct fieldwork, including but not limited to environmental sampling, operations and maintenance and inspections.
Must possess a valid driver’s license and clean driving record.
Position requires frequent (more than 50% of workday) standing/walking; often (25-50% of workday) performing power gripping/squeezing (hand tools, levers, etc.), operation of vehicles, performing repetitive or fine hand movements, and lifting of less than 25 pounds; occasionally (10-25% of workday) performing work with arms above shoulder level, repetitive bending & stooping, working at heights, climbing stairs, using portable ladders, work in an environment of heavy, moving, dangerous equipment, work in confined spaces, keyboard/mouse operations, work alone in isolated/remote areas, and lifting of 25-50 pounds; rarely (less than 10% of workday) wearing fall protection, and lifting of 50-75 pounds.
Position will include wearing associated personal protective equipment, including but not limited to gloves, safety glasses/goggles, face shield, safety shoes/boots, hard hat, hearing, and respiratory protection.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER (current) or ability to obtain within 60 days of hire (training provided).

Preferred Qualifications

1+ years of environmental remediation, construction, utilities, or industrial fieldwork experience.
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER with recent refresher; OSHA 10 or 30 Construction and CPR/First Aid certifications.
Experience with basic sampling, meter use (e.g., PID, multi-parameter), and remediation system O&M tasks.
Some experience or aptitude with flow meters, pH meters, and level probes would be beneficial but not required.
Proficiency with field documentation (daily reports, chain-of-custody, photo logs); basic Excel/Word skills.
Previous knowledge or experience with process control systems
Familiarity or previous experience with environmental regulatory compliance.
Mechanical aptitude and hands-on skills to operate groundwater treatment equipment.
Associate degree or college course education in engineering, chemistry, or other sciences.

Additional Information

Qualified applicants who are offered a position must pass a pre-employment substance abuse test.
In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background, medical and drug screening requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
This position does not include sponsorship for United States work authorization.
This position does not include relocation benefits.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Coordinator
jobs.description:
Description

We are currently seeking an Environmental Compliance Coordinator
to manage the environmental portion of a Distribution Transformer Inspection Program. The program inspects up to 40,000 underground transformers per year. This role combines office-based program management with field support and coordination of environmental compliance activities.

The ideal candidate is organized, self-motivated, and an excellent communicator who can manage databases, coordinate with contractors and internal stakeholders, and support timely environmental remediation and regulatory reporting.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Industry competitive pay.
Company vehicle with a fuel card for work purposes.
Medical/Dental/Vision/VOYA/Vacation Accrual/Paid Holidays/EAP, 401K, life insurance, short and long-term disability, Paid Maternity Leave.
Paid Sick Time.
Weekly Pay Cycle.
Participation in Referral Bonus Program.
Ongoing training and assistance with obtaining industry certifications.
A standard 5-day, 40-hour work week, with opportunities for overtime when needed and approved.
A hybrid schedule consisting of approximately 60% office work and 40% field work.
Three days per week working from an office is required; remote work from home two days per week is optional.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Program & Data Management

Manage the environmental portion of the Distribution Transformer Inspection Program.
Manage and maintain spreadsheets and databases used to track transformer replacement and repair status when oil contamination or leaks are present.
Coordinate with the Asset Management Team to support successful program rollouts across all 32 districts.
Track spend rates and manage budgets.

Spill Response & Environmental Compliance

Communicate with inspection contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure timely remediation of oil spills.
Report oil spills internally and, when required, externally to VADEQ.
Approve or deny environmental containment while inspectors are in the field.
Dispatch spill response vendors to remediate oil contamination.
Document spill response measures and perform QA/QC of cleanup efforts when necessary.
Make proper PCB/non-PCB determinations and manage PCBs in accordance with TSCA regulations when discovered.

Training & Team Support

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Advisor
jobs.description:
Gawaya Baya Wind Farm | FIFO from Queensland | 2/1 Roster | Symal Infrastructure

Lead environmental performance on a landmark renewable energy project
.

Symal Infrastructure is delivering the Gawaya Baya Wind Farm, a major renewable energy project in North Queensland, and we’re seeking an experienced Senior Environmental Advisor to join our project HSEQ team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced environmental professional to take a senior role on a $347M major infrastructure project, working alongside an experienced project leadership team and playing a key role in driving environmental compliance, sustainability and performance across the project.

The project comprises approximately 400MW of renewable energy generation, 68 wind turbine generators, 78km of access roads, significant bulk earthworks, concrete works, drainage infrastructure and major bridge construction, with a peak workforce of approximately 300 personnel.

The Opportunity

As Senior Environmental Advisor, you’ll be a key environmental leader on the project, providing specialist advice and practical support to the Project Manager, Environment & Sustainability Manager, construction teams, subcontractors and client representatives.

You’ll have a strong field presence and be responsible for ensuring environmental requirements are embedded into day-to-day construction activities, while proactively identifying risks, driving compliance and supporting the project to achieve its environmental and sustainability objectives.

You’ll be responsible for:

Leading the implementation and ongoing review of the Project Environmental Management Plan, Sustainability Management Plans and associated environmental controls.
Providing senior technical advice to project leadership, construction teams and subcontractors on environmental risks, compliance and best practice.
Driving environmental compliance across construction activities and ensuring legislative, contractual and project requirements are understood and achieved.
Leading environmental inspections, audits, monitoring programs and risk assessments.
Identifying environmental risks and implementing practical mitigation and control measures.
Managing environmental approvals, permits, licences and associated conditions.
Reviewing and providing input into environmental documentation, including EMPs, SEPs, SMPs, SWMS, procedures and construction methodologies.
Maintaining a strong field presence and working directly with supervisors, engineers and subcontractors to ensure environmental controls are effective.
Leading the identification, investigation and close-out of environmental non-conformances and corrective actions.
Supporting and, where required, leading environmental incident investigations and ensuring appropriate preventative actions are implemented.
Supporting regulatory engagement and environmental reporting requirements.
Preparing environmental and sustainability reporting for project leadership, senior management and clients.
Supporting project audits and maintaining compliance with relevant environmental management standards, including ISO 14001.
Working closely with the Client HSEQ team and participating in environmental audits, risk workshops, project meetings and incident investigations.
Delivering environmental training, inductions and toolbox sessions to employees and subcontractors.
Coaching and mentoring junior environmental team members and supporting their professional development.
Identifying opportunities to improve environmental performance through innovation, technology and industry-leading practices.
Contributing to a strong environmental culture across the project and ensuring environmental performance remains a priority throughout delivery.

About You

We’re looking for a hands-on and commercially aware environmental professional who can operate confidently within a major construction project environment.

You’ll ideally have:

A tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Earth Sciences, Science, Engineering or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience in a Senior Environmental Advisor or Environmental Advisor role within civil construction, infrastructure, resources, renewable energy or major projects.
Strong knowledge of Australian environmental legislation, approvals, compliance requirements and construction environmental management.
Proven experience implementing Environmental Management Plans and environmental controls across major construction projects.
Strong experience conducting environmental inspections, audits, monitoring and risk assessments.
Experience managing environmental incidents, investigations, corrective actions and regulatory requirements.
The ability to provide confident and practical environmental advice to project managers, engineers, supervisors and subcontractors.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build effective relationships with clients, regulators and project teams.
Excellent communication, reporting and documentation skills.
A proactive approach with the confidence to challenge poor environmental practices and drive positive outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and support less experienced environmental professionals.
White Card.
Current driver's licence.
Cert II Erosion and Sediment Control / Green Card, or equivalent experience, highly regarded.
ISCA Sustainability Accreditation desirable.

Why Join Symal?

At Symal, We Build Better Together.

We’re a team that rolls up our sleeves, gets involved and takes pride in delivering great outcomes. We value collaboration, different perspectives and people who are prepared to challenge the way things are done.

This is an opportunity to join a growing infrastructure business and work on a high-profile renewable energy project that will make a lasting contribution to Queensland's energy future.

You’ll work alongside experienced construction, project and HSEQ leaders while having the autonomy and support to make a genuine impact on environmental performance.

Career Development

At Symal, we invest in our people and support ongoing professional development across the HSEQ function.

You’ll have access to opportunities including:

Environmental management and compliance training
Environmental Management System auditing
ICAM training
ISCA sustainability development
Mentoring and leadership development
Progression into Environmental & Sustainability Management roles

The Gawaya Baya Project

Gawaya Baya Wind Farm is a major renewable energy development in North Queensland, approximately 2.5 hours from Townsville.

The project includes:

$347M D&C project
400MW renewable energy generation
68 wind turbine generators
78km of project roads
Approximately 1.8 million m³ of earthworks
Approximately 55,000 m³ of concrete
Major drainage and culvert work
60m Michael Creek bridge
Peak workforce of approximately 300 personnel

The Roster

2 weeks on / 1 week off

FIFO/DIDO opportunities are available from Queensland, with accommodation, flights/travel and site amenities provided in line with project arrangements.

Take the Next Step

If you’re an experienced environmental professional looking for the opportunity to take a senior role on a major renewable energy project, we’d love to hear from you.

Join Symal Infrastructure and help build the future of renewable energy in Queensland.

Apply now.

jobs.description:
Summary

The primary purpose of this position is to serve as a Regional Environmental Protection Specialist. The incumbent is responsible for assuring the region's compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), FTA’s environmental procedures (23 CFR part 771), and related Federal laws during its execution of the Federal transit program.

Duties

Help

As an Environmental Protection Specialist, you will:

Evaluate environmental documents—including Categorical Exclusions (CEs), Environmental Assessments (EAs), Environmental Impact Statements (EISs), Findings of No Significant Impact (FONSIs), and Records of Decision (RODs)—for legal sufficiency and compliance with 23 CFR 771.
Serve as the primary FTA Region 1 representative in interagency consultations with federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory bodies (e.g., EPA, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, State Historic Preservation Officers, and Tribal Historic Preservation Officers).
Serve as a subject matter expert on Executive Orders and directives related to NEPA, National Historic Preservation Act, Section 4(f) of the US DOT Act, FTA NEPA regulations and standard operating procedures, and the FTA project development process.
Conduct pre-award environmental reviews and field assessments to identify potential environmental hazards, noise/vibration issues, air quality impacts, or cultural resource conflicts early in project design.
Facilitate meetings with FTA recipients, manage a diverse workload with competing deadlines, identify and implement best management practices.
Lead interdisciplinary teams, coordinate with resource agencies, and mediate competing stakeholder interests.
Give presentations in professional settings, convey technical topics to non-technical audiences, and articulate complex policy positions to agency decision-makers.

The Ideal Candidate for this position
is a mid-career employee with experience implementing the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and/or other environmental laws, regulations, or policy for transit projects.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

You must be a U.S. citizen & meet specialized experience to qualify
Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date
Required documents must be submitted by the closing date.
Direct Hire Authority/SME will be used to fill this position

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT:

As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you may be required to serve a 1-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:

your performance and conduct;
the needs and interests of the agency;
whether your continued employment would advance the organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Upon completion of your probationary period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service.
GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only.
BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION: A background security investigation is required for all selected individuals. Appointment will be subject to the applicant’s successful completion of the security investigation and favorable adjudication. Failure to meet these requirements will be grounds for termination.
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).

Qualifications

To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience requirements for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.

To qualify for the Grade 12
, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-11 it must include:

Experience working with project sponsors/recipients, local and state agencies, and other federal agencies in compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and other environmental laws and regulations, including Section 4(f), as they relate to transit/transportation projects, AND
Experience applying environmental statutes, laws, regulations, and guidelines related to analyzing environmental impacts, protecting the environment, and preparing environmental documents for transit/transportation projects, AND
Experience in reviewing and analyzing environmental impacts that occur with transit/transportation projects in compliance with NEPA, Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act and Section4(f), and in mitigating those impacts, AND
Experience collaborating and communicating with internal and external subject matter specialists (such as planners and engineers) to ensure project compliance with NEPA; preparing written correspondence, reports, and memos for technical assistance or policy guidance; and presenting technical data to diverse stakeholders.

To qualify for the Grade 13
, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-12, it must include:

Experience performing project development activities and working with project sponsors/recipients, local and state agencies, and other federal agencies in compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and other environmental laws and regulations, including Section 4(f), as they relate to transit/transportation projects, AND
Experience applying environmental statutes, laws, regulations, guidelines, and the federal environmental review processes in compliance with NEPA, including the Clean Air Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act, Section 4(f) of the DOT Act, and other environmental laws, regulations, and policies, as they relate to federal environmental requirements in preparing environmental documents for transit/transportation projects, AND
Experience in managing, preparing, reviewing, and providing technical assistance for transit/ transportation projects that require any level of NEPA review (i.e., categorical exclusion, environmental assessment and/or an environmental impact statement) from beginning to conclusion and including mitigation and all consultation, such as with the State Historic Preservation Officer, USFWS, USACE, and Federally recognized tribes, AND

jobs.title: PhD: Moss traits and fire ignition in high-latitude peatland & tundra ecosystems
jobs.description:
Your job

Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems.

Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project
examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations
Analysing remote sensing data and global vegetation databases
Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting it at national and international conferences
Co-supervising BSc and MSc students

You will work here

The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group, (https://www.wur.nl/en/research-results/chair-groups/environmental-sciences/plant-ecology-and-nature-conservation-group.htm) specifically within the Vegetation-Climate Feedbacks team. You will be co-supervised by Dr. Thomas Janssen, Dr. José van Paassen and Dr. Juul Limpens.

Your qualities

You are a candidate with strong experimental skills, and conduct research responsibly. You work independently to find solutions for research challenges, while staying in communication with the team. You enjoy working with multiple project partners to efficiently arrange field and lab work.

You Also Possess

A successfully completed MSc degree in ecology, environmental sciences, climate studies or a related field
Affinity and experience with experimental design of lab- and/or field experiments
Excellent organizational and communicational skills
Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken
Experience with fire-related research is a plus

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

jobs.title: Director of Environmental
jobs.description:
Description

Director of Environmental

Position Title: Director of Environmental

Function / Department: Environment, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS&S)

Reports To: President

Direct Reports: Site Environmental Managers and specialists at Gramercy and St. Ann; environmental engineers, compliance analysts, monitoring technicians

Sites of Responsibility: Gramercy Alumina Refinery (Gramercy, Louisiana, USA) and St. Ann Bauxite Operations (Discovery Bay / St. Ann Parish, Jamaica)

Location / Base: Gramercy, Louisiana (primary), with recurring on-site presence in St. Ann, Jamaica

Travel: Approximately 20–35%, including regular international travel to Jamaica

Jurisdictions United States (Federal / State of Louisiana) and Jamaica, with the ability to extend to other jurisdictions for potential M&A or other reasons

Position Summary

The Director of Environmental provides strategic and operational leadership for all environmental compliance, stewardship, and sustainability activities across Atalco's integrated bauxite-to-alumina value chain. The role holds single-point accountability for environmental performance at two geographically and jurisdictionally distinct operations: the Gramercy alumina refinery in Louisiana, United States, and the St. Ann bauxite mining operation in Jamaica.

Reporting to senior leadership, the Director sets environmental policy and standards, ensures full compliance with all applicable United States federal and Louisiana state regulations as well as Jamaican national environmental and mining law, and drives a proactive culture of environmental risk management, continuous improvement, and responsible resource stewardship. The role is central to protecting Atalco's license to operate, managing all permitting, exploration, alumina processing, bauxite residue and mined-land liabilities, safeguarding air, water, and land resources, and maintaining constructive relationships with regulators, communities, and other stakeholders in both countries.

Scope of Operations

Gramercy Alumina Refinery — Gramercy, Louisiana, USA

A Bayer-process alumina refinery on the Mississippi River that converts imported bauxite into smelter- and chemical-grade aluminas. Key environmental features and risk areas include Title V air emissions sources (calcination, digestion, power/steam generation), process and stormwater discharges to the Mississippi River under a Louisiana water discharge permit, bauxite residue (red mud) storage and management areas, caustic and chemical handling, spill prevention, and hazardous and industrial waste management within a densely regulated US industrial corridor. This scope is expanding to cover gallium extraction from the Gramercy Bayer process, as well as potentially the beneficiation of critical minerals and other elements from the bauxite residue.

St. Ann Bauxite Operation — St. Ann Parish, Jamaica

An open-pit bauxite mining, drying, and export operation set in Jamaica's karst limestone terrain. Key environmental features and risk areas include permitting, exploration, sensitive specie preservation and relocation, land clearing and progressive mine development, mined-land reclamation and restoration, dust and air quality management from mining, trucking, railing, and drying, material handling/conveying, ship loading, protection of groundwater and surface water resources, biodiversity and reforestation obligations, haul-road and shipping-terminal impacts, and management of overburden and red-earth materials—all governed by Jamaican environmental permits, licenses, and mining lease conditions.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Strategy & Leadership

Define and own the environmental strategy, policy, standards, permits, and related management systems that apply consistently across both operations while respecting each jurisdiction's legal requirements.
Establish a single, harmonized environmental management framework (aligned to ISO 14001 principles) that sets a common standard of performance while accommodating US and Jamaican regulatory differences.
Serve as the company's principal environmental authority, advising the executive team and Board on environmental risk, liabilities, obligations, capital requirements, and emerging regulatory developments.
Embed environmental accountability into operational decision-making, capital planning, and site leadership performance objectives.

Regulatory Compliance — Gramercy (United States)

Ensure full and continuous compliance with all applicable US federal and Louisiana state environmental requirements, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA).
Own the site's Title V air operating permit, Louisiana water discharge (LPDES) permit, and all related permits, ensuring conditions, monitoring, and reporting obligations are met.
Maintain compliant relationships and correspondence with the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) and applicable local agencies.
Oversee Toxic Release Inventory (TRI / Form R), Tier II, greenhouse gas, and other mandated federal and state reporting.
Direct Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC), stormwater, and hazardous/industrial waste programs.
Optimize management of environmental liabilities and closure related plans.

Regulatory Compliance — St. Ann (Jamaica)

Ensure full compliance with Jamaican environmental and mining legislation, including the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA) Act, environmental permits and licenses, and conditions of the Mining Act and applicable Special Mining Leases.
Maintain effective working relationships with the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA), the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA), the Jamaica Bauxite Institute (JBI), Mines and Geology Division / Commissioner of Mines, and applicable local agencies.
Manage environmental permit and license applications, renewals, Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), environmental permit conditions, and related matters for mine exploration, development and expansion.
Ensure compliance with mined-land reclamation, restoration, and post-mining land-use obligations under Jamaican law and lease commitments.

Bauxite Residue, Waste & Materials Management

Direct the safe management, processing, monitoring, and long-term stewardship of bauxite residue (red mud) storage areas at Gramercy, including structural integrity, seepage control, water balance, and closure planning.
Oversee management of overburden, red-earth, tailings, and process waste materials at St. Ann in line with permit conditions and reclamation plans.
Ensure hazardous, industrial, and general waste is characterized, stored, transported, and disposed of in compliance with applicable regulations at both sites.

Air, Water, Land & Biodiversity

Oversee air emissions monitoring, control, and dust management across refining from bauxite discharging through to final product loading (Gramercy) and mining/drying/shipping (St. Ann) activities.
Manage water resources, process water, wastewater, and stormwater programs, including discharge monitoring, groundwater and surface-water protection, and water quality reporting.
Lead progressive mined-land reclamation, revegetation, reforestation, and biodiversity protection programs at St. Ann, and land stewardship and site remediation at Gramercy.

Permitting, Monitoring & Reporting

Own the full lifecycle of environmental permits, licenses, and authorizations at both operations—applications, renewals, modifications, and condition tracking.
Ensure timely, accurate, and defensible environmental monitoring, recordkeeping, and regulatory reporting in both jurisdictions.
Maintain an audit-ready compliance calendar and documentation system spanning both sites.

Incident Management & Emergency Response

Establish and maintain environmental incident prevention, spill response, and emergency preparedness programs at both operations.
Lead environmental incident investigations, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and regulatory notification and follow-up.
Ensure emergency response plans meet US and Jamaican requirements and are regularly tested and updated.

Auditing, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

Implement a program of internal and third-party environmental audits, inspections, and self-assessments across both sites.
Track environmental performance against targets, identify improvement opportunities, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Benchmark performance and adopt industry-leading practices in alumina refining and bauxite mining environmental management.

Stakeholder, Community & Sustainability Engagement

Represent Atalco with regulators, government agencies, industry bodies, and communities in both Louisiana and Jamaica.
Support community relations, land-use, and social-license initiatives associated with mining and refining operations.
Advance Atalco's sustainability, ESG, and greenhouse-gas / decarbonization reporting and commitments.

Team Leadership & Resources

Lead, develop, and mentor site environmental teams at Gramercy and St. Ann, building bench strength and consistent standards across borders.
Develop and manage the environmental function's operating and capital budgets, including compliance, monitoring, remediation, and reclamation expenditures.
Manage environmental consultants, laboratories, and specialist contractors in both jurisdictions.
Identify and develop succession candidates for environmental managers at both locations and other key environmental roles.

Dual-Jurisdiction Regulatory Scope

The role requires fluency in two distinct regulatory systems. The table below summarises the principal frameworks and authorities the Director is accountable for in each jurisdiction.

Area

Gramercy — United States (Federal / Louisiana)

Primary Agencies :

U.S. EPA

Louisiana Dept. of Environmental Quality (LDEQ)

Key Legislation:

Clean Air Act

Clean Water Act

RCRA (waste)

EPCRA / TRI; CERCLA

Air:

Title V operating permit; emissions monitoring for calcination, digestion & power generation

Water:

LPDES discharge permit to Mississippi River; stormwater; SPCC

Waste / Residue :

Bauxite residue (red mud) storage areas; hazardous & industrial waste management

Land :

Site land stewardship, remediation & residue-area closure planning

St. Ann — Jamaica

Primary Agencies:

National Environment & Planning Agency (NEPA)

Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA)

Jamaica Bauxite Institute (JBI); Mines & Geology Division

Key Legislation:

NRCA Act

Mining Act; Special Mining Leases

Environmental permits & licences

Applicable EIA regulations

Air:

Air / dust permit conditions for mining, haulage & bauxite drying

Water:

Effluent / discharge licences; groundwater & surface-water protection in karst terrain

Waste / Residue :

Overburden, red-earth & tailings management; process waste

Land :

Progressive mined-land reclamation, revegetation & post-mining land use

Required

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, Geology, or a closely related discipline.
Minimum 12–15 years of progressive environmental experience in heavy industry, with substantial exposure to mining, metals, refining, chemicals, or a comparably regulated sector.
Demonstrated leadership of environmental compliance across multiple sites, including managing professional environmental teams.
Proven, working knowledge of U.S. federal and state environmental regulation (Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA and related programs).
Direct experience with major environmental permits (e.g., Title V air, NPDES/LPDES water) including permit strategy, negotiation, and compliance.
Experience managing large-scale environmental liabilities such as residue/tailings storage, land reclamation, or remediation.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Position:

The candidate will work inside Environmental and Crew Systems within Airbus Defence and Space.

Join our dynamic team as an Environmental and Crew Support Systems Control Engineer, where you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our projects. We are seeking a talented individual to contribute to our innovative programs, focusing on ECS and Control & Monitoring systems across various aircraft platforms. In this position, you will have the opportunity to work on diverse programs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and make a significant impact on our aviation solutions. If you are passionate about engineering and eager to work in a challenging and rewarding environment, we invite you to apply and grow with us.

Description of the Job:

As an Environmental and Crew Support Systems Control Engineer, you will be an integral part of our team responsible for crew support and air systems in Airbus Defence and Space. Your work will encompass a wide range of systems, including pneumatics, air conditioning, ice protection, oxygen, and crew escape systems for all military platforms. Our team is recognized as a reference both internally and externally in various international program consortiums (e.g., EF, A400M).

Your role will cover the entire development life-cycle of control systems within our scope, from requirements analysis and control system architecture definition to development, integration, and certification/qualification. Given the variety of versions in different development and in-service stages, your job will be dynamic and diverse.

Key responsibilities will include:

Designing, developing, and testing control systems for environmental and crew support systems.
Collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless integration of systems.
Supporting aircraft deliveries and resolving in-service issues, providing technical expertise to ensure aircraft readiness.
Contributing to research and innovation initiatives to adapt air systems to new aircraft concepts.
Managing technical interfaces, stakeholders, and suppliers.

We are looking for a passionate engineer who is eager to make a significant impact in their career. The ideal candidate should be flexible, adaptable, and capable of handling both highly technical tasks and managing technical interfaces and stakeholders.

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the evolution of aviation systems, working on diverse programs and challenging projects. If you are ready to take on a dynamic and rewarding role, we invite you to join our team.

Tasks And Accountabilities

Define, develop, and integrate environmental control and crew systems architecture, including control and monitoring systems (hardware and software, interfaces, and wiring diagrams), ensuring safe integration and performance.
Manage the development of ECS solutions and maintain system configuration control throughout the product's life cycle, ensuring compliance with certification and qualification regulations.
Lead integration activities of electronic control units related to ECS and manage software configuration during the program's life.
Coordinate with suppliers to meet customer and airworthiness requirements, including technical coordination and official communication.
Validate, verify, and certify technical solutions from development to qualification phases, ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory requirements.
Stay updated with technological advancements and provide tools and methods for global integration of ECS components, ensuring system performance meets customer specifications.
Plan and oversee laboratory testing activities for ECS from development to in-service, and provide technical support for flight test programs and aircraft delivery in the Final Assembly Line (FAL).
Provide technical support for in-service events, including resolving technical issues and analyzing incidents/accidents, to maintain system airworthiness.

Required Skills

Degree in Aeronautical, Industrial, Telecommunications or Computer Engineer.
Spanish and English: Negotiation level.
Flexibility to adapt to different tasks and different environments, demonstrating versatility in various situations.
Ability to work effectively in a team environment, collaborating with other engineers, technicians, and stakeholders to achieve common goals.
Experienced in control systems with strong skills in both hardware and software integration, and knowledge of aerospace communication protocols e.g., ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, CAN, AFDX)
Proven experience in integrating electronic control units and managing software configurations, ensuring seamless system performance.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to resolve technical issues, analyze incidents, and create innovative control architectures. Ability to interpret and analyze data to ensure system performance meets customer specifications and regulatory standards.
Experience in defining, developing, and integrating complex systems, including both hardware and software components, to deliver comprehensive solutions.
Experience with modeling and simulation tools (e.g., CAMEO, SCADE, MATLAB/Simulink) to support system design and validation.
Familiarity with aerospace safety and certification standards (e.g., DO-178C, DO-254, CS25, CS23), ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.
Commitment to continuously develop skills and knowledge through training and professional development opportunities, staying updated with the latest industry advancements.

WHICH BENEFITS WILL YOU HAVE AS AIRBUS EMPLOYEE?

At Airbus we are focused on our employees and their welfare. Take a look at some of our social benefits:

Vacation days and additional days-off along the year (+35 days off in total)
Attractive salary and compensation package
Hybrid model of working when possible, promoting the work-life balance
Collective transport service in some sites
Benefits such as health insurance, employee stock options, retirement plan...
On-site facilities (among others): free canteen, kindergarten, medical office
Possibility to collaborate in different social and corporate social responsibility initiatives
Excellent upskilling opportunities and great development prospects in a multicultural environment
Special rates in products & benefits

WANT TO KNOW MORE ABOUT US?

Airbus is a leader in designing, manufacturing and delivering aerospace products, services and solutions to customers on a worldwide scale, pioneering sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world.

With around 130,000 employees and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe and a worldwide leader, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry, connecting people and places via air and space.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth.

jobs.description:
About Us

Shared Regulatory Services is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Environmental Health Officer to join our Housing Enforcement and Pollution Control Team.

As part of a multidisciplinary service covering Bridgend County Borough and the Vale of Glamorgan, the team is responsible for private sector housing, pollution control and public health functions. This is an exciting opportunity to make a real difference to local communities by helping to protect public health, improve housing conditions and ensure compliance with environmental health legislation.

About The Role

Pay Details:
Pay Grade 9

Hours of Work / Working Pattern:
37 hours/ 5 days a week/ Flexi

Main Place of Work:
Bridgend and Vale of Glamorgan

Description:

We are seeking an enthusiastic, proactive and professional Environmental Health Officer to undertake investigations and deliver effective enforcement in accordance with relevant environmental health legislation.
The successful candidate will be responsible for a varied caseload, undertaking a wide range of enforcement activities across housing and environmental protection functions.
Key responsibilities will include investigating statutory nuisance complaints, improving housing conditions within the private rented sector, and securing compliance with relevant legislation through informal and formal enforcement action where appropriate.
The postholder will work with owners, developers and partners to bring vacant and long-term empty properties back into use, using enforcement powers to support regeneration, housing supply and communities.
The postholder will also provide specialist environmental health advice and consultation responses in relation to Planning and Licensing applications, supporting the protection of public health and the wider environment.
Working closely with colleagues, partner agencies, landlords, businesses and residents, you will play an important role in improving housing standards and protecting the health and wellbeing of local communities.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and professional individual who is committed to delivering high-quality environmental health services and improving outcomes for local communities.

You will need to have:

A relevant Environmental Health qualification, degree or equivalent professional qualification.
The ability to work independently, manage a varied workload and prioritise competing demands effectively.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, partner organisations, businesses, landlords and residents.
Confidence in interpreting and enforcing a range of Environmental Health legislation in a fair, proportionate and consistent manner.
Excellent investigative, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound professional judgements.
The ability to prepare clear and accurate reports, records and enforcement documentation.

You will be able to demonstrate:

A proactive and customer-focused approach to service delivery.
The ability to build effective working relationships and work as part of a multidisciplinary team.
A commitment to protecting public health, improving housing standards and delivering positive outcomes for communities.

jobs.title: Environmental GIS and Data Manager
jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons is looking for an amazingly talented Environmental GIS and Data Specialist to join our team. In this role, you will combine Geographic Information Systems, environmental data management, workflow automation, and technical communication to support environmental site assessment, remediation, risk management, monitoring, sampling, and federal infrastructure projects.

You will work closely with environmental scientists, engineers, geoscientists, project managers, field personnel, construction professionals, and other GIS and data specialists. You will organize and validate environmental information, develop and maintain project databases, prepare high-quality maps and figures, automate repetitive processes, and convert field and laboratory data into clear, defensible client deliverables.

What You’ll Be Doing

Develop, administer, and maintain project geodatabases and environmental databases in accordance with Parsons and client standards.
Compile, import, organize, and standardize information from field programs, analytical laboratories, GPS and survey equipment, historical records, drawings, client systems, and government or open-source datasets.
Perform quality assurance and quality control of spatial and tabular data, including checks for completeness, accuracy, coordinate systems, location identifiers, units, laboratory qualifiers, and consistency between data sources.
Prepare professional maps, figures, and geospatial deliverables for environmental site assessments, investigations, remediation programs, monitoring projects, construction support, and site approval packages.
Produce site-location plans, property and facility plans, borehole and monitoring-well figures, sampling-location plans, analytical-results maps, groundwater-elevation and contour figures, remediation-progress plans, and other project-specific graphics.
Develop and maintain standardized templates, legends, symbology, naming conventions, metadata, and map-production procedures.
Build and maintain digital field forms and mobile data-collection workflows using ArcGIS applications or comparable platforms.
Use ArcGIS Pro, Python/ArcPy, SQL, and related tools to automate data validation, geoprocessing, map production, reporting, and other repetitive tasks.
Run, troubleshoot, document, and improve existing scripts and automated workflows.
Query environmental databases and prepare tables, charts, data summaries, dashboards, and exports for project teams and clients.
Support pre-visit digital reconnaissance by compiling topographic, environmental, infrastructure, utility, and other site information before field assessments.
Support evaluation of proposed and alternative project sites using GIS data, system requirements, site constraints, and available environmental and geotechnical information.
Prepare maps and data products identifying site-specific environmental constraints, utility conditions, access limitations, cost drivers, schedule risks, and other construction feasibility considerations.
Request, manage, organize, and maintain GIS data for potential project sites and ensure that collected information remains accessible to project and government teams.
Support environmental screenings, permitting evaluations, NEPA-related documentation, environmental compliance activities, and construction environmental support.
Assist with tracking environmental requirements, permit conditions, compliance milestones, regulatory reporting requirements, and project progress.
Support site visits, GPS and mobile-data collection, sampling-location verification, and implementation of digital field workflows.
Coordinate with project managers and technical staff to ensure GIS, data, reporting, and site assessment tasks are completed accurately, on schedule, and within project budgets.
Support technical-report preparation, including figures, tables, appendices, data-management descriptions, methods and results summaries, site assessment reports, and project recommendations.
Prepare detailed maps and supporting data for site assessment reports, including system-specific requirements and site constraints.
Coordinate with federal, state, and local agencies, installation personnel, utility providers, contractors, and other stakeholders when required.
Maintain clear documentation of databases, scripts, data sources, assumptions, and processing procedures so work can be reviewed, reproduced, and transferred between project teams.
Support multiple concurrent projects and task orders, including assignments at geographically dispersed locations.
Protect confidential, procurement-sensitive, and client information and follow applicable health, safety, quality, cybersecurity, data-security, and records-management requirements.

What Required Skills You’ll Bring

Active Secret security clearance required
Bachelor’s degree in GIS, geomatics, geography, environmental science, environmental engineering technology, earth sciences, computer or data science, information systems, or a closely related discipline.
10+ years of relevant experience, including GIS, database, environmental-data, or technical-reporting experience.
Practical proficiency with ArcGIS Pro, including geodatabases, data editing, geoprocessing, cartography, coordinate systems and projections, spatial analysis, and publication-quality map production.
Understanding of relational database structures and the ability to query, organize, validate, and manage tabular data using SQL, Microsoft Access, or a comparable platform.
Working knowledge of Python, preferably including ArcPy, with the ability to run, review, troubleshoot, and modify GIS or data-management scripts.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word, including preparation and formatting of tables, figures, and technical documentation.
Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to quality assurance, file management, data security, and documentation.
Ability to investigate and resolve data or software problems independently while knowing when to seek guidance.
Ability to manage multiple assignments, changing priorities, and concurrent projects in a project-driven consulting environment.
Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to prepare concise technical documentation.
Ability to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical personnel in a multidisciplinary team.
Valid Class 5 driver’s license and ability to travel occasionally for project requirements, if required.

What Desired Skills You’ll Bring

Master’s degree in a relevant discipline and/or professional designation.
Experience with environmental consulting, contaminated sites, petroleum hydrocarbon projects, site assessment, remediation, risk assessment, environmental monitoring, or construction support.
Familiarity with environmental data related to soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil vapor, air monitoring, boreholes, monitoring wells, and laboratory analyses.
Experience with laboratory electronic data deliverables, detection limits, qualifiers, environmental standards, and chemistry-data validation.
Experience with ArcGIS Online or Enterprise, Field Maps, Survey123, Dashboards, Experience Builder, StoryMaps, or similar tools.
Experience with Microsoft Access, SQL Server, EQuIS, laboratory information management systems, or environmental database platforms.
Experience preparing maps, figures, and reports for environmental site assessments, remediation, monitoring, construction, or infrastructure projects.
Familiarity with AutoCAD and data exchange between GIS and CAD systems.
Experience with GPS, Trimble, or comparable field-survey and data-collection equipment.
Familiarity with Power BI, Power Automate, SharePoint, or other reporting and workflow tools.
Experience preparing site assessment reports that include findings, analyses, recommendations, maps, and site-specific constraints.
Experience supporting NEPA, environmental permitting, stormwater management, waste management, contaminated-media management, or environmental compliance activities.
Experience with GIS data management for federal facilities, military installations, infrastructure programs, or other secure Government projects.
Experience coordinating with local governments, utility providers, regulatory agencies, installation personnel, and project stakeholders.
Experience supporting projects across multiple locations and adapting to changing task-order requirements.

Additional Position Expectations

Some assignments may involve access to secure Government facilities, Government information systems, or procurement-sensitive information.
Employees must comply with applicable cybersecurity, information-safeguarding, site-access, safety, quality, and environmental requirements.
Contractor personnel will provide technical analysis, data management, recommendations, and support but will not perform inherently governmental functions or make commitments on behalf of the Government.

Security Clearance Requirement

An active Secret security clearance is required for this position.

This position is part of our Federal Solutions team.

The Federal Solutions segment delivers resources to our US government customers that ensure the success of missions around the globe. Our intelligent employees drive the state of the art as they provide services and solutions in the areas of defense, security, intelligence, infrastructure, and environmental. We promote a culture of excellence and close-knit teams that take pride in delivering, protecting, and sustaining our nation's most critical assets, from Earth to cyberspace. jobs.title: Geospatial Engineering Surveyor
jobs.description:
About Castle Surveys

Castle Surveys is an independent, multidisciplinary geospatial and land surveying company, headquartered in Ashby de la Zouch with offices in Manchester, London, Cheltenham and Scotland. We deliver everything in-house, with no subcontracting, and work to an ISO 9001 aligned management system.
Our work is genuinely varied. On any given week the team might be scanning a listed building, mapping a motorway corridor, surveying a reservoir bed, tracing buried utilities or setting out a data centre floor. That variety is exactly what makes this a brilliant place to build a surveying career.

The role

We're looking for a Geospatial Engineering Surveyor to join our team. You'll be the person on site making sure the data is right: establishing control, carrying out topographic surveys, setting out, then processing it all back in the office and delivering clear, accurate results to our clients.
It's a hands on role with real responsibility. You'll work across construction, infrastructure, highways, utilities, heritage and development projects, sometimes as part of a team and sometimes leading small jobs yourself.
And it doesn't stop there. Once you've got the core skills nailed, we'll train you in our specialist areas, so the role can grow with you.

Key responsibilities

On site

Carry out topographic land surveys using total stations, GNSS and levels, capturing detail to the client's specification.
Establish and maintain survey control networks, including traverses, GNSS control and precise levelling, tied to OS National Grid and Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Set out for construction and engineering works, from site grids, piles and foundations to roads, drainage and structures.
Carry out as-built and monitoring surveys, and check work against design.
Use 3D laser scanners for measured building and structure surveys, [CONFIRM, e.g. Leica RTC360].
Plan your own site day: kit checks, calibration records, access and permits.

Back in the office

Process and adjust survey data, including control network adjustments and GNSS post processing.
Produce accurate 2D and 3D CAD drawings to Castle Surveys and client standards.
Write clear survey reports and control reports, including accuracy statements and QA records.
Check your own work and colleagues' work as part of our ISO 9001 aligned QA process.

Health, safety and clients

Work safely at all times, following RAMS, site rules and our Behavioural Safety Programme, and use your Stop Work Authority when needed.
Contribute to RAMS for your jobs.
Be the friendly, professional face of Castle Surveys on site, liaising with clients, site managers and engineers.
Look after company vehicles and survey equipment.

Where the role can take you

The core surveying skills are the foundation. Once you're confident with them, you can move into one or more of our specialist areas, with training provided.

Mobile mapping
Capturing highways, rail and urban corridors at road speed with vehicle mounted LiDAR and 360° imagery, then processing and extracting design ready data.

Drone (UAV) surveys
Planning and flying photogrammetry and LiDAR missions over sites, quarries, roofs and infrastructure
CAA flyer ID, GVC, and flight training under our Operations Manual

Hydrographic surveys
Bathymetric surveys of reservoirs, rivers, canals and harbours from our survey boats, including multibeam and single beam work

HP SitePrint robotic layout
Printing building layouts directly onto slabs and floors for contractors, including data centre and commercial fit out projects

What you'll need

Essential

At least [INSERT, e.g. 2] years' experience as a land, engineering or geospatial surveyor.
Confident with total stations, GNSS and levels on site.
Solid understanding of survey control, coordinate systems and survey accuracy.
Experience of setting out on construction or engineering sites.
Good working knowledge of CAD, ideally AutoCAD or Civil 3D, and survey processing software such as [INSERT, e.g. Leica Infinity, n4ce or LSS].
Clear, accurate written reports.
CSCS card, or willingness to get one.
Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel and stay away when a job needs it.
A careful, safety first attitude and pride in getting things right.

Desirable

A degree, HNC or HND in geomatics, surveying, civil engineering or similar.
Working towards, or holding, RICS or CICES chartered status.
Experience with 3D laser scanning and point cloud software, such as Leica Cyclone or Autodesk ReCap.
Any exposure to mobile mapping, drone surveys, hydrographic work or robotic layout.
Rail (PTS), highways or utility survey experience.
First aid or SSSTS qualifications.

What we offer

A competitive salary, depending on experience.
23 days' holiday plus bank holidays.
Company pool vehicle or allowance, fuel card,
Pension scheme.
Clear progression into specialist areas such as mobile mapping, drones, hydrographic surveying and HP SitePrint.
The latest kit, from Leica instruments and scanners to mobile mapping systems and survey vessels.
A friendly, owner led company where your work is noticed and your ideas are listened to.
Toil System

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note telling us about the surveys you've enjoyed most to info@castlesurveys.co.uk, with "Geospatial Engineering Surveyor" in the subject line.

Castle Surveys is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone, and we're happy to make reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process; just let us know.

jobs.title: Geospatial Data Scientist Lead
jobs.description:
The Company

We are NEURAL EARTH
. We bring clarity to physical risk, enabling leaders to engage with confidence and enact resilient, business-critical decisions. Today's environmental, economic, and infrastructure challenges are deeply interconnected, yet the data required to understand these relationships is scattered across siloed and aging systems. Neural Earth enables operational execution, delivering a single decision intelligence platform that unifies planetary, governmental, and asset-level data, always on and always learning. This is technical work that requires patience. It requires teams willing to operate at the intersection of AI research, geospatial science, distributed systems, and enterprise deployment. It is also incredibly rewarding. Join us at Neural Earth — the next frontier is here.

THE TEAM

Neural Earth's Science team transforms raw environmental data into intelligence that moves markets and protects lives. You will join a growing group of geospatial data scientists, ML specialists, and researchers led by a strong leader, who sets a high bar: the work must be publishable in quality and deployable in production. You will collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, and Revenue to make sure what we build in science reaches the customers who need it.

THE ROLE

This is a founding, staff-level role with a direct report. You will own Neural Earth's geospatial data science function, define the technical strategy for how we ingest, structure, and pipeline multi-hazard geospatial data, and make that data usable by our ML and AI teams to power quantified intelligence products used by insurers, government agencies, and infrastructure operators. You are comfortable across geospatial data broadly, not specialized in a single sub-discipline like meteorology. You work at the intersection of geospatial engineering, data infrastructure, and applied science. You do not stop at the paper. You build things that ship, scale, and make hazard data understandable to people who are not scientists. This is you!

How You'll Be Successful

Model: Design and deploy Python-based geospatial models that quantify environmental and physical hazards at a level of precision that drives real business decisions, not just research outputs.
Build: Architect Neural Earth's geospatial data pipelines from the ground up, including the systems, infrastructure, and scientific frameworks that turn raw hazard data into indexed intelligence products customers can act on. Structure and prepare that data so it is ready to run through the models our ML and AI teams build, and own the production pipelines that keep it flowing reliably.
Translate: Convert complex, multi-hazard scientific findings into business-ready products that are legible and compelling to insurance underwriters, government operators, and enterprise decision-makers.
Lead: Serve as Neural Earth's internal and external subject matter expert on geospatial data science, driving customer calls, proposals, and strategy discussions, while managing and developing a direct report.
Validate: Establish rigorous validation standards for all geospatial models, ensuring methods are reproducible, cross-validated, and defensible across industries and geographies.

WHY WE VALUE YOU

You have 5+ years of experience working with geospatial data broadly, across formats and hazard types, in a research or applied setting, in addition to any graduate degree.
You write Python fluently and have built production-grade geospatial models using GeoPandas, Rasterio, GDAL, xarray, and Shapely.
You know how to engineer and structure geospatial data so it is ready to feed ML and AI models built by others. You would rather apply and extend someone else's research five different ways than chase original research yourself.
