jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Environment Testing in Little Rock, AR is seeking a Sample Receiving Technician to join our team. Our laboratory specializes in environmental testing. Providing analytical data and support to a diverse range of clients.

The Sample Receiving Technician is responsible for logging and tracking the receipt and shipment of samples into and out of the laboratory, verifying sample receipt, and supporting accurate and timely documentation. This role assists with preparing bottle kits for client delivery, sample login, labeling, routing, prioritization, and storage in accordance with Chain of Custody requirements and documented procedures. The Sample Receiving Technician may also support sample pick-up and delivery, customer service, courier duties, and the proper disposal of samples and waste in accordance with applicable procedures.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Receive and unload incoming samples or consignments in accordance with SOP; verify receipt against the Chain of Custody (COC), match samples to the corresponding quote, and document discrepancies daily. Review COCs for accuracy, completeness, and correctness, and seek resolution when needed.
Log samples into the laboratory information management system daily and assign job numbers for tracking purposes; distribute associated paperwork to Project Managers.
Label samples with assigned job numbers and deliver them to the appropriate laboratories for analysis each day.
Prepare bottle kits daily for shipment to clients for sample collection and return analysis, following established procedures, including EPA and DOT requirements.
Ship samples to other laboratories in accordance with DOT regulations when testing is not performed at the local facility.
Dispose of spent samples, waste, and other potentially hazardous materials in accordance with established procedures.
Clean and organize the department daily to maintain a safe, orderly work environment.
Maintain and promote safety by conducting all operations in a safe and environmentally compliant manner.
Stock supplies and assist with inventory management to ensure appropriate quantities of materials are available to perform assigned tasks.
Perform sample splitting and composites as requested.
Perform courier duties as needed to support laboratory and client requirements.
Comply with all driver procedures, certification requirements, and company driver policies.
Organize walk-in coolers to support sample storage and retrieval.
Ship empty coolers back to clients and other Eurofins laboratories; log all outgoing coolers to maintain a detailed cooler inventory.
Conduct all client interactions in a professional and courteous manner.
Perform other duties as assigned by local management.

Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Valid state-issued driver’s license to operate company vehicles.
Basic computer skills include; ability to accurately input data into LIMS systems and ability to manage multiple emails.
Must be able to lift 55 lbs routinely and safely and must be able to work standing for most of the day
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

Additional Information

This is a full time position Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. Some weekend work and overtime may be required.

Pay Rate Range for this position is $17 -$21 / hour (DOE).

Candidates within a commutable distance to Little Rock, AR are encouraged to apply.

We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Natural Resources and Lands Management Division:

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section of NRLM:

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships:

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Job Description

Role Description:

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.
Prepares or coordinates permit applications, right-of-way and special use authorization requests, and related submissions to local, state, and federal agencies.
Obtains authorizations under CWA

401/404, NPDES
402, Fish & Game Code

1602/1610, ESA/CESA, NHPA
106, ARPA, FLPMA, Raker Act, Wilderness Act, Wild & Scenic Rivers Act, and related federal/state authorities. Prepares, reviews, and coordinates CEQA, NEPA, NHPA, FLPMA, and related environmental review and compliance documentation.
Prepares and manages technical studies and reports concerning environmental, biological, cultural, land, and other natural resource matters.
Critically reviews and evaluates consultant work associated with planning, permitting, environmental review, technical studies, and compliance monitoring, and develops scopes of work and supports consultant contract administration, including schedules, budgets, deliverables, and fieldwork coordination.
Coordinates interdisciplinary review of project proposals, technical studies, and environmental documentation; performs environmental review of third-party applications for use of SFPUC lands.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species .

Peraton is seeking a Senior GIS Developer
to lead the production of federal species range maps for a high-priority data integration program. You will produce range maps for marine and anadromous taxa in compliance with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), facilitating iterative review cycles with government SMEs and coordinating formal government sign-off.

Work Location:
Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

Lead species range map production, producing complete range maps for all marine and anadromous taxa in full compliance with the FWS Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Obtain and review the FWS Range Mapping SOP at or before project kickoff
Conduct spatial data aggregation and normalization of range data from cloud data platform outputs, applying CRS transformations and spatial format standardization
Validate spatial intersects against authoritative geographic layers, addressing dynamic habitat boundaries and overlapping Critical Habitat designations
Facilitate iterative range map review cycles with both FWS Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries (National Marine Fisheries Service) SMEs, incorporating feedback and producing revised map versions
Produce QA documentation for each individual range map, ensuring all maps meet SOP acceptance criteria before submission for government sign-off
Coordinate FWS Ecological Services sign-off on the Range Map Set deliverable
Support the development of updated range maps post-production as part of operational handoff documentation

Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience, or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience, or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 12 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.
Extensive GIS experience with a focus on species range mapping or federal environmental applications.
Direct experience with FWS Range Mapping SOP or equivalent federal range mapping standards.
Proficiency in ArcGIS, QGIS, or equivalent GIS platforms.
Proficiency in Python for GIS automation and spatial data processing, including ArcPy or equivalent scripting libraries.
Proficiency in SQL for querying and validating spatial data within cloud data platforms.
Experience with coordinate reference system transformations and spatial data normalization.
Experience conducting spatial intersect validation and Critical Habitat analysis.
Strong QA documentation skills for geospatial deliverables

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with NOAA Fisheries marine or anadromous species range data.
Familiarity with Databricks or cloud data platforms for spatial data retrieval.

jobs.description:

10/02/2026

Application Deadline

10/18/2026

Agency

Department of Fish and Wildlife

Salary Range

$4,738 - $7,247

Position Type

Employee

Position Title

Fish Screening, Passage and Restoration Coordinator (Natural Resource Specialist 2)

Job Description

Help the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife fulfill its mission:
To protect and enhance Oregon's fish and wildlife and their habitats for use and enjoyment by present and future generations.

We are hiring for one full-time, permanent position located in Klamath Falls, Oregon.

What You Will Do

In this role, you will be tasked with advancing ODFW priorities for fish screening, fish passage and aquatic restoration efforts in the Klamath Watershed. The position is a critical liaison between project proponents, the fish screening program, fish passage program and Habitat Division. You will be responsible for outreach and providing technical assistance to irrigation districts, water users, watershed councils and conservation groups in the Klamath Basin. Additionally, you will perform data collection, analysis, and evaluation for potential fish screening and passage projects and associated habitat restoration projects, as well as project coordination. You will be part of the Klamath Watershed District and as such, will have the opportunity to participate in a wide range of other fish, wildlife, and habitat related activities throughout the Klamath Basin.

This position will also require the successful candidate to either possess or obtain an All-Terrain Vehicle Safety Education card and a Boater Education Card within the first 6 months of hire.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required.

For a full review of the position details, duties, and working conditions, please review the position description located here.

Clearly describe how you meet the desired attributes in your application materials. We cannot accept additional application materials after the application deadline. These materials determine whether you move forward in the selection process and help establish your starting salary. Be sure your work and education history is accurate, thorough, and fully reflects your skills and experience, even if they do not seem directly related to the position. Click here to learn more about
Equal Pay Analysis
and
What You Need to Know to Get the Job

Minimum Qualifications

What we are looking for:

To be considered for this position, applicants must meet one of the following options:

Option 1: Six years of biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included one year of at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports
Option 2: Two years of biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included one year of at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports, AND a Bachelor's degree in Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Bachelor’s degree with at least 45 quarter (30 semester) hours of biological/ecological coursework
Option 3: One year biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports, AND a Master's degree Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Master’s degree in biological/ecological sciences
Option 4: A Doctorate degree in Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Doctorate degree in biological/ecological sciences.

Note: Applicants who have obtained a Master’s degree or Doctorate that included work experience from an internship, work/study, thesis, or similar program may list this experience in their application to receive credit for the work experience. The Master’s degree/Doctorate and applicable work experience will be considered separately, and both the education and applicable experience may count toward minimum qualifications.

Desired Attributes

Proven experience collaborating with other entities which may include: Tribes, watershed councils, non-governmental organizations, water users, and private landowners to advance fish and/or wildlife habitat projects.
Experience in providing technical expertise for fish, wildlife, or habitat related projects.
Experience implementing aquatic or riparian restoration projects.
Proven ability to build and maintain successful interagency, Tribal, and non-governmental partnerships.
Excellent public speaking, writing, and outreach abilities.
Ability to use persuasive diplomacy while working with landowners, partner agencies, and the public.
Experience with fish passage and screening technology and solutions.

Application Details and Instructions

The State of Oregon does not request or require your age, date of birth, attendance or graduation dates from an educational institution during the application process.
The salary listed is the non-PERS qualifying salary range. If the successful candidate is PERS qualifying, the salary range will reflect an additional 6.95%.
This recruitment will be used to establish a list of qualified people to fill the current vacancy and may be used to fill other vacancies as they occur.
State of Oregon Employees, must apply through their employee Workday account.
Please save a copy of this job announcement for reference, as it is not available for you to view after the announcement deadline.
First time applying to the State of Oregon? Consider utilizing a WorkSource Oregon Resource event! You can also view this video or this knowledge article for assistance.
Reasonable accommodation for interviews will be provided upon request to individuals with disabilities.
The job posting closes at 11:59 PM (PDT/PST) on the close date. After you submit your application, be sure to respond to the two questionnaires relating to public records requests and veterans’ preference immediately following your submittal. These questions are necessary to complete the application process
If you are experiencing difficulty applying for this position or have questions, please call 503.947.6051 and ask to speak to a recruiter.

Benefits Of Joining Our Team

ODFW is dedicated to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workforce as we strive to represent and better serve our neighboring communities. Our most important asset is our employees, and each person brings unique, different, and important contributions to the workplace and community we serve. With Oregon’s changing demographics, a workforce that reflects this change will make us stronger and create an opportunity for better decision making.

To learn more about the agency and the work we do, view the following video at https://myodfw.com/about

If you enjoy the outdoors, Oregon is the place for you. We have glaciated mountain peaks to the east, the Pacific Ocean to the west and the massive Columbia River Gorge to the north. You can fish 365 days a year, and there is hunting for big game, waterfowl, and game birds. The Oregon coast attracts thousands of people who clam, crab and fish in the ocean for halibut, salmon, and tuna. The outdoor opportunities are endless when it comes to fish and wildlife in Oregon! Oregon is known for their vineyards, breweries, and adventures for the whole family to enjoy. To learn more about the department, the work we do, and see our beautiful state, view the following video at https://youtu.be/8CjDPiPMGAk

Additional Benefits Include

11 paid holidays a year and a competitive benefits package
Advancement and learning opportunities that will help grow your career with the State of Oregon

Additional Information

If you are hired, you will become part of the State's management service. /The employee in this position will be represented by the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) and will be subject to all terms and conditions of the collective bargaining agreement. Pay and benefits on all job listings may change without notice.
Finalists are subject to both a criminal history and motor vehicles check. Driving is required for this position. Adverse background and/or driving information may disqualify you from further consideration.
Within three days of hire, applicants will be required to complete the U.S. Department Homeland Security's I-9 form confirming authorization to work in the United States. ODFW participates in E-Verify. ODFW is not able to support VISA sponsorships
Veterans’ and Oregon National Guard preference: Eligible Veterans and Oregon National Guard servicemembers (current and former) who meet the qualifications of the position will be awarded candidate preference. For more information, please visit Veterans Resources.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Planning, Geography, and Environmental Studies
jobs.description:
Job Summary

UFV's Department of Planning, Geography and Environmental Studies (PGES) in the Faculty of Science invites applications for a tenure-track, open-rank Professor of Land-Use Planning with an interest in one or more of the following areas: sustainable development, food security, environmental, and Indigenous community planning. The successful applicant will join a thriving faculty that supports programs in Geography, Environmental Studies, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The Bachelor of Regional and Community Planning (BRCP) degree has recently been accredited and has strong enrollment. The successful candidate will help to further grow and strengthen the new planning program in PGES and contribute to practicums and professional experience, PGES programs’ curriculum development and teaching.

The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses and supervise undergraduate research students through studio, applied practicum, and independent study courses. Teaching assignments may include Settlements(PLAN 160), Social Geography: The Urban Experience (GEOG 241), GIS for the Built Environment (GEOG 355), Quantitative Methods in Geography (GEOG 252), Planning Law (PLAN 310) and Indigenous Land Use and Community Planning (PLAN 410), but the final list will be tailored to the expertise of the successful candidate. In addition to teaching, the successful candidate will actively participate in PGES activities, service, events, and initiatives, and will be committed to ongoing professional development.

PGES seeks a collegial and energetic individual with exceptional communication skills, demonstrated excellence in teaching at the undergraduate level, and experience in teaching across traditional disciplinary boundaries and delivering courses in community settings. The successful candidate is expected to build relationships with Fraser Valley municipalities and Indigenous communities by providing students with collaborative and integrative applied experiential learning opportunities. Incorporating Indigenous perspectives in the curriculum is essential, as is teaching international students and managing the needs of students in a diverse learning environment.

Short-listed applicants will have an emerging record of applied research or professional productivity commensurate with their experience. The ability to attract external funding and establish a successful applied research program at UFV to support research and student learning experiences are highly desirable. The ability to use Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing, statistical software (SPSS/STATA), and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence to support land-use planning will be an asset, as is experience with community outreach in agricultural regions with rapidly growing urban centers.

Qualifications

Extensive knowledge of land-use planning: urban spatial structure and physical design within urban and regional settings.
A master’s degree in urban and regional planning or a closely related field from a recognized post-secondary institution is required, in addition to extensive professional experience. However, a PhD in the mentioned disciplines is preferred.
Registered Professional Planner certification with the Canadian Institute of Planners, facilitated by the Planning Standards Board of Canada, is required .
Teaching experience at the undergraduate level with recent evidence of teaching excellence is preferred.
Familiarity with technology-supported teaching both in the classroom, online and in the planning profession.
Effective cross-cultural, interdisciplinary communication skills and experience working with Indigenous communities are assets.
A growing list of impactful applied research and/or community-based planning initiatives.
Interest in service contribution to PGES, UFV, and Indigenous communities of the Fraser Valley.

How to Apply

To be considered for this position, please submit a complete application package that includes a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching philosophy statement, research interest statement, samples of scholarly activities (e.g., publication or project portfolio), and three letters of reference. In your application, please indicate your eligibility to work legally in Canada.

Applications will be reviewed by the SAC in December 2026, however the posting will be kept open for applications until the end of January 2027.

You will receive a confirmation email once you successfully apply for the position. If not, do not hesitate to contact the Njoyn Help Desk at candidate.njoynhelp@cgi.com or 1-877-427-7717, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. (EST).

UFV is committed to equity in employment, and all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. UFV will contact only candidates receiving an interview. Shortlisted applicants may be required to undergo a criminal record check and a verification of their education credentials.

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Cherie Enns, RPP, Chair, Bachelor of Regional and Community Planning, University of the Fraser Valley, at cherie.enns@ufv.ca.

About UFV

The University of the Fraser Valley is located on the traditional territory of the Halq'eméylem-speaking peoples. We express our gratitude and respect for the honour of living and working in Stó:lo Tém:éxw (Stó:lo Land; Stó:lo World). In all that we do, UFV strives to support and honour the Stó:lo peoples goals of self-determination and well-being on these lands. A commitment to Indigenization and Reconciliation is core to our institutional Vision and Integrated Strategic Plan: IYAQAWTXW — which means House of Transformation. This commitment includes the goal of centering Indigenous ways of knowing throughout our organization, recognizing our responsibilities to community, and a multi-year plan to increase the number of Indigenous faculty, staff, and administrators working at UFV.

UFV has campus locations in Abbotsford, Chilliwack, Mission, and Hope in the beautiful British Columbia, and in Chandigarh, India. Recognized as one of BC's top employers, UFV offers a combination of career and lifestyle benefits. Join a team of 1,400 passionate professionals who value integrity, inclusivity and excellence. At UFV, you will serve a vibrant community and shape the future of 15,000 students.

Indigenization, equity, and diversity are essential to our work as a university. A diverse community fosters the inclusion of voices that have been historically underrepresented and marginalized. At UFV, we are committed to recruiting a diverse workforce that represents the community we proudly serve. We encourage applications from Indigenous peoples, members of groups that experience discrimination due to race, colour, place of origin, ancestry, and/or religion, persons who identify as women and 2SLGBTQ+, and persons with disabilities. We invite applicants to complete a confidential self-identification survey as part of the application process. All questions are voluntary, with an option to decline to answer. Information will be used to support efforts to broaden the diversity of the recruitment process, and results are not shared with the selection committee. Inquiries about the survey may be directed to careers@ufv.ca. Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. In an effort to be both environmentally and fiscally responsible, UFV will contact only candidates receiving an interview. We thank all applicants for considering UFV for employment. Shortlisted applicants may be required to undergo a criminal record check and/ or a verification of their education credentials.

UFV is committed to the principle of equity in employment.

jobs.title: Environmental Planner/Permitting Specialist
jobs.description:
What’s the Opportunity?

Anchor QEA is seeking a full-time Environmental Planning and Permitting Specialist to support the acquisition of regulatory permits and approvals for waterfront construction and redevelopment, dredging, and restoration projects primarily located in California. You will assist project managers with completing permit applications, including developing and reviewing environmental studies, status reports, and other associated deliverables; coordinate with team members to obtain necessary inputs, such as engineering design drawings, GIS analysis or mapping, and technical editing review; and complete quality control review of work products in collaboration with project managers. This position may also require some fieldwork, primarily in the local area. You will be a key member of project teams with opportunities to continue learning and helping to solve challenging environmental problems.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will support project teams, in collaboration with project managers, to obtain federal, state, and local permits and approvals mainly in California by:

Completing permit applications related to Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act, Sections 401 and 404 of the Clean Water Act, Section 1600 of the California Fish and Game Code, the Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act, the California Coastal Act, and other relevant local, state, and federal regulations
Completing supporting documentation and analyses, requiring review of relevant regulatory codes, preparation of compensatory mitigation plans, and documentation of alternatives analysis processes
Contributing to the development of technical discipline reports and studies, which may include those to support California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) compliance
Coordinating input from others as needed to deliver complete work products
Participating in client meetings and responding to agency, tribal, and public comments and questions on work products
Conducting fieldwork or site visits as needed (predominantly local travel)

What Are We Looking For?

Ideal Candidates Will Have The Following

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in a related field (e.g., environmental planning or policy, natural resources, etc.)
Minimum of three years relevant experience, preferably in consulting
Knowledge of environmental regulations with experience conducting ecological research or land use analysis
Demonstrated understanding of California permitting processes, including Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act, Sections 401 and 404 of the Clean Water Act (e.g., Individual Permits, Nationwide Permit Program Pre-construction Notifications, Regional General Permits), and Section 1600 of the California Fish and Game Code (e.g., Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements)
Experience conducting aquatic resource delineation surveys, applying delineation results to project impact assessments, and preparing permit applications
California Rapid Assessment Method certification is preferred, but not required
Ability to adapt to changing priorities and multiple concurrent projects/tasks, working both in teams and independently
Ability to excel in a fast paced, client service-oriented team environment and proven ability to work across disciplines internally and externally
Strong professional written and verbal communications skills

What Can You Expect?

You Can Expect

Highly supportive environment as part of multi-disciplinary, collaborative teams
Opportunities to help shape project outcomes through impact-focused roles
Strong emphasis on professional development for technical and leadership growth
Opportunities for client and agency interaction, helping to guide key decision makers
Culture of flexibility and accountability with an emphasis on work-life balance

Who Are We?

Anchor QEA is an environmental science and engineering consulting firm that is focused on improving the environment and our communities by solving challenging problems. We employ more than 400 people in offices around the United States. Our vision is for a growing company that is our clients’ first choice for solving their most challenging problems and our employees’ first choice as a company where they want to work. Learn more about Anchor QEA at www.anchorqea.com

How to Apply?

Apply online through Anchor QEA’s Open Positions page at https://www.anchorqea.com/careers/careers-open-positions/. Veterans are encouraged to apply.

Additional Information

We work hard to embrace diversity and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, Anchor QEA is committed to a diverse, multi-cultural work environment. Anchor QEA does not discriminate in employment based on age, race, creed, gender, religion, marital status, veteran’s status, national origin, disability or sexual orientation.

jobs.title: Journey Environmental Services Specialist
jobs.description:
This posting intends to fill one (1) full-time position, and establish an eligibility list which may be used to fill future regular full-time or limited term vacancies over the next two (2) years.

This position is responsible for the overall coordination and implementation of SMUD's Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP). The role involves turning HCP commitments into an effective, ongoing program by overseeing implementation, compliance, monitoring, and reporting of the plan and its associated permit requirements. The successful candidate will conduct desktop environmental reviews of projects, assign environmental measures, track data, provide environmental training, calculate compensatory mitigation requirements, audit construction implementation of required measures, and prepare reports to ensure compliance with the HCP and incidental take permits. Coordination of these environmental requirements ensures HCP commitments are integrated into project activities and daily operations. The person in this position will be responsible for advancing and strengthening SMUD’s existing HCP implementation program by working with field and operational staff to translate regulatory and biological requirements into practical, repeatable operational processes.

Purpose

Serve as a technical resource supporting and coordinating SMUD’s projects, environmental programs and regulatory requirements, including:
Plan, develop, implement, and evaluate environmental programs;
Work with contractors and consultants;
Train business unit personnel in environmental procedures;
Ensure work quality and accuracy as it relates to environmental issues;
Ensure compliance with applicable environmental rules, policies, regulations, and procedures.

Nature and Scope

There are four (4) levels in this job classification series that have similar job content but with progressively more challenging degrees and levels of skill, responsibility, knowledge, experience, and qualification requirements:

Flex classifications (that permit progression from lower-level classes to higher level classes without examination based upon assessment of an individual's experience and performance) within the series:

Entry
: Incumbent acquires knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the tasks associated within the series but are not yet demonstrating these at the Journey level.
Journey
: Incumbent is demonstrating the required skills and knowledge to independently perform the full scope of the job.

Non-Flex classifications (that promote from lower-level classes to higher level classes and require an examination, such as an interview, based upon individual experience and performance) within the series.

Senior
: Advanced journey level resource who is responsible for advanced assignments, as dictated by the work needing to be performed; may serve in a lead and/or supervisory capacity.
Supervisor
: Working supervisor directing the work of a functional team.

Entry to Journey
: Incumbents at the entry level are required to successfully “progress” to the journey level within 60 months of appointment to remain within the job series.
Seniors and Supervisors must be hired through a promotional process and do not automatically progress from lower levels in the series.

Duties and Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance

Plan, develop, implement, and evaluate environmental programs to ensure compliance with applicable environmental rules, policies and regulations.
Prepare, review and submit permit applications, technical reports, and compliance documentation in a timely and accurate manner.
Monitor organizational activities for compliance and recommend corrective actions as needed.
Data Collection and Analysis

Conduct field assessments, sampling, and analysis of environmental data (e.g., air, water, soil, biological resources, hazardous materials) to evaluate risks and potential impacts.
Interpret environmental data and prepare detailed technical reports, summaries, and recommendations.
Provide technical expertise to support decision-making and project planning.
Environmental Education and Training

Develop, coordinate and deliver training programs for staff and stakeholders on environmental regulations, policies, and best practices.
Promote environmental awareness within the organization and community through presentations, workshops, and educational materials.
Project Management

Manage or serve as a key contributor to environmental projects and initiatives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate with cross-functional teams to integrate environmental considerations into project planning, design and implementation.
Track project milestones, budgets and deliverables, ensuring successful project outcomes.
Sustainability Initiatives

Identify opportunities to reduce the organization’s environmental footprint and improve sustainability practices.
Develop strategies, track progress, and report on sustainability metrics and goals.
Community Engagement

Represent the organization in meetings with regulatory agencies, community organizations, and external partners.
Facilitate public outreach, engagement and education efforts on environmental issues and programs.
Emergency Response Preparedness

Develop and maintain response plans for environmental emergencies such as spills, releases or contamination events.
Participate in drills, training, and incident response activities to ensure organizational readiness.
Research and Monitoring

Stay current on emerging environmental regulations, policies and technologies and evaluate their potential impacts on organizational operations.
Conduct research and prepare recommendations for program or policy updates.
Grant Writing and Funding Acquisition

Research and identify funding opportunities to support environmental programs and initiatives.
Prepare grant proposals and manage awarded projects to ensure compliance with funding requirements.
Collaboration and Communication

Serve as a liaison between departments, leadership, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders on environmental issues.
Clearly communicate technical information, both orally and in writing, to diverse audiences including non-technical staff and the public.
Other Duties

Perform other related responsibilities as assigned. Work schedules, locations, and hours may vary depending on business and project needs.

Required Education

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental studies, engineering, biology, geology, archaeology, or a related field or equivalent experience. If no degree, seven or more (7+) years of experience are required.

Required Experience Qualifications

Three or more (3+) years of relevant work experience as an Environmental Specialist or Technician or equivalent role, with specific experience performing relevant environmental tasks and duties.

Required Licenses/Certificates

Must possess and maintain a valid California Driver’s License (CDL) with a satisfactory driving record (not more than two moving violations in the last two years).

Knowledge Of

Environmental fundamentals, procedures, policies, standards, practices, and industry trends pertaining to one or more of the following: California Environmental Quality Act; Clean Water Act; endangered species; stormwater; hazardous materials business plans; soil sampling, management, disposal, cathodic well installation; air quality permitting; water quality permitting; and/or greenhouse gas reporting;
Regulatory processes at the federal, state and local levels to effectively represent SMUD in environmental concerns;
Methods and techniques for report preparation and writing;
Techniques and practices for problem research and resolution;
Methods and techniques for record keeping;
Standard operating procedures for modern office equipment including a computer and applicable software;
English grammar, punctuation and vocabulary standards.

Skills To

Plan, develop, implement, and administer environmental programs on one’s own;
Conduct environmental audits, inspections and assessments;
Interpret, assess and apply pertinent policies, procedures, regulations, and requirements relative to environmental fields;
Promote regulatory awareness among business unit managers;
Recommend changes to work processes to reduce risk and work closely with others to implement changes;
Conduct trend analysis of data, identify and assess problems, and recommend solutions;
Develop and provide training as needed;
Apply applicable laws, codes and regulations;
Use a wide variety of electronic equipment and software relevant to the tasks;
Communicate effectively orally and in writing internally/externally;
Establish and maintain effective working relationships internally/externally.

Desirable Qualifications

Implementation and management of complex environmental programs including program development.
Environmental compliance experience including biological resources and regulatory expertise.
Experience working with regulatory agencies, permitting process and environmental compliance programs.
Knowledge of CEQA, federal and state endangered species regulations, and habitat conservation plans.
Familiarity with utility construction methods.
Ability to coordinate and collaborate effectively with planning and field staff, consultants, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders.
Experience coordinating cross-functional teams.
Independent decision-making and sound environmental judgement.
Ability to identify and resolve compliance issues proactively.

Physical Requirements

Applicants must be able to perform the essential job functions with or without a reasonable accommodation.

Hybrid Work

This position will be required to work onsite one or more days a week on a regular basis; sometimes more or less, depending on the work and, at any of our SMUD locations. SMUD takes pride in powering the Sacramento region community where we live and work. We value the strong working relationships we develop with our colleagues. Our approach to remote work will continue to evolve. Please be aware that should SMUD’s business needs change, emergencies occur, or various other reasons arise, you may be required to report onsite on a part-time or full-time basis.

CalPERS

SMUD is a CalPERS agency
. As a member of the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS), SMUD offers eligible employees access to a defined benefit pension plan along with other valuable retirement and health benefits. This program helps provide financial security both during your career and after retirement. To learn more about CalPERS and the benefits it offers, please visit www.calpers.ca.gov.

Impulsados por la innovación y centrados en crear momentos de alegría a través de los alimentos y bebidas, nuestras decisiones se guían por y para el consumidor, creando oportunidades para que nuestros asociados realicen un trabajo significativo y tengan un impacto duradero en las comunidades a las que servimos.

Responsibilities

La oportunidad

Liderar la estrategia regional de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Sustentabilidad (EHS)
para las operaciones de Chile, Argentina, Uruguay y Paraguay con alcance en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota.

Gestionar riesgos críticos y fortalecer la prevención de incidentes, asegurando el cumplimiento del marco regulatorio de seguridad, salud ocupacional y medioambiente en los tres países. Liderar la agenda de sustentabilidad en materia de agua, energía, emisiones, residuos y envases, traduciendo los compromisos corporativos en planes de acción medibles.

Liderar y desarrollar al equipo regional de EHS, así como asesorar al liderazgo de Operaciones en decisiones relacionadas con la seguridad de las personas, la continuidad operacional y los riesgos regulatorios. Impulsar una cultura preventiva integrada en la operación y orientada a la reducción sostenible de riesgos críticos.

Tu impacto

Define la estrategia regional de seguridad, salud ocupacional y sustentabilidad, y responde por su ejecución en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota de Chile, Argentina y Uruguay.
Asegura el cumplimiento del marco legal de seguridad, salud y medioambiente en los tres países, incluidos la gestión preventiva exigida a la organización, los protocolos de vigilancia de la salud y el control documental y en terreno de empresas contratistas.
Gestiona la relación con autoridades y organismos administradores: permisos, autorizaciones sectoriales, reportes regulatorios y atención de fiscalizaciones, respondiendo por su oportunidad y exactitud.
Conduce la investigación de accidentes e incidentes de alto potencial, valida las causas raíz y verifica el cierre efectivo de los planes de acción.
Lidera la agenda de sustentabilidad de la operación —agua, energía, emisiones, y residuos —, traduciendo los compromisos corporativos en metas por sitio con responsables y plazos.
Define el modelo de formación en seguridad y salud, y responde por su cobertura y por el cumplimiento de las horas de formación exigidas por la normativa.
Lidera el equipo regional de seguridad, salud y medioambiente, y administra el presupuesto del área.
Reporta el desempeño del área al equipo de liderazgo de Operaciones y a la organización regional, mediante indicadores de exposición y de avance de los planes de control, no únicamente de accidentabilidad ocurrida.

Formación en Ingeniería Industrial, Química, Ambiental, Mecánica o carrera afín.
Más de 10 años de experiencia liderando Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Medio Ambiente (EHS) en operaciones industriales, manufactura, logística o distribución. Experiencia en la industria de alimentos y bebidas será considerada un plus.
Más de 4 años de experiencia liderando equipos EHS a nivel país o regional, idealmente equipos multiculturales y distribuidos en diferentes países.
Experiencia sólida en gestión de riesgos críticos, prevención de fatalidades, investigación de incidentes y análisis de causa raíz.
Conocimiento y experiencia en gestión de contratistas y cumplimiento regulatorio en materia de seguridad, salud ocupacional y medioambiente en entornos multinacionales.
Experiencia en implementación y auditoría de sistemas ISO 45001 e ISO 14001.
Conocimiento en gestión ambiental operacional, incluyendo agua, energía, residuos, emisiones y sustentabilidad.
Experiencia liderando procesos de transformación cultural y/o regulatoria en EHS.
Inglés avanzado.
Disponibilidad para viajar entre 30% y 40% del tiempo dentro de la región SoCo.
Deseable: Posgrado en Gestión, Sustentabilidad, Salud Ocupacional o área relacionada.
Deseable: Registro o certificación como Experto en Prevención de Riesgos, de acuerdo con la normativa local.

Si esta es una oportunidad que te interesa, te alentamos a postularte aún si no cumples con el 100% de los requisitos.

Qué puedes esperar de nosotros:

Oportunidades para aprender y desarrollarte todos los días a través de una amplia oferta de programas.
Plataformas internas digitales que promueven el self-learning.
Programas de desarrollo de acuerdo con habilidades de Liderazgo.
Entrenamientos especializados de acuerdo con el rol.
Experiencias de aprendizaje con proveedores internos y externos.
Nos encanta celebrar el éxito, por lo que contamos con programas de reconocimiento por antigüedad, comportamientos, liderazgo, momentos de vida, entre otros.
Programas de bienestar financiero que te ayudarán a alcanzar tus metas en todas las etapas de la vida.
Un programa de flexibilidad que te permitirá balancear tu vida personal y laboral, adaptando tu jornada laboral a tu estilo de vida.
Y porque tu familia también es importante para nosotros, ellos también pueden gozar de beneficios como nuestra Línea de Bienestar, miles de Convenios y Descuentos, programas de Becas para tus hijos, Planes de Ayuda para diferentes momentos de vida, entre otros.

Practice/Department: Compliance

Dudek’s journey began in 1980 with a vision to serve Southern California’s water and wastewater agencies.

Today, we are a 100% employee-owned firm supporting clients nationwide and delivering projects that improve and protect the built and natural environments of communities throughout the United States. Our work has been recognized by leading industry organizations , and we’ve been honored with multiple national Top Workplace Awards.

Our employee-owners are unified by a singular commitment to supporting projects that address key societal issues, such as the transition to renewable energy, infrastructure hardening and repair, environmental protection, and community resilience.

Learn more about our award-winning culture

you will have the opportunity to shape.

Position Overview

Who You Are

As an employee-owner
, you embrace accountability, working safely, and collaboration while thinking resourcefully and independently.

Like all Dudekians , you are curious and solution-oriented
, with the ability to adapt quickly to changes and approach challenges with a spirit of innovation
.

How You’ll Make An Impact

Dudek is seeking a self-motivated, enthusiastic individual for an Environmental Compliance Specialist. The selected individual will support environmental compliance efforts, regulatory research, field monitoring, data collection, reporting, and ensure project adherence to environmental laws and regulations. Additionally, the Environmental Compliance Specialist I will assist with inspecting construction project(s) for compliance with Storm water regulations, particularly the California Construction General Permit as a Storm Water Inspector. A Storm Water Inspector is responsible for ensuring site compliance with the California NPDES Construction General Permit, the project’s Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), and any other applicable requirements (e.g. Dewatering Permits, etc.).

The Environmental Compliance Specialist will gain hands-on experience in environmental compliance processes while working under the guidance of senior Environmental Compliance professionals.

Duties And Responsibilities

Regulatory Compliance and Permitting

Assists in researching and interpreting environmental regulations and policies to support project compliance.
Helps prepare and submit permit applications, compliance reports, and environmental documentation.
Supports project teams in ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local environmental laws (e.g., National Environmental Policy Act [NEPA], California Environmental Quality Act [CEQA], Clean Water Act [CWA], and Clean Air Act [CAA]).

Field Monitoring and Data Collection

Conducts site visits and field assessments to monitor environmental conditions and ensure regulatory adherence.
Collects and analyzes environmental data/samples related to air, water, and soil quality.
Assists in implementing best management practices (BMPs) for erosion control, stormwater management, and other environmental protections.
Conduct routine storm event and post-storm inspections to verify site compliance with SWPPP, maps and permit conditions.
Trouble-shoot site compliance and BMP issues.

Reporting and Documentation

Assists in preparing technical reports, impact assessments, and compliance audits.
Maintains, organizes, and prepares environmental records, monitoring/inspection logs, and field notes.
Supports teams with environmental impact mitigation planning and tracking.

Project Coordination and Communication

Supports coordination efforts with regulatory agencies, project managers, and field teams to ensure smooth compliance workflows.
Participates in team meetings and project discussions to provide regulatory insight.
Assists in responding to compliance-related inquiries and project needs.
Communicate site/BMP issues and inspection results with construction and client personnel

Professional Development and Industry Engagement

Stays up to date on environmental policies, industry trends, and best practices.
Participates in training programs, workshops, and professional organizations.
Seeks mentorship and learning opportunities to advance technical knowledge and compliance expertise.

Minimum Qualifications

1+ years’ experience in environmental compliance, stormwater inspections, regulatory assessments, or permitting.
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, or a related life sciences field.
Strong communication and teamwork abilities.
Capable of field work and walking on difficult terrain.
Must possess a valid driver’s license and have active personal automobile liability insurance by first day of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

Understanding of environmental laws and regulations.
Strong technical writing and analytical skills.
Strong Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS), or environmental modeling tools is a plus.
Familiarity with Best Management Practice (BMP) and NPDES regulation knowledge.
Familiarity with construction job sites and plans.
Access to a 4WD vehicle for use during inspections (preferred not required). If a 4WD vehicle is required for a specific site inspection, one can be provided.

Compensation:
$25.00-$38.00 hourly*

Final agreed-upon compensation will be based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, an individual’s related experience, education, certifications, skills, and work location. Successful candidates must pass a pre-employment drug test and background check prior to beginning employment.

Working Conditions

This job operates in a remote or office-based environment and this role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, printers, etc.
This job requires occasional project site visits, based outdoors which can include excessive noise, uneven walking surfaces, extreme weather, and moving vehicles and equipment.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. This job requires the following:

Working on a computer, sitting, or standing for long periods of time in an office or remote office setting.
Attending meetings, both in person and virtually, and speaking on the phone with peers, clients, etc.
Specific vision abilities, including close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

jobs.title: Environmental Representative II
jobs.description:
Generally responsible for environmental compliance activities for divisional facilities in North Dakota. This position will report to the Division Environmental Manager and will work as part of a multi-disciplinary team in a fast-paced oil and gas environment. The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting implementation of environmental programs for compliance with environmental laws and regulations as applicable to the upstream and midstream sectors of the oil and gas industry.

The primary responsibilities include but are not limited to: spill response and remediation support; air compliance inspections including LDAR, air permitting support, SPCC compliance inspections and plan upkeep, due diligence support, storm water inspections, site inventory, site diagram development, avian and wildlife protection, waste management including TENORM survey, support agency compliance inspections and audits, various sampling support of environmental media and oversight of general housekeeping of operations as pertaining to environmental quality and protection.

This position works closely and in conjunction with operations staff and other environmental staff and acts as a liaison between the division and environmental agencies, including coordination of agency inspections and follow-up activities. This position must have a working knowledge and maintain a proficient knowledge of applicable regulations while conducting regulatory assessments of divisional locations. We are looking for a self-motivated, hard-working team player who pays close attention to detail. This position requires an individual who is comfortable working alone while being fully capable of working within a team and interdisciplinary setting. Strong organizational and communication skills are essential.

This position requires recurring work outdoors, exposure to inclement weather and frequent travel to the field/facility sites (20% office, 80% field work). Infrequent travel to Divisional or Corporate Headquarters may be required. Physical requirements include extensive walking on uneven terrain and climbing/descending stairs, ability to lift and carry heavy objects (estimate up to 50 pounds), ability to carry 5-10 lbs for extended periods of time, and work at heights up to 30ft. This position also requires sufficient personal mobility, physical reflexes, and manual dexterity. Work is high paced and generally recurring in nature.

Job Requirements

Scope Of Duties & Responsibilities

Promote environmental awareness at all levels of field management and operations including recurring monthly training of field operation personnel on various standard and/or emerging environmental matters.
Maintain a current working knowledge of environmental regulations pertinent to oil and gas operations and respective to relevant federal, state and local jurisdictions.
Demonstrated ability to perform field environmental activities which may include compliance inspections, sampling various media, well gauging, GPS surveying, oversight of monitor well installation and remedial activities.
Use of various technologies including FLIR/OGI to evaluate and inspect sites for internal and agency purposes of process improvement and compliance.
Operational knowledge sufficient or demonstrate mechanical aptitude to provide minor maintenance support to operations in support of compliance programs (i.e. air quality, SPCC and storm water) and applicable repair deadlines.
With the support of the Air team, advise production operations and facility engineers on permitting requirements and obligations, emission control options, facility design and air compliance documentation.
Ability to develop and maintain relationships, manage multiple responsibilities, and meet often aggressive project deadlines.
Develop site facility/security diagrams and record equipment inventories to support various compliance programs (ex. air permitting, GHG, SPCC) using a strong knowledge of oil and gas operations and processes.
Support maintenance of a variety of plans, including, but not limited to: SPCC, storm water, waste management and other related compliance plans.
Efficiently input, monitor and trend variety of environmental data to inform and support development of proactive programs of prevention, compliance and operations management;
Support annual implementation of internal audit program to maintain comprehensive compliance of operations within the basin.
Attend industry trade group meetings and participate in industry regulatory efforts.
Demonstrate knowledge and ability to prevent, respond, mitigate and remediate impacts associated with operational spills and leaks including preparation of spill notifications and reports to the applicable agencies.
Assist and support air emission testing, notification and reporting as required by federal and state permits and regulations.
Other duties:
As required to support operations respective to environmental compliance, and
As assigned by the environmental manager.
Bachelor's degree or an advanced degree in environmental science, applied science, engineering or a related technical field preferred. High School Diploma required.
Minimum of 3+ years of related environmental experience, at least 2 years of which is related to oil and gas related environmental experience oil and gas related environmental experience.
Working knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations (NSR, Title V, NSPS, MACT, GHG, etc.).
Capable of performing on-call duties as necessary.
Demonstrated ability to analyze and prepare reports and other related correspondence, both internal and external.
Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills with strong problem-solving abilities.
Demonstrated written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Organized and able to manage multiple concurrent activities and programs timely and with a high degree of accuracy.
Demonstrated abilities with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio) as well as other internal programs as necessary.
Ability to foster cooperation and collaboration with diverse multi-disciplinary teams.

is seeking an Entry Level Environmental Planner
to join our growing Environmental Practice in Mechanicsburg, PA
. This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring a minimum 3 days of onsite office attendance.

delivers integrated environmental planning, permitting, compliance, site assessment, and remediation solutions that support infrastructure and development projects across North America. Our professionals work with clients to navigate complex federal, state, and local environmental regulations while managing risk and protecting natural and built environments. December 2026 graduates are encouraged to apply!

Assisting with the preparation of NEPA documentation, environmental assessments, technical reports, and related project deliverables.

, depending on experience, qualifications, and geographic location.

Incentive compensation for eligible positions.

Our clients choose us for our expertise and prefer us for our nimble approach, creativity, and personal touch. Backed by over a century’s experience, together we’re building a lasting legacy for future generations: stronger communities, a healthier planet, and better lives.

Broadbent & Associates, Inc.
(Broadbent) of Fort Collins, Colorado
is looking to hire an organized full-time Staff Geologist / Staff Environmental Scientist
to work with a wide variety of environmental projects. Our office is located in the heart of Old Town Fort Collins. This staff geologist/scientist position earns a competitive salary
, depending on experience. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package
, including a bonus program, 100% medical insurance premium coverage, dental, vision, a health savings account (HSA), a generous 401(k) retirement plan with safe harbor contribution and company match, vacation, sick leave, ability to earn additional paid time off, disability and life insurance, solid opportunities for advancement, and a friendly and fun work environment in all of our offices
. If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, in the essential environmental remediation and water resource arena, consider applying to Broadbent today!

About Broadbent & Associates, Inc.

Founded in 1987, Broadbent is a full-service environmental remediation, water resource, and civil engineering firm. We provide professional services throughout the United States to the oil and gas industry, mining operations, agricultural companies, municipalities, private industries, governmental agencies, public and private utilities, and developers. Our mission is to build long-term client relationships by providing sound scientific solutions to comprehensive resource management challenges. We're very client-focused with a commitment to providing services in a time-efficient and cost-effective manner.

Broadbent takes care of our customers AND employees like family. Our ability to hire and retain long-term skilled key personnel has significantly contributed to our success. That's why we offer competitive pay
, opportunities for personal growth
, and a great work environment with a sense of camaraderie
.

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A STAFF GEOLOGIST/SCIENTIST

As a Staff Geologist/Scientist, you are the backbone of Broadbent. Your hard work ensures that we deliver for our clients. Under the supervision of a Senior Geologist, you provide support on a range of environmental projects including: Emergency Response, Phase 1 Environmental Site Assessments, soil and groundwater characterization, air sampling, remediation system operation and maintenance, lithologic logging and well construction monitoring, water and wastewater treatment facility monitoring, and water resources activities. You conduct field work to drive project execution and ensure that appropriate health and safety procedures are being followed.

Your people skills are essential as you interact regularly with local clientele and contractors. Though you do spend a lot of time at the job sites and interacting with people, you also make sure to keep up on all your administrative responsibilities. You provide accurate data to our Senior and Associate Scientists and prepare daily reports. Ensuring that clients are happy as well as that all jobs are delivered on-time, within the scope, and on-budget gives you a great sense of accomplishment!

Qualifications For a Staff Geologist / Staff Environmental Scientist

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology or Environmental Science
Zero to two years of environmental-related work experience
Ability to work outdoors, traverse moderate terrain and lift up to 50 pounds
Technical writing competency
Strong technical and computer skills
Self-starter, quick learner and effective communication skills
Ability to work individually and as part of a team
GIS experience a plus

Are you detail-oriented? Do you have strong problem-solving and research skills? Are you organized and able to effectively prioritize multiple tasks? Do you have excellent communication skills? Are you energetic, self-sufficient, and motivated? Are you collaborative and team-oriented? If so, you might just be perfect for this Staff Geologist/Scientist position!

STAFF GEOLOGIST/STAFF ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST WORK SCHEDULE

This full-time Staff Geologist/Scientist position typically works Monday - Friday with some traveling and weekend work. One week sampling assignments once per quarter. Extended deployments for emergency response are possible for up to two to three weeks.

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

About the Team:
The Search team is dedicated to building a fully managed, one-stop platform for information retrieval and analytics. Deeply compatible with Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and Milvus, the platform serves four core scenarios—GenAI applications, search, security, and observability—and provides comprehensive capabilities across full-text search, vector search, geospatial search, and hybrid search. We are also building next-generation Agentic Search products, including RAG, AI-powered search, and multimodal retrieval, continuously pushing the boundaries of intelligent search technology.
We are deeply involved in the open-source ecosystem and have contributed hundreds of PRs across the OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, Lucene, and Milvus communities. Several members of our team hold key leadership roles in these communities, including Governing Board Member, Technical Steering Committee Member, PMC Member, and Maintainer, helping shape the evolution of the broader search and database ecosystem through sustained technical contributions.

On the business side, we not only provide reliable infrastructure for some of ByteDance’s largest-scale vector and full-text hybrid search workloads, but also deliver enterprise-grade cloud search services to external customers through Volcano Engine, helping businesses unlock growth through data. We embrace a pragmatic yet ambitious engineering culture: while continuously publishing innovative research at top-tier conferences such as VLDB and ICDE, we remain strongly focused on real-world impact and commercial adoption, building a comprehensive product portfolio that serves a wide range of search and AI use cases.

Our team brings together leading database researchers and exceptional engineers from around the world. We are looking for talented individuals with expertise in search or vector database engine development, distributed systems architecture, or AI model innovation to join us. Together, we will explore uncharted technical territory, define the data foundation for the AI era, and empower both ByteDance and enterprises across industries to achieve AI-driven transformation.

Responsibilities
- Develop and evolve our Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and Milvus products, building high-performance and scalable search and vector retrieval capabilities.
- Develop high-performance full-text and vector search, including hybrid search, filtered search, multi-vector search, and large-scale ANN retrieval.
- Optimize vector indexing and distributed retrieval across HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, RaBitQ, storage, caching, and I/O.
- Explore cloud-native Vector Lakebase architectures for scalable search over data lakes and object storage.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications
- B.S in Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, or a related field.
- Strong software engineering skills in C++, Golang, Java, or Python.
- Experience with search engines, databases, storage systems, or distributed systems.
- Hands-on experience with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch or Milvus in production or system development.
- Strong understanding of distributed systems and performance optimization.

Preferred Qualifications
- Deep experience with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Lucene, Milvus/Knowhere, or similar systems.
- Strong knowledge of full-text search and (multi)-vector indexing, including HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, or related ANN algorithms.
- Experience optimizing billion-scale or larger vector retrieval for latency, throughput, recall, and cost.
- Experience with cloud-native storage, compute-storage separation, object storage, or lakehouse/lakebase architectures.

Founded in 2012, ByteDance's mission is to inspire creativity and enrich life. With a suite of more than a dozen products, including TikTok, Lemon8, CapCut and Pico as well as platforms specific to the China market, including Toutiao, Douyin, and Xigua, ByteDance has made it easier and more fun for people to connect with, consume, and create content.​

Why Join ByteDance

Inspiring creativity is at the core of ByteDance's mission. Our innovative products are built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and enrich life - a mission we work towards every day.​
As ByteDancers, we strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our Company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​
Diversity & Inclusion​
ByteDance is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At ByteDance, our mission is to inspire creativity and enrich life. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.​

Reasonable Accommodation

ByteDance is committed to providing reasonable accommodations in our recruitment processes for candidates with disabilities, pregnancy, sincerely held religious beliefs or other reasons protected by applicable laws. If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation, please reach out to us at https://tinyurl.com/RA-request​

Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and experience, and location.
