jobs.title: Environmental Advisor
jobs.description:
About The West Region Delivery Team

The West Region Delivery Team consortium comprises Abergeldie Complex Infrastructure and Fulton Hogan for construction, Programmed for maintenance and facility management, and Stantec and Atlas for design and engineering.

The West Region Delivery Team is integrated with Sydney Water under a collaborative contracting framework, Partnering for Success (P4S). The West Region Delivery Team has been engaged to deliver design, construction, maintenance and facility management services for a ten (10) year program across Sydney Water's wastewater, water and recycled water systems.

About The Opportunity

We are seeking an Environmental Advisor to join the West Region Delivery Team, supporting the delivery of a diverse portfolio of water and wastewater infrastructure projects for Sydney Water.

Supporting multiple construction projects across the program, you will provide environmental advice, identify and manage risks, implement controls and help ensure compliance throughout project delivery. Working closely with operational and project teams, you will help drive environmental performance and best practice across active construction sites.

Key Responsibilities Include

Providing day-to-day environmental support and guidance to project delivery teams.
Conducting environmental inspections, audits and compliance assessments across construction sites.
Monitoring and reporting on compliance with environmental management plans, approvals, permits and legislative requirements.
Supporting the implementation and maintenance of erosion and sediment controls
Assisting with environmental risk assessments and identifying opportunities to improve environmental performance.
Investigating environmental incidents, non-conformances and complaints, and supporting corrective actions.
Preparing environmental reports, monitoring records and project compliance documentation.
Delivering environmental awareness training and guidance to project personnel and subcontractors.
Liaising with clients, regulators and key stakeholders on environmental matters.
Supporting the development and continuous improvement of environmental management processes and systems.

What You'll Bring To The Team

Tertiary qualifications Environmental Science/Environmental Engineering or a related discipline.
A minimum of 3 years' experience in an Environmental Advisor or similar role within civil infrastructure construction.
Experience working on linear infrastructure projects such as water, wastewater, roads, rail, utilities or similar construction environments.
Sound knowledge of environmental legislation, regulatory requirements and environmental management systems.
Practical experience with erosion and sediment control planning, implementation and monitoring, including a strong understanding of Blue Book requirements.
Strong report writing skills and the ability to prepare clear, accurate and concise environmental documentation.
Experience conducting environmental inspections, audits, incident investigations and compliance assessments.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build effective working relationships across site teams.

Why You Should Work With Us

Our people are what make Abergeldie successful, and we make sure that this is the kind of place where great people enjoy working for the long term. We have a range of employee benefits, including the Abergeldie Bonus Scheme, where all eligible employees share in the benefits of the projects they have helped to deliver. When we deliver winning projects, we celebrate success together.

Interested?

If this sounds like you, apply now or reach out to Dee Paton ([email protected]) for more information.

jobs.title: Spatial Analyst
jobs.description:
Accent Environmental is a Melbourne-based environmental consultancy of specialists working on environmental impact assessments, landscape and visual impact assessments, and approvals for renewables, mining and other major projects across Australia and internationally. Accent places a strong emphasis on clear visual communication to complement and enhance our high quality written reports.

We're looking for a Spatial Analyst to join our team and help deliver spatial analysis, GIS and visual communication across our project work - producing the spatial and visual information and figures that go into our technical reports and building your skills across a range of different projects and sectors. You'll work closely with our Lead Spatial Analyst, who is focused on the high quality delivery of our spatial work and the expansion of our capabilities. You'll be part of an evolving practice, picking up and helping develop new tools, methods and analytical approaches.

What you'll be doing
Sourcing and quality-checking spatial data across our projects - satellite imagery, cadastral data, environmental datasets, and client-supplied files
Producing maps, figures, and spatial analysis for environmental and social impact assessments, landscape and visual impact assessments, including in the renewables and mining sectors
Assisting with spatial modelling and analysis - constraints mapping, viewshed and visual impact analysis, site suitability
Helping build and maintain our GIS workflows, spatial databases, and mapping templates
Supporting both senior and junior staff as they build their GIS knowledge and skills
Contributing spatial input to proposals and tenders

What we're after

jobs.description:
About The Opportunity

SWCA Environmental Consultants is seeking an Associate Project Restoration Engineer
with a passion for ecosystem restoration and water resource engineering. This role will focus on advancing our ecological restoration practice in North Carolina and the Southeast, while also supporting projects across the U.S. Reporting into SWCA’s Charlotte, North Carolina, this position offers flexibility to work hybrid within the Charlotte Metro area, or be fully remote (distributed) within the SW USA. The ideal candidate will have experience in stream, wetland, and coastal/living shoreline design, with strong skills in applied hydraulics, hydrology, and geomorphology, as well as proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D and hydrology/hydraulic modeling.Responsibilities will include occasional travel to project sites for field assessments, data collection, and client meetings. This is a full-time, regular (with full benefits), salaried, exempt position.

Individuals with an EIT and are working toward a PE license are also highly encouraged to apply.

Application Deadline
: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews may be scheduled as qualified candidates are identified. This position may close without prior notice once a strong candidate pool is established.

About SWCA

SWCA Environmental Consultants is a 100% employee-owned environmental consulting firm providing full spectrum environmental services across the United States. Our North Star is to be the best place to work and a leader in sustainability, delivering sound science and creative solutions to complex environmental challenges.

We are guided by our core values every day. We collaborate as #OneSWCA, we are #AlwaysLearning, we #NeverSettle, and we #GiveBack to our communities. With offices nationwide, SWCA offers a collaborative, team focused environment where employees can build meaningful and long-term careers.

What you will accomplish

Leads management activities by overseeing technical tasks, schedules, budgets, and deliverables to ensure successful completion of assigned projects. Manages various aspects of project execution, including client communication, team coordination, and quality assurance. Responsible for preparation of design reports and plans that make up elements of design deliverable packages.
Develops engineering designs for assigned projects, including stream and wetland restoration, living shorelines, and nature-based infrastructure. Applies advanced technical expertise to refine designs and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.
Conducts field investigations and detailed analyses for assigned restoration projects, ensuring designs minimize environmental impacts while meeting project requirements. Provides technical guidance to optimize solutions.
Prepares comprehensive construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents to guide project implementation. Ensures all documentation adheres to industry and regulatory standards. Supports quality assurance reviews for analyses and deliverables.
Oversees permitting processes by preparing regulatory documentation for reviews and approvals. Collaborates with agencies to address compliance requirements.
Performs modeling and calculations to support design optimization and assess environmental impacts. Uses modeling tools to simulate project conditions and optimize solutions.
Coordinates with multidisciplinary teams to integrate environmental science and engineering principles into project designs. Facilitates collaboration among scientists, planners, and engineers to achieve project objectives.
Provides construction-phase services by monitoring progress, ensuring adherence to specifications, and addressing on-site challenges. Communicates with contractors to resolve issues and maintain project quality.
Engages with clients and stakeholders to communicate project goals, progress, and outcomes. Builds and maintains relationships to support business development and client satisfaction.
Mentors junior staff by providing technical guidance, training, reviewing work products, and fostering professional growth. Encourages knowledge sharing and collaboration within the team.
Follows applicable federal, Tribal, state, local, industry, contractual, and company regulations, standards, and specifications.
Performs related work as assigned.

Additional Job-Specific Responsibilities

Develop construction plans within AutoCAD Civil 3D. Typically restoration plans but occasional site civil support may be required.
Perform hydraulic, hydrologic, and water quality assessments, modeling, and analysis in support of the above listed projects.
Communicate and work with project managers to keep projects on schedule and on budget.
Attend and participate in annual internal design training meetings to support personal-skills growth and career planning.
Work independently and multi-task regularly in a fast-paced environment; work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
Take responsibility for team safety, develop safety plans (when applicable), and anticipate potential safety hazards.

Minimum Qualifications

Four years of relevant, progressively responsible experience. Six years of related experience is preferred; or any equivalent combination of experience, performance, training, and/or education. Knowledge normally obtained through a bachelor's degree and active Professional Engineer (PE) license required.

Experience And Qualifications For Success

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Agricultural, Biological, Civil, Environmental, or Coastal Engineering)
EI certification (Engineering Intern)
Ability to travel on short-term overnight efforts to collect field data and meet with clients, up to 25% of the time.
Experience with HEC-RAS and other hydraulic and hydrologic modeling and analysis software.
Experience developing ecological restoration design construction plans in AutoCAD Civil 3D.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing primary tasks and small to medium sized projects with limited oversight.
Experience mentoring and successfully delegating tasks to junior team members.
Experience with urban stream restoration projects
Experience with mitigation banking projects

Other Job Conditions

This position may require domestic travel, including travel by commercial airline. Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain all valid travel documents and identification required for work-related travel throughout the duration of employment.

Pay Range

SWCA is committed to salary equity and transparency. The expected pay range for this Charlotte, NC based position is $82,347 to $105,716 per year. Actual pay may vary based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other factors permitted by law. Eligible employees may also receive performance-based bonuses.

As a 100% employee owned company, we invest in your future. Our Total Rewards package includes an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, 401(k) with profit sharing, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, wellness programs, and professional development opportunities.

Closing

If you need accommodation due to a disability, please contact accommodations@swca.com or call 1 480 581 5378. If you require assistance with the application process, please contact recruiting@swca.com.

SWCA may use approved technology, including AI-assisted tools, to support parts of the application and recruiting process. All selection and hiring decisions are made by SWCA employees, and candidates are not selected or rejected by automated systems. We are committed to a fair, transparent, and human-centered hiring experience.

Candidates may use AI tools to help prepare application materials and interviews. However, all application materials, assessments, and interview responses must accurately reflect their own experience, skills, and qualifications. AI must not be used to fabricate experience, complete assessments on their behalf, or otherwise misrepresent their background or abilities.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We recognize the valuable skills and experiences our internal team members bring to SWCA’s continued success. Qualified internal candidates are encouraged to apply and will be seriously considered for this position. Job Description

The GE Vernova Environmental & Properties Risk team in the GE Vernova Supply Chain Development organization provides strategic and technical support to manage environmental risk across the GE Vernova global footprint. As a member of this team, this Senior Project Manager will serve as a lead project manager for a portion of GE Vernova’s portfolio of remedial projects. In addition, this Senior Project Manager will serve a key support role for the assessment and mitigation of environmental risk in transactions – including mergers & acquisitions, real estate and restructuring activities – and strategic initiatives. This Senior Project Manager will work closely with team members from Environmental & Properties Risk, real estate, sourcing, special projects, strategy, finance, legal, EHS, governmental affairs, communications, operations, and facilities to provide technical leadership and coordination.

Job available in multiple locations

Remote, United States of America
Remote, Brazil
Remote, Mexico

Job Description

What you’ll do

In serving as a Senior Project Manager within the Environmental & Properties Risk team you will be responsible for managing the investigation and remediation of a portion of GE Vernova’s portfolio of remedial projects through the management of external consultants and coordination with key internal stakeholders. This role will be responsible for coordinating all aspects of the assigned remedial project execution, from initial risk review and project planning to final completion, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, safety standards, and budget constraints. These responsibilities include technical delivery, schedule management, fiscal management, serving as an internal and external stakeholder liaison, reporting requirements, and coordination with project team members. In addition, this Senior Project Manager will provide technical support for other critical functions within the Environmental & Properties Risk group such as M&A, real estate and restructuring activities.

Qualifications

General Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited University or College in environmental science, geology, engineering, biology, chemistry, or equivalent discipline.
Solid proven applied experience in project management experience in environmental, remediation, environmental transactions and/or EHS within a company, regulatory agency and/or consulting firm.
Minimum of:
Solid proven experience managing complex remediation projects involving soil, groundwater and soil vapor issues, including experience with PCBs, hydrocarbons, and chlorinated solvents; and/or
Solid proven experience in providing environmental transactional support for real estate and/or M&A transactions including:
Expert familiarity with ASTM standards and processes for assessing risk via Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments.
Demonstrated experience preparing/using Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments to assess risks; and
Experience coordinating environmental due diligence efforts for multiple, simultaneous, large, and/or complex transactions.

Ability to understand materiality, risks and trade-offs relative to other considerations.
Understanding of legal requirements, regulatory environment, environmental risk, reputational considerations, local issues, etc.
Provide strategic oversight, direction and communication including planning, progress, and financial updates to management on projects.
Proven ability to manage and coordinate consultant teams to generate project cost estimates, scopes of work, proposals, and reports.
Experience preparing financial estimations and planning necessary for long-term projects.
General familiarity relevant environmental issues and considerations related to historical and current manufacturing and energy operations.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication and presentation (oral/written) skills; public presentations both in person and virtual are an essential part of job function.
Demonstrated collaboration skills within diverse teams.
Ability to clearly communicate complex technical information in an easy-to-understand manner.
Demonstrated success in coordinating technical, financial, reputational and legal considerations for complex projects.
Strong technical and analytical aptitude to understand and articulate complicated trade-offs.
Experience working with sensitive and confidential information.
Experience working cross-culturally in large, matrixed organizations and ability to navigate geographies, cultures, relationships, etc.
Ability and willingness to travel including internationally (~30% travel).
Proficiency with MS Office Programs including Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
English proficiency and a minimum of business fluency in at least one of the following languages: Spanish or Portuguese.

Qualifications That Will Make You Stand Out

Graduate degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, biology, chemistry, business or relevant related discipline.
Highly collaborative person with outstanding communication skills.
Strategic and flexible thinker who uses a 360 degree perspective to assess risks.
Ability to problem-solve creatively, to be flexible and think outside the box.
Ability to see big picture while not losing sight of critical details.
Ability to be flexible, follow tight deadlines, and deliver results quickly.
Ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Demonstrated project management skills including project initiation, scoping, resorting, scheduling, budgeting, risk management and communication.
Great energy and enthusiasm for position and environmental risk management.
Fluency or familiarity with additional prominent language(s) such as Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Mandarin, or Vietnamese.
Familiarity with LEAN principals.

GE Vernova employees rise to the challenge of building a world that works. In order to meet this mission, we provide varied, competitive benefits to help support our workforce: Our Culture | GE Vernova (gecareers.com)

Inclusion & Diversity

Water Quality & Remote Sensing Research Scientist

ARC CREST

NASA Ames Research Center / CSUMB Dept of Applied Environmental Science

Job Announcement

Priority Screening Deadline: October 5, 2026. All positions are open until filled.

This position is dependent upon grant funds. Subject to annual NASA review

Position December 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027.

SALARY

–

Position Summary

Under the general direction of the Principal Investigator under the NASA ARC-CREST Cooperative Agreement, the Research Scientist is responsible for conducting scientific research, publishing scientific papers, and developing proposals for new research activities. Additionally, the Research Scientist will serve as a water quality and remote sensing subject matter expert and contribute to NASA capacity building efforts with the Applied Remote Sensing Training (ARSET) program.

The main objectives of this research are validation and advancement of satellite-based water quality and cyanobacterial harmful algal bloom monitoring tools that utilize NASA Earth observation data including hyperspectral imagery. Work under this position includes in situ water quality and optical data collection for remote sensing validation, image processing, atmospheric correction, data analysis, and water quality solutions development.

The candidate will need to be capable of both working independently and collaborating within a team environment on tasks performed across a spectrum of disciplines. The candidate needs to have excellent writing and oral presentation skills. This position will work closely with scientists at NASA Ames Research Center. The successful candidate will have the opportunity and support to develop and lead innovative research on remote sensing of water quality.

Examples of Duties

Key Responsibilities

–

Assist In All Portions Of Content Creation And Delivery Of Online NASA ARSET Trainings For The Water Quality Applications Area Including

–

Conduct background research for training topics.

–

Create and review training presentations.

–

Assist with content creation for training promotion in collaboration with the ARSET communications lead.

–

Assist with participant questions via email and during the training sessions.

–

Contribute to creation of post-training surveys and review of results.

–

Conduct research on application of NASA Earth observations to water quality solutions.

–

Complete water quality and remote sensing validation field work on inland waters.

–

Analyze complex spatial and temporal water quality datasets.

–

Present research results and scientific meetings and to partners and stakeholders at workshops and meetings.

–

Author peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts, research and technical reports, and research proposals.

–

Foster and maintain collaborative links with federal, state, and local agencies in addition to local groups and individuals, research organizations, and the public.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education And Experience

–

Doctoral degree or the equivalent in Civil and Environmental Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Hydrology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.

–

Previous Experience With The Following

–

Publication of scientific manuscripts

–

Conducting research or applied science projects with NASA EO data

–

Development of research projects and proposals

–

jobs.title: Geospatial Web Developer
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Geospatial Web Developer provides web application development expertise to support TNC’s diverse and geographically distributed conservation science and marketing communities.

The Geospatial Web Developer will support and develop web GIS applications and solutions according to system requirements following TNC methodologies and best practices. In supporting existing applications and advising professionals across our global organization, they will also play a key role in shaping web application guidelines as we strive for a more consistent approach to web map and application delivery across teams and platforms. While we extensively use Esri tools and technologies, we also use and support other platforms and technologies, including open-source geospatial software.

The Geospatial Web Developer is a member of the Conservation Application Development team but will work with other functional teams in the Conservation & Geospatial Systems group within Information Technology (IT), and with other TNC business units in a variety of development and design roles. The Web Developer will help in creating and maintaining web mapping applications and visualization tools focused on supporting our goal to conserve 4 billion hectares of Earth’s oceans, 650 million hectares of land, 30 million hectares of lakes and wetlands, and 1 million kilometers of river systems. The Geospatial Web Developer will spend approximately 75% of their time designing, developing and maintaining applications and infrastructure, including working with product owners to refine requirements and related tasks, and approximately 25% of their time providing guidance and support to others developing web mapping applications.

This is a fully remote position where the chosen candidate can work anywhere TNC is registered to work with preference to candidates who can serve Eastern and Pacific time zones.

This position is not eligible for relocation, or visa .

Responsibilities & Scope

Analyze and document end-user and technology-user business requirements for technology projects with wide range of complexity at varying levels of impact on organization-wide initiatives.
Design and develop new, complex technology systems and solutions according to system requirements following TNC methodology and development best practices.
Act as lead technologist on technology application maintenance projects related to application upgrades, conversions, and modifications. Perform tasks assigned as required to complete project including design, development, running specific programs, generating reports, and analyzing results.
Provide support for production problems as assigned.
Act as quality assurance analyst to conduct peer reviews and validate programmer analyst work done for moderately complex systems before their release to production in all phases of the project life cycle.
Act as Project or Technical Lead as assigned. Develop accurate project plans with realistic estimations and provide technical expertise to team members and users to help resolve complex project-related problems.
Learn continuously and seek opportunities to grow as a developer.

We’re Looking For You

Are you a Geospatial Web Developer looking for a new challenge and an opportunity to advance your skills and career in a global conservation organization? If you are a detail-oriented, responsible team player passionate about conservation and technology and understand the state of the art in web application delivery, then you are the type of person we are looking for! We are looking for a talented Web Developer with strong customer service skills who understands the intersection of conservation, GIS, and application development to join our collaborative, fun, and rewarding team of professionals supporting conservation and geospatial innovation across our global organization. Come join our team and be a part of an organization that creates innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that people and nature can thrive together.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor's degree in computer science, or a related field and three years of experience in programming and systems design OR an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Three years’ progressive experience with frontend web development (JS/TypeScript, HTML, CSS).
Experience with UI/UX, web design and usability principles in application development.
Experience with web mapping APIs (ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript, Mapbox, Leaflet), or other relevant geospatial experience.
Experience with component-based frontend frameworks and libraries (e.g., Vue, Angular, React).
Experience with source control and code repositories (e.g., Bitbucket, Github).
Experience analyzing complex, system-wide technical specifications, debugging applications, and producing effective user and technical documentation.

Desired Qualifications

Ability to work on projects independently and with a team of developers.
Experience using AI coding assistants for accelerating development tasks.
Experience in both cartographic and graphic design, including mapping and charting libraries (e.g., Chart.js, amCharts, D3).
Experience with ArcGIS Online (AGO) tools and platforms (e.g., Experience Builder, AGO dashboards).
Backend development experience (experience with .NET/C# is a plus).
Knowledge of database management systems (e.g., Esri’s File Geodatabase, PostgresSQL/PostGIS, AWS RDS, AWS Aurora, Microsoft SQL Server, or MySQL).
Knowledge of and experience with cloud computing services (AWS preferred).
Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) and deployment pipelines.
Experience with app containerization (e.g., Docker).
Leadership skills and an ability to coordinate application delivery and best practices across different organizational units.
Strong interest or a background in natural sciences and conservation.
Strong time management skills and the ability to prioritize multiple competing demands.
Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience are appreciated, including experience with web maps supporting different languages.

Salary Information

This position may be based in any country where TNC has an established entity, taking into consideration legal restrictions, such as non-national ratios and immigration processing times. For U.S. based applicants only, the starting pay range for this position is generally within the range of $80,840.00 – $128,700.00
for annual base salary and is based on location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. For all other applicants, pay ranges will be in local currency, the pay range will be based on the local labor market, and not tied to the above pay range. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment and used to determine your actual pay range.
Additionally, for all applicants, actual pay will fall within a range based on a variety of factors including, for example, the candidate’s qualifications, specific skills, and experience.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

jobs.title: Director, Remote Sensing
jobs.description:
WGI is seeking a Director, Remote Sensing
to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. This position is responsible for the people, technology, equipment, processes, and quality systems necessary to successfully execute WGI's airborne remote sensing programs while engaging with leadership of our other Departments.

The Director, Remote Sensing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the Remote Sensing Department. This individual is accountable for departmental performance, staff development, resource planning, technology and equipment strategy, quality, production capacity, and successful project delivery. The Director will maintain sufficient technical expertise to provide oversight, evaluate risk, support complex project decisions, and ensure appropriate technical leadership is available throughout the project lifecycle.

This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team of sensor operators, LiDAR analysts, imagery and photogrammetric professionals, and other geospatial technical staff while coordinating closely with project managers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other WGI disciplines. The Director will be responsible for developing scalable production processes, maintaining high standards for quality and consistency, optimizing staff and equipment utilization, and ensuring that WGI remains at the forefront of remote sensing technology.

This is an in-office leadership position
with travel required to support operations, projects, staff, clients, business development, and field activities.

At WGI, you will find talented, passionate associates providing exceptional service in collaborative, team-driven environments, all while having fun and enjoying the work they do. We work to stay ahead of the curve by investing in the latest tools and technology. As one of the nation’s top consulting firms, we consistently strive to promote efficiency, cultivate a culture our associates can proudly embrace, and empower our associates to advance their career growth at WGI and beyond.

WGI is always looking for remarkable individuals to join our team and help us grow in our vision. If you think you are an innovative, self-motivated team player, and want to shape your community, join our WGI team today!

WGI offers a complete Benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, LTD & STD, Life Insurance, 401k with match, PTO, Holidays, HSA with company contribution, Pet insurance, and Employee Assistance Program.

Operational Leadership: Lead the operations of WGI's Remote Sensing Department, including staffing, production capacity, equipment, resource allocation, workload balancing, project performance, and operational priorities. Establish scalable processes, accountability, and performance measures that support consistent, predictable, and profitable project delivery.
Maintain visibility into backlog, production capacity, staffing availability, equipment utilization, and upcoming project demand to proactively identify resource constraints and develop appropriate staffing, subcontracting, scheduling, or technology solutions.

Airborne Acquisition Operations: Provide operational oversight of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition programs. Ensure qualified technical personnel, appropriate equipment, documented procedures, quality controls, and adequate resources are in place to support safe, efficient, and successful acquisition.
LiDAR & Imagery Production: Provide leadership and technical oversight for WGI's airborne, mobile, terrestrial, and UAS LiDAR and imagery production capabilities. Ensure production teams have effective workflows, appropriate technical leadership, adequate resources, and clearly defined quality standards from initial processing through final delivery.
Quality Management: Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive QA/QC procedures throughout the acquisition and production lifecycle. Establish measurable checkpoints for collection completeness, trajectory quality, relative and absolute accuracy, point density, imagery quality, calibration, classification, data integrity, metadata, and final deliverables. Perform quarterly audits to ensure Project Manager’s compliance to WGI’s established Quality Assurance Program.
Technical Leadership: Maintain strong working knowledge of Remote Sensing technologies, methodologies, specifications, and industry standards. Provide technical oversight for complex projects, support technical decision-making, and ensure appropriate subject-matter experts are engaged to resolve specialized technical issues. Develop and empower technical leaders within the department rather than creating dependency on a single technical resource.
Project Delivery: Maintain visibility across active Remote Sensing projects and proactively address schedule, staffing, technical, equipment, or quality issues that could affect successful delivery. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.
People Leadership: Lead, mentor, develop, and evaluate Remote Sensing staff and technical leaders. Establish clear expectations, accountability, career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities. Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.
Equipment & Technology Management: Oversee the effective deployment, maintenance, calibration, and lifecycle planning of remote sensing sensors, GNSS/IMU systems, computing infrastructure, storage, and supporting equipment. Participate in evaluation and justification of significant technology and capital investments.
Automation & Process Improvement: Promote automation, batch processing, scripting, and standardized production workflows to improve quality, repeatability, throughput, and cost efficiency. Identify production bottlenecks and implement measurable improvements.
Technical Risk & Issue Resolution: Ensure complex technical, equipment, software, processing, and data-quality issues are appropriately escalated, investigated, and resolved. Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.
Financial & Resource Management: Assist with the development of department budgets, staffing plans, capital expenditures, equipment utilization, project performance, and resource forecasting. Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.
Business Development & Client Support: Support WGI's business development activities through technical presentations, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, project approaches, and client meetings. Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.
Innovation: Evaluate emerging LiDAR, imagery, UAS, positioning, cloud-computing, AI/ML, and geospatial technologies. Recommend technologies and investments that improve WGI's capabilities, productivity, quality, or competitive position.
Safety & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture across airborne, vehicle-based, UAS, and field operations. Ensure departmental activities comply with WGI policies, applicable regulations, aviation requirements, client requirements, professional standards, and established operating procedures.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Surveying, GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline preferred; advanced degree a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.
Data: Management of large point-cloud and imagery datasets, high-performance processing environments, network/cloud storage, metadata, archival and data-transfer workflows.

Preferred Licenses & Certifications

Professional credentials should be considered favorably and may be factored into position level and compensation, including:

ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist (CP)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Scientist - LiDAR (CMS-LiDAR)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Technician - LiDAR (CMT-LiDAR)
Professional Surveyor/Professional Land Surveyor licensure
Surveyor Intern/LSIT certification
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
Other relevant geospatial, photogrammetric, aviation, project-management, or technical certifications

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. We are unable to sponsor or take over the sponsorship of employment visas.

If you have what it takes to join our growing organization and want to be part of a dedicated team, please apply today. In return, WGI provides a competitive salary and an outstanding work environment. WGI is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled.

jobs.title: Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Full-Time Experienced Environmental Engineer
, to join our Site Investigation & Remediation (SIR) team in Asheville, North Carolina.

Our Carolinas team offers a collaborative, close-knit culture backed by the resources of a national platform. You’ll work alongside a multidisciplinary group of engineers, geologists, scientists, and technical specialists committed to delivering high-quality, technically sound solutions.

This is a hybrid role based in Asheville, with regular in-office presence expected to support team collaboration and client engagement.

In this role you will have the opportunity to provide project assistance and guidance on multi- phase environmental work processes, including but not limited to: site investigation, remediation, developing corrective action strategies, managing aspects of brownfields redevelopment projects (i.e., vapor intrusion mitigation and environmental management plans), environmental permitting, and assisting with recommendations to avert degradation of air, water, and land resources. Responsible for ensuring projects are delivered with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.

Your Impact

Develop environmental site investigation and remediation strategies for a diverse client base (federal, municipal, commercial, industrial) and projects from various regulatory programs (Superfund, Brownfields, Voluntary Cleanup, etc.)
Develop technical scopes of work, schedules, and cost estimates for site investigation and remediation activities, based on applicable regulations and client objectives.
Lead multi-media investigations that may include subsurface boring and trenching oversight, groundwater monitoring and injection/recovery well installations, aquifer testing, multi-media sampling, and field mapping.
Conduct analysis, evaluation, and interpretation of geologic, hydrogeologic, and analytical data obtained during field investigations.
Evaluate remedial performance and direct appropriate O&M and system optimization activities.
Prepare a variety of technical reports: remedial alternative evaluations, feasibility studies, pilot test work plans, remedial design, contractor specifications & bid documents, remedial performance evaluation, pre-design investigation, etc.
Interact with regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and clients in a confident and professional manner.
Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurements, statistical analysis, and reporting.
Prepare and implement site-specific Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs) and Health and Safety Plans (HASPs).
Remain current in latest environmental engineering techniques and emerging contaminants of concern.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP's Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental or Civil Engineering, or closely related discipline.
3 to 5 years of relevant post education experience in environmental engineering.
Engineer in Training Certification (North Carolina preferred or ability to obtain).
Knowledge of engineering principles, practices, and methods and their application to environmental and project work-related issues.
Ability to coordinate with agency regulators and understand requirements.
Knowledge with the concepts of reducing and eliminating the use or generation of hazardous substances, processes, or products., and mitigation programs.
Knowledge of the techniques used in identifying, measuring, sampling and studying environmental control.
Knowledge of relevant environmental laws, regulations, compliance practices, and record-keeping requirements.
Familiarity with North Carolina NPDES permitting and SPCC planning and reporting.
Capable interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
Effective self-leadership with attention to detail, results orientation, and managing multiple priorities in a dynamic work environment.

jobs.title: Director, Remote Sensing
jobs.description:
WGI is seeking a Director, Remote Sensing
to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. This position is responsible for the people, technology, equipment, processes, and quality systems necessary to successfully execute WGI's airborne remote sensing programs while engaging with leadership of our other Departments.

The Director, Remote Sensing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the Remote Sensing Department. This individual is accountable for departmental performance, staff development, resource planning, technology and equipment strategy, quality, production capacity, and successful project delivery. The Director will maintain sufficient technical expertise to provide oversight, evaluate risk, support complex project decisions, and ensure appropriate technical leadership is available throughout the project lifecycle.

This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team of sensor operators, LiDAR analysts, imagery and photogrammetric professionals, and other geospatial technical staff while coordinating closely with project managers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other WGI disciplines. The Director will be responsible for developing scalable production processes, maintaining high standards for quality and consistency, optimizing staff and equipment utilization, and ensuring that WGI remains at the forefront of remote sensing technology.

This is an in-office leadership position
with travel required to support operations, projects, staff, clients, business development, and field activities.

At WGI, you will find talented, passionate associates providing exceptional service in collaborative, team-driven environments, all while having fun and enjoying the work they do. We work to stay ahead of the curve by investing in the latest tools and technology. As one of the nation’s top consulting firms, we consistently strive to promote efficiency, cultivate a culture our associates can proudly embrace, and empower our associates to advance their career growth at WGI and beyond.

WGI is always looking for remarkable individuals to join our team and help us grow in our vision. If you think you are an innovative, self-motivated team player, and want to shape your community, join our WGI team today!

WGI offers a complete Benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, LTD & STD, Life Insurance, 401k with match, PTO, Holidays, HSA with company contribution, Pet insurance, and Employee Assistance Program.

Compensation Range:
$175,000 - $200,000

Operational Leadership: Lead the operations of WGI's Remote Sensing Department, including staffing, production capacity, equipment, resource allocation, workload balancing, project performance, and operational priorities. Establish scalable processes, accountability, and performance measures that support consistent, predictable, and profitable project delivery.
Maintain visibility into backlog, production capacity, staffing availability, equipment utilization, and upcoming project demand to proactively identify resource constraints and develop appropriate staffing, subcontracting, scheduling, or technology solutions.

Airborne Acquisition Operations: Provide operational oversight of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition programs. Ensure qualified technical personnel, appropriate equipment, documented procedures, quality controls, and adequate resources are in place to support safe, efficient, and successful acquisition.
LiDAR & Imagery Production: Provide leadership and technical oversight for WGI's airborne, mobile, terrestrial, and UAS LiDAR and imagery production capabilities. Ensure production teams have effective workflows, appropriate technical leadership, adequate resources, and clearly defined quality standards from initial processing through final delivery.
Quality Management: Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive QA/QC procedures throughout the acquisition and production lifecycle. Establish measurable checkpoints for collection completeness, trajectory quality, relative and absolute accuracy, point density, imagery quality, calibration, classification, data integrity, metadata, and final deliverables. Perform quarterly audits to ensure Project Manager’s compliance to WGI’s established Quality Assurance Program.
Technical Leadership: Maintain strong working knowledge of Remote Sensing technologies, methodologies, specifications, and industry standards. Provide technical oversight for complex projects, support technical decision-making, and ensure appropriate subject-matter experts are engaged to resolve specialized technical issues. Develop and empower technical leaders within the department rather than creating dependency on a single technical resource.
Project Delivery: Maintain visibility across active Remote Sensing projects and proactively address schedule, staffing, technical, equipment, or quality issues that could affect successful delivery. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.
People Leadership: Lead, mentor, develop, and evaluate Remote Sensing staff and technical leaders. Establish clear expectations, accountability, career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities. Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.
Equipment & Technology Management: Oversee the effective deployment, maintenance, calibration, and lifecycle planning of remote sensing sensors, GNSS/IMU systems, computing infrastructure, storage, and supporting equipment. Participate in evaluation and justification of significant technology and capital investments.
Automation & Process Improvement: Promote automation, batch processing, scripting, and standardized production workflows to improve quality, repeatability, throughput, and cost efficiency. Identify production bottlenecks and implement measurable improvements.
Technical Risk & Issue Resolution: Ensure complex technical, equipment, software, processing, and data-quality issues are appropriately escalated, investigated, and resolved. Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.
Financial & Resource Management: Assist with the development of department budgets, staffing plans, capital expenditures, equipment utilization, project performance, and resource forecasting. Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.
Business Development & Client Support: Support WGI's business development activities through technical presentations, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, project approaches, and client meetings. Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.
Innovation: Evaluate emerging LiDAR, imagery, UAS, positioning, cloud-computing, AI/ML, and geospatial technologies. Recommend technologies and investments that improve WGI's capabilities, productivity, quality, or competitive position.
Safety & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture across airborne, vehicle-based, UAS, and field operations. Ensure departmental activities comply with WGI policies, applicable regulations, aviation requirements, client requirements, professional standards, and established operating procedures.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Surveying, GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline preferred; advanced degree a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.
Data: Management of large point-cloud and imagery datasets, high-performance processing environments, network/cloud storage, metadata, archival and data-transfer workflows.

Preferred Licenses & Certifications

Professional credentials should be considered favorably and may be factored into position level and compensation, including:

ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist (CP)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Scientist - LiDAR (CMS-LiDAR)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Technician - LiDAR (CMT-LiDAR)
Professional Surveyor/Professional Land Surveyor licensure
Surveyor Intern/LSIT certification
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
Other relevant geospatial, photogrammetric, aviation, project-management, or technical certifications

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. We are unable to sponsor or take over the sponsorship of employment visas.

If you have what it takes to join our growing organization and want to be part of a dedicated team, please apply today. In return, WGI provides a competitive salary and an outstanding work environment. WGI is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled

jobs.title: Director, Remote Sensing
jobs.description:
WGI is seeking a Director, Remote Sensing
to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. This position is responsible for the people, technology, equipment, processes, and quality systems necessary to successfully execute WGI's airborne remote sensing programs while engaging with leadership of our other Departments.

The Director, Remote Sensing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the Remote Sensing Department. This individual is accountable for departmental performance, staff development, resource planning, technology and equipment strategy, quality, production capacity, and successful project delivery. The Director will maintain sufficient technical expertise to provide oversight, evaluate risk, support complex project decisions, and ensure appropriate technical leadership is available throughout the project lifecycle.

This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team of sensor operators, LiDAR analysts, imagery and photogrammetric professionals, and other geospatial technical staff while coordinating closely with project managers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other WGI disciplines. The Director will be responsible for developing scalable production processes, maintaining high standards for quality and consistency, optimizing staff and equipment utilization, and ensuring that WGI remains at the forefront of remote sensing technology.

This is an in-office leadership position
with travel required to support operations, projects, staff, clients, business development, and field activities.

At WGI, you will find talented, passionate associates providing exceptional service in collaborative, team-driven environments, all while having fun and enjoying the work they do. We work to stay ahead of the curve by investing in the latest tools and technology. As one of the nation’s top consulting firms, we consistently strive to promote efficiency, cultivate a culture our associates can proudly embrace, and empower our associates to advance their career growth at WGI and beyond.

WGI is always looking for remarkable individuals to join our team and help us grow in our vision. If you think you are an innovative, self-motivated team player, and want to shape your community, join our WGI team today!

WGI offers a complete Benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, LTD & STD, Life Insurance, 401k with match, PTO, Holidays, HSA with company contribution, Pet insurance, and Employee Assistance Program.

Operational Leadership: Lead the operations of WGI's Remote Sensing Department, including staffing, production capacity, equipment, resource allocation, workload balancing, project performance, and operational priorities. Establish scalable processes, accountability, and performance measures that support consistent, predictable, and profitable project delivery.
Maintain visibility into backlog, production capacity, staffing availability, equipment utilization, and upcoming project demand to proactively identify resource constraints and develop appropriate staffing, subcontracting, scheduling, or technology solutions.

Airborne Acquisition Operations: Provide operational oversight of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition programs. Ensure qualified technical personnel, appropriate equipment, documented procedures, quality controls, and adequate resources are in place to support safe, efficient, and successful acquisition.
LiDAR & Imagery Production: Provide leadership and technical oversight for WGI's airborne, mobile, terrestrial, and UAS LiDAR and imagery production capabilities. Ensure production teams have effective workflows, appropriate technical leadership, adequate resources, and clearly defined quality standards from initial processing through final delivery.
Quality Management: Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive QA/QC procedures throughout the acquisition and production lifecycle. Establish measurable checkpoints for collection completeness, trajectory quality, relative and absolute accuracy, point density, imagery quality, calibration, classification, data integrity, metadata, and final deliverables. Perform quarterly audits to ensure Project Manager’s compliance to WGI’s established Quality Assurance Program.
Technical Leadership: Maintain strong working knowledge of Remote Sensing technologies, methodologies, specifications, and industry standards. Provide technical oversight for complex projects, support technical decision-making, and ensure appropriate subject-matter experts are engaged to resolve specialized technical issues. Develop and empower technical leaders within the department rather than creating dependency on a single technical resource.
Project Delivery: Maintain visibility across active Remote Sensing projects and proactively address schedule, staffing, technical, equipment, or quality issues that could affect successful delivery. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.
People Leadership: Lead, mentor, develop, and evaluate Remote Sensing staff and technical leaders. Establish clear expectations, accountability, career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities. Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.
Equipment & Technology Management: Oversee the effective deployment, maintenance, calibration, and lifecycle planning of remote sensing sensors, GNSS/IMU systems, computing infrastructure, storage, and supporting equipment. Participate in evaluation and justification of significant technology and capital investments.
Automation & Process Improvement: Promote automation, batch processing, scripting, and standardized production workflows to improve quality, repeatability, throughput, and cost efficiency. Identify production bottlenecks and implement measurable improvements.
Technical Risk & Issue Resolution: Ensure complex technical, equipment, software, processing, and data-quality issues are appropriately escalated, investigated, and resolved. Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.
Financial & Resource Management: Assist with the development of department budgets, staffing plans, capital expenditures, equipment utilization, project performance, and resource forecasting. Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.
Business Development & Client Support: Support WGI's business development activities through technical presentations, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, project approaches, and client meetings. Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.
Innovation: Evaluate emerging LiDAR, imagery, UAS, positioning, cloud-computing, AI/ML, and geospatial technologies. Recommend technologies and investments that improve WGI's capabilities, productivity, quality, or competitive position.
Safety & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture across airborne, vehicle-based, UAS, and field operations. Ensure departmental activities comply with WGI policies, applicable regulations, aviation requirements, client requirements, professional standards, and established operating procedures.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Surveying, GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline preferred; advanced degree a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.
Data: Management of large point-cloud and imagery datasets, high-performance processing environments, network/cloud storage, metadata, archival and data-transfer workflows.

Preferred Licenses & Certifications

Professional credentials should be considered favorably and may be factored into position level and compensation, including:

ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist (CP)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Scientist - LiDAR (CMS-LiDAR)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Technician - LiDAR (CMT-LiDAR)
Professional Surveyor/Professional Land Surveyor licensure
Surveyor Intern/LSIT certification
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
Other relevant geospatial, photogrammetric, aviation, project-management, or technical certifications

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. We are unable to sponsor or take over the sponsorship of employment visas.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Geothermal Senior Planner (Environmental Planner 4)
within the Shorelands & Environmental Assistance
(SEA) program.

Note
: This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. It may be extended based on funding availability.

Location:

This position can be based at any of the following duty stations:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Eastern Region Office in Spokane, WA .
Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, WA .

Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the selected duty station.

Note: If the selected duty station is the Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, the salary will include an additional 5% premium pay due to its location in King County. Salary range: $6703- $9012 monthly.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
One to two days per week of on-site attendance is required
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Duties

This Geothermal Senior Planner position provides a unique opportunity to lead Washington’s emerging statewide geothermal energy planning and policy efforts within Ecology’s Shorelands & Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program. In this role, you will guide multi-agency collaboration, facilitate complex policy discussions, and deliver high-visibility legislative and technical reports that inform Washington’s transition to clean energy. You will serve as a senior planning consultant to the Clean Energy Coordination Section Manager, shaping policy direction, supporting future statewide planning and rulemaking, and ensuring consistent, transparent, and legally defensible processes related to geothermal development.

You will also support Ecology’s coordination of the geothermal energy collaborative process established by the Legislature—bringing together state agencies, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community interests to identify risks, opportunities, and regulatory needs associated with geothermal technologies. Through this work, you will develop guidance, regulatory gap analyses, outreach materials, environmental review support, and planning documents that advance agency priorities and contribute to the long-term protection and sustainable use of Washington’s natural resources.

What You Will Do

Support Ecology’s statewide geothermal energy collaborative process, managing cross-program and multi-agency teams to develop legislative reports, technical analyses, environmental review support, and statewide guidance documents.
Coordinate with experts across Ecology, other state agencies, federal partners, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community groups to ensure inclusive, informed, and well-aligned planning and environmental review processes.
Research existing regulatory frameworks and conduct regulatory gap analyses to evaluate the need for future statewide planning, policy development, and rulemaking related to geothermal energy.
Provide senior-level planning, policy interpretation, and technical consultation to Ecology leadership, program managers, and staff on geothermal topics, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) processes, regulatory implications, and interagency coordination.
Facilitate resolution of complex, sensitive, and high-profile issues involving diverse perspectives, technical uncertainty, emerging technologies, and major environmental considerations.
Support SEPA planning and project review activities by coordinating technical input, reviewing impact analyses, and ensuring documents are clear, consistent, and meet procedural and legal standards.
Plan, coordinate, and conduct public meetings, hearings, workshops, and comment periods, developing accessible materials and ensuring meaningful engagement of Tribes, community members, and interested parties.
Represent Ecology at multi-agency workgroups, public forums, advisory committees, and policy discussions related to geothermal development, clean energy planning, and statewide environmental review.
Develop and refine tools, guidance, and communication products—working closely with internal and external communications experts—to ensure information is accurate, transparent, and accessible to diverse audiences.
Ensure all deliverables, including legislative reports and technical documents, are efficient, effective, defensible, and aligned with agency policy, scientific information, and interested parties expectations.
Support broader Clean Energy Coordination Section priorities by contributing to statewide planning documents, environmental reviews, interagency coordination efforts, and rulemaking activities related to clean energy development.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Environmental Review: Ability to support complex SEPA environmental review processes, coordinate technical input across programs, interpret impact analyses, and ensure documents meet legal and procedural requirements.
Regulatory Analysis: Ability to analyze and implement federal, state, and local regulations and synthesize technical and regulatory information.
Policy and Planning Analysis: Ability to analyze environmental data, evaluate planning and regulatory implications, and develop recommendations grounded in scientific information and agency policy.
Multi-Agency Coordination: Skill in organizing and facilitating collaboration among state, federal, Tribal, and local government partners to align environmental review timelines, expectations, and shared work products.
Public Process Administration: Experience planning and managing public meetings, hearings, and comment periods, including preparing clear, accessible materials for diverse audiences.
Cross-Program Facilitation: Skilled at navigating complex, sensitive issues involving multiple parties; able to synthesize technical and regulatory information and support resolution of divergent viewpoints.
Technical Communication: Ability to convey complex environmental, regulatory, or policy information clearly and professionally in written and verbal formats for varied audiences.

Education:
involving a major study in land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning, geography, land use or environmental law, public administration with an environmental emphasis, or closely related field.
