9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree in above mentioned field.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree in above mentioned field.

Special Requirements

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license

Desired Qualifications

Experience with advanced, enhanced, or conventional geothermal technologies or geothermal development.
Experience with oil and gas subsurface development, impacts, and mitigation.
Experience with power plant development to support the electrical grid.
Experience developing SEPA or National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) EISs for complex or high-profile proposals, including programmatic reviews or multi-disciplinary impact analyses.

system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We believe that DEIRis both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Regional Compliance Inspector - Refrigerant Management Program (Environmental Specialist 3)
within the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP).

The salary listed includes 5% premium pay due to the position location in King County.
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

A minimum of one day per week is required in the office. This position is expected to be in the office for a full workday every Tuesday.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by October 4, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Do you want your work to directly reduce climate-polluting emissions in Washington State? Does the idea of helping businesses understand and comply with environmental regulations appeal to you? Are you interested in conducting on-the-ground inspections and working one-on-one with the regulated community to keep refrigerant systems operating safely and responsibly? If you answered “yes,” then this role may be a great fit for you!

The Refrigerant Management Program (RMP) regulates facilities with large refrigeration and air-conditioning systems to ensure they follow best practices that reduce leaks of climate-polluting fluorinated gases. As a Regional Compliance Inspector, you will help facilities register in the RMP, provide technical guidance, and conduct inspections across the Northwest region to verify compliance.

Your work will directly support Ecology’s statewide effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from refrigeration systems. You will develop specialized knowledge of Washington’s hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) regulations, interpret technical requirements for the public, and help facilities identify practical, cost-effective ways to meet their obligations. If you are motivated by fieldwork, enjoy problem-solving, and want your work to contribute to meaningful climate solutions, this position offers a rewarding opportunity.

In This Role, You Will

Provide technical assistance to facility owners and operators, helping them understand refrigerant rules, reporting obligations, and how to comply with RMP processes.
Explain refrigerant regulations in a clear, accessible way during one-on-one interactions, online office hours, and public meetings.
Assist facility owners and operators with entering required data into the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Management Program (RAMP) database.

Conduct inspections of facilities subject to the Refrigerant Management Program (RMP), both remotely and in person.
Verify that facilities are following state and federal HFC rules and maintaining records that meet program requirements.
Review RMP registrations and annual reports, identify potential compliance issues, and help return facilities to compliance through follow-up actions.
If necessary, collect and document information necessary for enforcement actions.

Coordinate with teammates across the state to ensure consistent application of inspection procedures and regulatory interpretations, and on potential ways to improve compliance.
Collaborate with Ecology outreach staff to promote awareness of climate-friendly refrigerants and refrigerant alternatives.
Develop/maintain professional knowledge of applicable HFC laws, refrigerant technologies, leak detection methods, and emerging industry issues.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:

Regulatory Application and Interpretation – Demonstrated competence with interpreting and applying environmental or regulatory requirements to accurately assess facility compliance and support consistent implementation of program obligations.
Inspection and Field Evaluation – Experienced in conducting structured compliance inspections or field evaluations to determine whether facilities follow required procedures and maintain accurate operational or recordkeeping practices.
Professional Judgment and Compliance Determination – Skilled at using analytical thinking, evidence review, and sound professional judgment to identify potential violations, recommend corrective actions, and support facilities in returning to sustained compliance.
Technical Assistance and Communication – Ability to explain complex regulatory or technical information in clear, understandable terms to help regulated entities meet program requirements and successfully use required database tools.
Collaborative Coordination Across Teams – Demonstrated competence with coordinating work and sharing information across the regional inspection team to ensure consistent approaches to inspections, education, compliance assistance, and enforcement activities.
Data, System, and Technology Proficiency – Skilled with learning and using program-specific databases and analytical tools to track inspection activities, organize documentation, analyze compliance trends, and prepare accurate reports that support program decision-making.
Independent Project and Workload Management – Ability to independently plan, prioritize, and complete inspections, follow-up activities, and documentation to meet program expectations and support timely, effective compliance outcomes.
Research and Emerging Issues Analysis – Experienced in gaining understanding of new or evolving technical, regulatory, or environmental issues to identify trends, evaluate potential impacts on program implementation, and recommend improvements that strengthen compliance and reduce emissions.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; Environmental Health or Occupational Safety and Health (OSHA) studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
A Master’s degree or above.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid state driver’s license or provide alternate reliable transportation for travel throughout Ecology’s Northwest Region area.

Desired Qualifications

Environmental Compliance and Inspection Experience – Experienced in performing environmental compliance, inspection, or auditing work to assess facility operations, evaluate records or procedures, and recommend corrective actions that strengthen adherence to regulatory requirements.
Climate and Air Quality Knowledge – Demonstrated competence with understanding air quality concepts and climate change science to evaluate how refrigerant emissions and compliance activities support statewide emission reduction goals.
Greenhouse Gas Program Familiarity – Experienced in working with state or federal greenhouse gas reduction programs to understand how HFC-related requirements fit within broader regulatory or climate-policy frameworks.
Program-Specific Technical Learning – Ability to quickly learn and apply new technical subject matter, including refrigerant types, climate-friendly alternatives, and leak detection methods, to support high-quality inspections and compliance assistance.

jobs.description:
GIS Specialist, Raleigh, NC, US

Technical Specialist- Junior

NCDIT-Transportation (NCDIT-T) GIS Team is seeking a Technical Specialist – Junior that will provide dedicated support the State Traffic Operations Center (STOC) and Transportation Mobility & Safety Unit by assisting with maintaining and updating GIS data used in routing, traffic operations, and incident response. This role works with TM&S staff to understand basic workflow needs, assist with gathering requirements, and help build simple to moderately complex maps, dashboards, and GIS tools that support daily operations. The primary focus is to communicate clearly with non-GIS users, ask questions to understand requests, and follow established GIS Unit standards when creating or updating data and applications. Daily work includes editing geometry, updating events and attributing data, performing QA/QC checks, and assisting with progress tracking and documentation. The role may also support Arcade coding and help with ETL processes under guidance from more senior team members.

This position will require an advanced knowledge of ArcGIS Online, the Esri Software Suite, and ArcGIS Enterprise. The candidate must be able to build web mapping applications independently, publish hosted and referenced feature services, and understand the life cycle of GIS products from requirements gathering to databases, schema creation, cartography, application development, and maintenance.

Note: Candidates must be willing and able to perform 12+ hour days in the event of a major emergency activation, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. The ideal candidate will be able to travel to and from the STOC in Raleigh for in-person support during a major activation lasting >5 days. The State will not cover this travel expense, and it must be budgeted and supplied by the contracting firm. Candidates will be paid a flat hourly rate during approved overtime hours, if required. Preference will be given to candidates that live within <1 hour commute to STOC.

The ideal candidate will be able to shadow meetings, listen to issues, and independently identify potential GIS solutions based on complex issues. The ability to quickly generate solutions and describe them to non-IT personnel is essential to this role. Documentation, organization, and communication skills are required. This position will report to the Specialist – Expert position and must be able to take direction and work collaboratively extremely well, both in person, and remotely.

A sample of work is required as part of the submission for this position. A sample of work can include documentation of a GIS process, a cartographic map, a report on a GIS solution, or a link to a GIS application in which the candidate was the primary creator/developer.

Role/Responsibilities

Update and maintain GIS data by editing geometry, events, and attributes to support STOC and TM&S operations.
Perform routine QA/QC checks to ensure data accuracy and follow established GIS Unit workflows and standards.
Assist in creating and updating basic to moderate complexity maps, dashboards, and GIS tools used for routing, signal operations, incident response, and situational awareness.
Work with TM&S staff to understand their requests, ask clarifying questions, and document requirements in a clear and simple way.
Write basic Arcade code to support mapping, queries, calculations, and display.
Support ETL processes under guidance from senior GIS staff, helping keep data and applications up to date.
Attend STOC meetings to observe workflows and learn operational needs, gradually building the context needed to support the future GIS solutions.
Provide general GIS support by answering user questions, troubleshooting simple issues, and escalating more complex problems to senior staff.
Report to Specialist – Expert and work effectively as a team.

Skill Matrix

ArcGIS Online Administration, Web Mapping, and Cartography Required 4 Years

Strong oral and written communication, translation of non-GIS meetings and requests to GIS outcomes Required 4 Years

GIS for Public Safety Nice to have 2 Years

Environmental Specialist Mid HI, TO647(35534)

This position is contingent upon contract award, customer approval, and the availability of funding. The final scope, responsibilities, work location, schedule, position requirements, and employment start date may change based on final contract requirements.

Are you looking for an Environmental Specialist role where you can directly shape installation compliance, conservation, and environmental risk management? Join Serco and Team KIRA in supporting the 647th Civil Engineer Squadron (647 CES) at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH).

As a Mid-Level Environmental Specialist, you will support the transition of environmental records, facility documentation, and compliance programs from Navy systems into Air Force authoritative repositories. Your work will help ensure environmental information is accurate, organized, and available to support compliance, Activity Management Plans (AMPs), project development, and installation decision-making.

You will manage environmental compliance and conservation activities, coordinate with regulators and mission partners, support hazardous material requirements, conduct inspections and field assessments, and provide environmental input for facility and infrastructure projects.

Why Join Serco and Team KIRA?

Support environmental stewardship and mission readiness across Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam.
Help establish a high-integrity baseline of environmental records, compliance documentation, and program data.
Provide defensible environmental recommendations that support installation planning and decision-making.
Collaborate with an integrated team supporting the transition of environmental, facility, utility, and real property programs from Navy oversight to Air Force stewardship.

As a Mid-Level Environmental Specialist, You Will

Manage day-to-day environmental compliance, conservation, stewardship, and sustainability activities in accordance with applicable federal, state, Department of Defense, and Air Force requirements.
Identify environmental compliance risks, required actions, mitigation measures, and abatement needs.
Prepare technical environmental program documentation and support compliance reviews.
Provide environmental planning input for facility, utility, and infrastructure projects to help integrate environmental requirements early in project development.
Lead the transfer, validation, organization, and upload of environmental documentation from Navy systems into Air Force repositories, including NexGen IT and SharePoint.
Ensure transferred records comply with Air Force records management standards and support environmental program audits, quality reviews, and installation decision-making.
Coordinate with regulators, host and tenant organizations, mission partners, and community groups.
Develop and review environmental permits, regulatory submittals, compliance actions, and response packages for notices of violation.
Conduct internal environmental inspections and maintain inspection criteria, schedules, and checklists.

Job Description

Job Title:
Adjunct Conservation Educator - Internships

Summer (May - August): Monday through Friday, 8:30am – 4:30pm; 38 hours per week

Fall (September – January): 8:30am – 4:30pm; 25-39 hours per week

Job Description:
The Adjunct Conservation Educator will support the implementation of two internship programs—Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) and the Emerging Leaders in Conservation Solutions Internship (ELCSI)—providing coordination, mentorship, instruction, and support to both high school and undergraduate/trade school students.
Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) May – September
Project TRUE is a 21-week research mentoring program for rising high school juniors and seniors from the Bronx, providing hands-on urban ecology research experiences and mentorship from undergraduate students and STEM professionals. The Adjunct Educator will assist with the implementation and coordination of the program, collaborating with the Project TRUE leadership team to support and co-mentor undergraduate and high school students as they develop and conduct authentic research projects at the Bronx Zoo. The Educator will support the planning and facilitation of science and mentorship curriculum, guide students through research project development, data collection and analysis, and help students synthesize and communicate their findings.
Emerging Leaders in Climate Solutions Internship (ELCSI) September – April
ELCSI is a new internship opportunity for undergraduate and trade school students who are not pursuing STEM fields but are interested in exploring how climate solutions can be incorporated into their future careers. The program provides foundational knowledge of climate science and climate change through hands-on learning and field experiences that introduce interns to a range of careers connected to climate solutions. As the primary point of contact for ELCS, the Adjunct Educator will lead the day-to-day implementation and coordination of the internship, serving as a facilitator, mentor, and instructor for a cohort of 15–20 interns. The Adjunct Educator will coordinate field experiences, develop and facilitate learning activities aligned with program objectives and outcomes, and provide guidance and support as interns develop their culminating projects and reports. Across both programs, the Adjunct Educator will foster meaningful learning experiences, provide mentorship, and help inspire the next generation of conservation and environmental professionals.

Responsibilities:
Adjunct Conservation Educator - Internships will…

Serve as an educator, mentor, and facilitator for high school, undergraduate, and trade school participants, sharing knowledge and enthusiasm for urban ecology, climate science, conservation, and scientific research.

Assist with the development, adaptation, and facilitation of science research and mentorship curriculum, including lessons and hands-on activities. (Project TRUE)

Guide students through authentic research projects, including experimental design, field methods, data collection and analysis, synthesis of findings, and development of research posters and abstracts. (Project TRUE)

Serve as the primary point of contact for the Conservation Solutions Internship, coordinating program activities, communication, logistics, and day-to-day implementation. (ELCS)

Coordinate fieldwork, field trips, and experiential learning opportunities that connect ELCS participants to climate science, conservation, and related career pathways. (ELCS)

Teach lessons and facilitate hands-on learning experiences in classroom, zoo, outdoor, and field research settings, and support ELCS participants in developing culminating projects and reports.

Collaborate with program staff, mentors, scientists, educators, and external partners to support effective program implementation and meaningful participant experiences (ELCS)

Prepare and maintain program materials, supplies, and research equipment; monitor participant engagement; and provide mentorship and guidance to support participants’ academic and professional development.

Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualification Requirements

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in science, education, or related field

One-year prior teaching or mentorship experience

Ability to work within a highly team-oriented environment, as well as independently

Excellent verbal communication skills to help interpret science concepts and to coordinate with others

Reliable, flexible, and accountable

Willingness to travel to field locations throughout the 5 boroughs

Must be able to lift and carry up to 20lbs and face the rigors of fieldwork including long periods of time outdoors, large amounts of walking and standing, and exposure to the elements and rugged/overgrown terrain

Educational background in ecology, environmental science or education preferred

Valid driver’s license preferred

We ensure that everyone has an opportunity to fully contribute to our mission.
Benefits and Perks

Critter Control Operations specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail

Tacoma Power is seeking a Natural Resources Operations Manager to set the direction and drive the delivery of work spanning Northwest fisheries, environmental commitments, and natural resources operations. This leader will establish how scientific, regulatory, and operational priorities are balanced and translate that direction into clear decisions, coordinated work plans, and defined accountability, guiding complex Natural Resources initiatives from concept through implementation and sustained operation.

Northwest fisheries expertise is foundational to this role, and the successful candidate must have professional experience in at least one of the following areas: fisheries resource management, hatchery operations, or fish passage at Northwest hydroelectric facilities. Candidates must also have experience leading major environmental capital projects from initial planning through implementation and transition into sustained, full-scale operation.

Reporting to the Assistant Section Manager for Natural Resources, the Operations Manager directs fisheries resource programs and fish facility operations, working through facility managers, oversees field technician deployment (support for Science and Research, Wildlife and Lands, Water Resources, and Fisheries Operations), and data analytics throughout the department. At the heart of the role is the ability to integrate forward looking strategy, fisheries science, monitoring data, technical information, current FERC license requirements, and operational realities so fish facilities, natural systems, and hydroelectric operations are planned and managed in coordination. This approach supports safe operations, regulatory compliance, long-term stewardship, and reliable, flexible clean power. A defining requirement of this role is the ability to build the structure and capacity needed to take complex Natural Resources initiatives and capital solutions from initial concept through successful implementation and sustained operation. This means setting priorities, aligning resources, and establishing the roles, workflows, and accountability necessary to advance relicensing, current license implementation, and recovery efforts while meeting ongoing operational commitments. The Operations Manager will also guide supervisors and staff through future operational and organizational changes while maintaining continuity. With future studies, relicensing, and evolving regulatory obligations ahead, this leader will be an integral part of the leadership team to position Natural Resources to meet new demands while maintaining safe, reliable operations.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership and Delivery

Lead environmental capital projects from initial planning through successful implementation and transition into sustained operation.
Provide direction and oversight for fisheries resource management and fish facility operations at the Cowlitz and Cushman projects, working with facility managers to ensure alignment and accountability across programs.
Lead department-wide data and analytics, ensuring information is effectively collected, analyzed, and used for reporting and decision support.
Establish field support with integrated priorities and implementation plans across support for Science and Research, Wildlife and Lands, Water Resources, and Fisheries Operations based on operational capacity, safety requirements, regulatory commitments, and long-term objectives

People and Supervisor Leadership

Lead supervisors and multidisciplinary staff across facility operations, field services, technical services, data and analytics, and program delivery.
Support hiring, performance management, coaching, and professional development.
Maintain a regular field presence to understand operational conditions and support staff.

Coordination and Representation

Partner with Natural Resources leadership, Generation, Tribes, agencies, and other stakeholders to align scientific, regulatory, and operational priorities.
Represent operational impacts, resource needs, project dependencies, and opportunity costs in planning, studies, relicensing, and decision-making.

Budget, Contracts, and Resources

Oversee significant operational budgets and sponsor high-profile capital and non-capital projects.
Manage consultant and vendor contracts supporting fish facilities, Natural Resources initiatives, and field operations. Perform owner’s representative functions for assigned capital projects.

Compliance and Accountability

Ensure fish facility operations, fisheries resource management, and related aquatic and terrestrial activities comply with FERC license requirements, applicable permits, and other regulatory obligations.
Maintain effective systems for tracking regulatory commitments, project progress, operational data, documentation, and reporting.
Provide clear operational updates to leadership and elevate significant issues with recommended actions.

Preferred Leadership Attributes

Experience leading operational teams in a regulated fisheries or natural resources environment.
Ability to provide leadership across aquatic and terrestrial resource areas, including disciplines beyond the individual’s primary area of expertise.
A track record of guiding teams through operational or organizational change without disrupting critical services. A collaborative approach to building alignment across scientific, technical, regulatory, and operational disciplines.
Sound judgment when balancing immediate operational needs, ecosystem objectives, regulatory requirements, and clean-power priorities.

Qualifications

Minimum Education*

Bachelor's degree in public or business administration or directly related field

Minimum Experience*

6 years of progressively responsible analytical and/or program coordination or management work in operational, utility, or natural resources environments including 1 year prior at senior, lead or supervisory level

Equivalency: 1 year of experience = 1 year of education

Knowledge & Skills

The successful candidate will demonstrate the following knowledge and skills:

Applied knowledge of fisheries programs, hatchery operations, or fish passage.
Knowledge of the regulatory requirements affecting hydroelectric fisheries programs, including FERC license requirements, permits, and associated compliance obligations.
Experience translating scientific, regulatory, and operational requirements into clear work plans, priorities, and deliverables.
Strong project leadership across interdependent teams, competing priorities, and organizational change.
An understanding of how fish facility operations, field technician deployment, data collection, analysis, and regulatory reporting work together.
Experience managing operational budgets, contracts, and resources in support of program and project commitments.
Effective collaboration with Tribes, agencies, technical experts, utility partners, and other stakeholders.
Sound judgment in identifying operational risks, explaining their impacts, and recommending practical solutions.

Selection Process & Supplemental Information

Tacoma Power is a municipally owned public power utility that delivers nearly all of its energy from hydroelectric resources. Serving approximately 180,000 customers, we operate in a highly regulated environment where operational reliability, stewardship, and long-term planning are essential.

As one of three operating divisions of Tacoma Public Utilities, alongside Tacoma Water and Tacoma Rail, Tacoma Power offers leaders the opportunity to do meaningful, highly visible work that directly impacts communities, infrastructure, and natural resources.

Our Natural Resources team brings scientific, technical, and operational expertise to meeting the regulatory requirements and stewardship commitments associated with Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric projects. Environmental Specialist Junior, HI TO647

This position is contingent upon contract award, customer approval, and the availability of funding. The final scope, responsibilities, work location, schedule, position requirements, and employment start date may change based on final contract requirements.

Are you interested in an Environmental Specialist role where your work could help protect both mission and community? In this proposed entry-level position, you would support environmental program management, records transition, regulatory coordination, field inspections, hazard tracking, and environmental documentation at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam.

You would support the 647 CES environmental program and assist with transitioning environmental records, facility data, and compliance documentation from Navy systems to Air Force systems. Your work would contribute to environmental compliance, mission readiness, and long-term installation stewardship.

Why Join Serco?

Support Air Force mission readiness and environmental stewardship.
Build experience in environmental compliance, permitting, inspections, records management, and installation planning.
Collaborate with an integrated team supporting environmental, engineering, planning, geospatial, and financial programs.
Help deliver accurate environmental data and compliant documentation that support installation decisions.

As An Environmental Specialist, You Would

Support environmental program management, compliance reviews, reporting, and coordination with environmental program managers.
Apply applicable federal, state, Department of Defense, and Air Force environmental requirements to identify risks, document issues, and support mitigation actions.
Assist with transferring environmental permits, studies, compliance records, and related documentation from Navy databases to designated Air Force systems, including NexGen IT and SharePoint.

Support authorized coordination with regulators, mission partners, and community stakeholders.

Wildlife and Habitat Conservation Scientist (AI Training)

About The Role

We're looking for wildlife and habitat conservation scientists to help shape how AI understands biodiversity protection and ecosystem management. Your field expertise will directly influence the accuracy and reliability of AI systems tackling some of the most important ecological challenges of our time.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role — work on your own schedule while contributing to cutting-edge AI development.

Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: Flexible, asynchronous

What You'll Do

Review AI-generated wildlife and habitat conservation scenarios for scientific accuracy
Evaluate the quality of ecological reasoning and proposed conservation strategies
Identify unrealistic assumptions, logical gaps, or misapplied conservation methods
Provide clear, structured feedback to improve the ecological validity of AI outputs
Work independently and asynchronously to meet project deadlines on your own schedule

Who You Are

3+ years of experience in wildlife biology, ecology, habitat conservation, or a related field
Strong working knowledge of biodiversity principles and ecosystem management
Able to critically evaluate applied ecological reasoning presented in written form
Comfortable reviewing and annotating structured scientific content
Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and reliable

Nice to Have

Graduate degree in Ecology, Wildlife Biology, Environmental Science, or a related discipline
Hands-on field research or conservation program experience
Familiarity with AI systems, content evaluation, or scientific review workflows

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects with top research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work on your own schedule, from anywhere
Freelance perks: autonomy, variety, and global collaboration
Make a meaningful impact by ensuring AI gets conservation science right
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension

jobs.title: Sr. Regional Enviro Engineer - Water Compliance, AWS Environmental Team
jobs.description:
Description

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE) specializing in water compliance, you will support water-related environmental compliance at AWS data centers. You will provide technical expertise in permitting and compliance across National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Significant Industrial User (SIU) discharge, potable water systems, groundwater wells, onsite wastewater treatment systems, stormwater, and water-quality monitoring and reporting. You will evaluate existing and proposed infrastructure, develop scalable compliance programs and technical standards, monitor environmental performance, and partner with design, construction, operations, and other stakeholders to incorporate water-related regulatory requirements into site design and operation.

Key job responsibilities

Lead water compliance programs for water supply and discharge across US data center locations
Develop and maintain the water compliance program that guides how sites and REEs obtain, renew, modify, interpret, and implement NPDES and other water discharge permits under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and applicable state regulations, and translate effluent limitations, monitoring, operating, reporting, and notification requirements into site-level compliance programs
Provide guidance on evaluating regulatory applicability and permitting requirements for new sites, expansions, operational changes, and new or modified discharges
Provide guidance on evaluating industrial wastewater and stormwater permitting and compliance, including federal pretreatment under 40 CFR Part 403, local sewer-use ordinances, POTW requirements, pollution-prevention plans, inspections, best management practices, monitoring, and reporting
Provide technical guidance on potable water systems and onsite wastewater systems, including design, operation, monitoring, and compliance under applicable drinking-water and septic requirements
Develop standard templates and technical guidance for water-quality sampling and monitoring plans, review site plans, and set standards for sampling equipment, monitoring systems, and analytical methods under 40 CFR Part 136
Evaluate water and wastewater treatment processes, system performance, waste-stream characterization, water balances, and discharge pathways to determine permitting and compliance implications
Build the mechanisms, dashboards, and metrics that track water-quality data, lab reports, DMRs, and compliance performance, and support sites in identifying trends, exceedances, corrective actions, and forecasting across sites
Read and evaluate engineering plans, process-flow diagrams, P&IDs, and specifications, and partner with design, engineering, construction, and operations teams to build water-related controls into current and future designs early
Clearly communicate the technical and regulatory basis for environmental requirements and influence partner teams to implement compliant, practical, and scalable solutions
Set the standards and oversight mechanisms that keep work by employees, contractors, and consultants aligned with applicable environmental requirements and Amazon standards
Support REEs and sites in their interactions with regulatory agencies, utilities, POTWs, consultants, and contractors, and engage directly on program-level matters
Support time-critical regulatory notifications, permit applications, and monitoring reports, and support emergency response planning and incident investigations, including root causes and corrective and preventive actions
Develop and deliver water compliance training for relevant staff
Stay current with evolving water regulations and industry best practices for domestic and non-contact cooling, particularly in the data center sector

About The Team

The AWS Environmental is a team of professionals responsible for the environmental planning, delivery, and operational compliance of all AWS global infrastructure projects.

Basic Qualifications

Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field
Experience with NPDES and industrial wastewater permitting and compliance, including interpreting effluent limitations, sampling/monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and noncompliance notification requirements under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and federal pretreatment requirements under 40 CFR Part 403, and applicable state or local regulatory programs.
Experience developing or implementing water-quality sampling and monitoring programs, including sampling plans, sampling locations, analytical parameters and methods, sampling equipment, laboratory coordination, and data evaluation.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in engineering or equivalent
Experience supporting water compliance across multiple facilities, jurisdictions, or regulatory programs, and with public water system requirements under the Safe Drinking Water Act, 40 CFR Part 141, and applicable state drinking-water programs.
Working knowledge of potable water and septic/onsite wastewater treatment systems, including their design, operation, monitoring, and regulatory compliance.
Experience with industrial wastewater treatment, pretreatment systems, publicly owned treatment works, and local industrial-user permits, including evaluating the design and operation of water and wastewater treatment, conveyance, storage, sampling, and monitoring systems.
Experience reviewing civil, mechanical, plumbing, and process designs for water-related regulatory and permit compliance.
Experience developing scalable environmental standards, procedures, tools, or compliance mechanisms for use across multiple sites, and managing multiple technically complex projects and regulatory deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Strong analytical, technical-writing, communication, relationship-building, influencing, and negotiation skills.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

You will partner with AWS stakeholders to develop regional and site-specific development strategies enabling the construction and operation of AWS datacenters and infrastructure. You will lead environmental due diligence for site selection and acquisition, develop and execute regional and site-specific environmental permitting strategies, support environmental compliance during design and construction, and prepare for data center operations. This role requires regular engagement throughout the development lifecycle with multiple AWS stakeholders including Real Estate, Legal, Risk, Water, Design, Public Policy, Construction, and Operational teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulatory agencies, consultants, and contractors.

A successful candidate in this role will have a proven track record of delivering multiple, high-priority projects with tight timelines that require strong communication with partner teams, outside consultants and counsel, and regulatory agencies. The candidate must have a strong understanding of multi-media United States environmental permitting, remediation, and compliance requirements associated with large-scale infrastructure including experience with Clean Water Act (CWA) 404 and NPDES permitting. Preference in experience with OH EPA, IDEM, MO EDQ.

Key job responsibilities

Assess environmental risks and requirements and develop mitigations and strategies to support data center siting and development strategies and site-specific project delivery.
Lead technical aspects of environmental due diligence, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, regulatory and permitting evaluations, natural, biological and cultural resource evaluations, and noise assessments.
Deliver environmental permits, approvals, and plans to enable on-time and compliant construction and operations for new data center locations and expansion of existing sites.
Communicate environmental requirements, risks, and activities to internal and external project partners.
Coordinate with partner teams including Real Estate, Design, Water, Legal, Risk, Power, and others to optimize site designs to consider natural resource or operational constraints.
Develop site development and permitting strategies that are environmentally responsible and sustainable while meeting project timelines.
Lead regulatory agency interactions and negotiations in support of environmental permit acquisition and regional development strategies.
Develop, manage and track metrics to evaluate project success

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Position Title

Florida Conservation Program Manager

Department/Program

Florida Conservation

Senior Director of Florida Conservation

About Ocean Conservancy

For more than 50 years, Ocean Conservancy has delivered effective, evidence-based solutions for the ocean and all who depend on it. Today, we continue to unite science, people and policy to protect our ocean from the greatest challenges it faces: climate change, plastic pollution and biodiversity loss. We are a 501(C)3 headquartered in Washington, D.C. that inspires a worldwide network of partners, advocates and supporters through our comprehensive and clear-eyed approach to ocean conservation. Together, we are securing a healthy ocean and a thriving planet, forever and for everyone.

Position Summary

As a core member of Ocean Conservancy’s Florida Conservation Team, the Florida Conservation Program Manager
will provide critical mission support and added capacity, and will expand and enhance the organization’s ability to work with partners in state and local governments and within the conservation community across Florida. The Manager will serve as a key point of contact with both existing and new local government partners, and will provide lead flagship projects such as grassroots marine debris efforts, marine plastics assessments and grassroots advocacy, sea level rise and climate change initiatives, water quality and abundance interventions, and marine wildlife and habitat protection efforts. The Manager will also represent Ocean Conservancy in public appearances, testimony, and in outreach and education activities.

The Manager will report to the Senior Director of Florida Conservation, and will preferably be based in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Primary Responsibilities

Seek, manage, and expand upon community led initiatives to reduce marine debris and nutrient pollution across Florida, including in key regions that align with the Florida Program Multi Year Strategy – Tampa Bay, Indian River Lagoon, and Biscayne Bay, among others.
Lead strategic development of marine debris positions for the organization that can be deployed at the local government and state levels.
Develop and advance community driven interventions on water quality and marine debris
Participate in the development of grant applications and budget development to attract funding for water quality and marine debris projects in Florida.
Network and partner with state and local government officials on marine conservation priorities in target regions of Florida including South Florida, West Central Florida, Southwest Florida, the I-4 corridor, and Northeast Florida.
Lead the coordination and networking of environmental NGO peers and partners statewide to maximize impact for marine conservation, including in formal Ocean Conservancy led coalitions
Network with impacted stakeholders on issues including water quality and abundance, sea level rise and climate change, marine debris and ocean plastics, and habitat and wildlife
Represent Ocean Conservancy in public settings, including events such as conventions, symposia, and restoration and cleanup events
Provide public testimony to local and state government on marine conservation issues, for example in support of marine debris regulation or fertilizer ordinances
Help develop and refine Ocean Conservancy’s policy positions on marine conservation issues affecting the state

Required Skills/Qualifications/Experience

The successful candidate will, at a minimum, possess the following qualifications:

3-5 years experience in the field of environmental conservation in Florida; an advanced degree (in science, law, policy, or a field related to conservation) will be considered in lieu of experience.
A genuine, ardent passion for the conservation of Florida’s marine environment, and a deep connection to the state and its ecosystems.
Familiarity and experience with the latest marine conservation issues in Florida, and with the potential spectrum of solutions to address those issues – this includes water quality and abundance, nutrient pollution, plastic pollution and marine debris, sea level rise and climate change, and threats to wildlife and habitat, among others.
Innate empathy and a willingness to work with people from across economic and political spectrums and from diverse communities to achieve a greater good
Excellent communications skills, both written and verbal; facility with public speaking; experience and comfort with speaking to the media a plus.
Experience and familiarity with environmental policy analysis and advocacy and a desire to develop policy positions that will have a positive impact for Florida’s marine environment
Highly detail oriented, adaptable, well-organized, and self-starting – ability to work independently and manage up
Highly collaborative and outgoing with large, multi-disciplinary teams

EDUCATION/TRAINING

Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to Ocean Conservancy’s marine conservation mission

Compensation

Ocean Conservancy is committed to fair pay practices and posts expected salary ranges for each of its positions. Compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s specialty skills, years of experience, location, and unique background. The expected starting salary range for this role is $70,000 - $80,000 annually. We would welcome the opportunity to connect with potential candidates whose salary requirements may be outside of the expected range.

TO APPLY

If you think you’d be a great fit for the job and are interested in joining Ocean Conservancy’s team, please apply here. Please include a resume and cover letter in one file on your application.

HYBRID WORK ENVIRONMENT

Ocean Conservancy embraces a hybrid work environment, which allows our staff the flexibility to work virtually and in-person while building strong connections across the institution.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Ocean Conservancy provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

We encourage applicants who have a diverse level and range of relevant skills and experiences to apply. A 100% match is not required. We want to support employees’ career growth and in return, our employees help Ocean Conservancy grow into a stronger, more inclusive institution.

▪Observe the implementation of industrial safety, occupational health, fire protection and accident prevention (e.g. walk through the work areas and report the inadequacies , as well as suggest actions for their elimination; inspect work accidents; train safety personnel; cooperate in approval of hazardous materials and creating instruction for their use, etc.).

▪Planning, Conducting work environment measurement required by law (e.g. lighting, Noise, Air quality, Pollution released to environment, soil and groundwater contamination etc.)

include your age, date of birth, or the dates you attended or graduated from school. Only provide this information if it is specifically requested to meet job requirements or to follow federal, state, or local laws or rules.

About The Position

Under the direction of a PBOT-MO Environmental Systems Division (ESD) Manager II. The purpose of this position supports the coordination, prioritization, sequencing, and accomplishment reporting for sewer/stormwater inspection, cleaning, repair and utility locates work orders for sewer cleaning, associated with the maintenance and operations of the City of Portland Wastewater/Stormwater Collection System.

What You’ll Get To Do, Examples Of The Work That This Position Would Provide Includes, But Is Not Limited To The Following

Plan, prepare and distribute work for Sewer/Stormwater Cleaning, Inspection, Utility Locates & Repair.
Review, develop and implement continual improvements.
Perform research, respond and assess service requests.
Review data from work performed to track performance and budget.
Maintain databases, compliance records, and create regular reports on status, actions, trends.
M ay supervise employees and may lead staff on assigned programs, projects, and functions.
Intra-Bureau and Inter-Agency Coordination.
Emergency Response associated with weather events affecting system operations, as well as response to snow/ice events.
Special Projects and Duties as assigned.

Who You Are

Data User & Analyst: You are able to access key data, analysis the data, present in formats to support fact-based options for decision-making.
Decision Maker: You are a strong decision maker, able to arrive at independent decision to authorize and coordinate the prioritization of work.
Organized: You have a keen attention to detail, providing a high level of resource management while maintaining accurate records, an aptitude for continuous improvement, and your change management skills are strong.
Flexible: You’ve demonstrated the ability to maintain flexible, agile and calm in a high-paced environment that relies on quick and stable decision-making.
Problem Solver: You can identify problems early and value collaboration. You utilize active listening, effective communication and facilitation skills in working with others to find resolutions.
Authentic: You treat community members, co-workers, and employees with respect and are accountable.
Dedicated: Have a passion for public service and hold a high level of pride in making sure the projects, tasks, and emergencies are effectively and efficiently completed.
Manage projects and people: Experience supervising employees and/or lead staff on assigned programs, projects, and functions.
Team Player: An outgoing professional who values building trust, partnerships, and relationships to accomplish objectives more effectively for the team.

About the division/bureau: Transportation/Environmental Systems Division

The Environmental System Division (ESD) is part of Portland Bureau of Transportation Maintenance & Operations Group (PBOT-MO). ESD provides maintenance and operations activities to support the City of Portland’s Wastewater & Stormwater Collection System. ESD provides Stormwater/Sewer Cleaning, Inspection, Underground Utility Locates, and Sewer/Stormwater Repair maintenance activities via a ‘Cooperative Work Agreement’ to the Bureau of Environmental Services (BES), in support of the City of Portland’s federal and state permits protecting public health, safety and the environment, known as the ‘National Pollution Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)’ permit.

The Portland Bureau of Transportation is a community partner in shaping a livable city. We plan, build, manage, and maintain an effective and safe transportation system that provides people and businesses access and mobility. We keep Portland moving. For more information about the Portland Bureau of Transportation, please visit Transportation | Portland.gov . The Portland Bureau of Transportation embraces diversity, models inclusivity, and promotes equity through its service delivery, internal operations, organizational culture, and in its work with partners and the community.

To Qualify

Applicants must demonstrate how their education, training, and experience meet each of the minimum qualifications listed below:

Knowledge of wastewater and stormwater collection systems operations, such as cleaning, inspection, repair and utility locates to support federal/state permit requirements.
Experience exercising independent judgement, problem-solving, and initiative within established procedures, guidelines and authority.
Experience providing responsive customer service and clear communication to a variety of technical and non-technical stakeholders with minimal supervision.
Experience utilizing multiple database systems and software systems, including standard business applications (MS Office 365 or other similar), specialized software for work order/asset management (Maximo, Infor (Hansen)) and on-line ticket reporting software (Zendesk, TrackIT).
Experience managing projects and people, including supervising employees or leading staff on assigned programs, projects or functions, and the ability to work effectively and respectfully within a diverse workforce while responding appropriately to questions and service requests.

Applicant must also possess:

Safety training certificates based on business functions.

Although Not Required, You May

Incident Command Training from FEMA.
Have an Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) Wastewater Collection Certification Level 1 or Level 2.

Job Information

Job Title: Wildlife Technician (Hay Zama Bison)

Job Requisition ID: 87893

Ministry: Forestry and Parks

Location: High Level

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Temporary – Wage (up to 5 months)

Scope: Open Closing

Date: October 4, 2026

Classification: Natural Resources 5

Salary: $28.60 to $36.19 Per hour

Forestry and Parks are responsible for managing our forests, public lands and provincial parks. Our Ministry accountabilities include:

Growing Alberta’s environmentally responsible wood products and forestry sector.
Protecting Alberta’s forests from wildfire.
Preserving our provincial parks for the recreation and enjoyment of Albertans.
Enabling access to public lands for recreation and purposes while prioritizing conservation.
Managing public lands and balancing sustainable rangelands and grazing leases for Alberta producers.

Within the Ministry, Land Operations Division, delivers an integrated approach to the management of provincial Crown Land. The work of the Division reflects the full range of users of the province’s Crown land including conservation, recreation, tourism, energy, forestry, agriculture and traditional land uses.

Role Responsibilities

The Hay-Zama Bison Technician supports senior and area Wildlife and Species at Risk (SAR) Biologists in the delivery of the Wood Bison Conservation and Recovery Program in northwestern Alberta.

This position plays a key role in coordinating and supporting all aspects of the Hay-Zama bison harvest season, including engagement with Indigenous and non-Indigenous harvesters, issuing licenses and registration certificates, collecting and processing disease monitoring samples, and liaising with local communities and stakeholders.

The role also contributes to the implementation of approved recovery actions for Wood Bison, such as population surveys, habitat monitoring, and conflict mitigation measures.

Key Responsibilities

Support the delivery of the Hay-Zama bison harvest season by issuing Indigenous hunter licenses and compulsory registration certificates, collecting and processing biological samples for disease monitoring, and providing information and coordination support to harvesters.
Conduct and assist with wildlife surveys, data collection, and field monitoring activities (ground-based and aerial).
Compile, organize, and manage biological data for entry into the Fish and Wildlife Management Information System (FWMIS).
Support human-bison conflict management and safety awareness initiatives.
Collaborate with Dene Tha’ First Nation partners, Indigenous communities, and municipal stakeholders to advance bison conservation and recovery objectives.

The Job Description is provided for Further details on this position.

APS Compentencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: Understands how individual actions and data collection contribute to broader conservation outcomes. Anticipates long-term implications and adjusts work to support program goals.
Build Collaborative Environments: Fosters respectful relationships with colleagues, Indigenous partners, and stakeholders. Encourages open communication and teamwork to achieve shared objectives.
Agility: Adapts effectively to changing priorities, field conditions, and timelines. Maintains composure and initiative in dynamic work environments.
Drive for Results: Takes responsibility for delivering quality outcomes and meeting commitments. Seeks feedback and applies learning to improve performance.

Qualifications

Two-year completed diploma in Natural Resources Technology, Environmental Science, Wildlife Management, or a closely related field.
Valid Driver’s License (Class 5).

Equivalency
: Directly related education or experience considered based on:1 year of education for 1 year of experience; or 1 year of experience for 1 year education

Assets

Current First Aid certification (CPR Level C).
Experience in wildlife or natural resource fieldwork, including data collection, sampling, and monitoring.
Experience using GPS, GIS (ArcGIS), and data management tools for recording and analyzing field data.
Experience preparing technical summaries, reports, or database entries related to wildlife or environmental programs.
Experience participating in aerial or ground-based wildlife surveys is considered an asset.
Experience operating field equipment such as 4x4 vehicles, ATVs, and boats in remote or rugged environments.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointment to a job classification.

Notes

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

This competition is recruiting for seasonal wage position that would begin November 1, 2026, and end March 31, 2027 (5 months), based in High Level, Alberta.
The role is primarily field based in remote and rugged areas of northwest Alberta. Fieldwork may require extended stays in
camps with limited amenities, exposure to variable weather, and physically demanding tasks.
Field operations involve the use of 4x4 vehicles, ATVs, boats, and helicopters. Flexibility in work hours is required to support seasonal bison management activities.

About

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.

Application Opening Date: September 28, 2026

Location: 1 Lakeshore Drive, Moccasin, CA, Moccasin, California, United States

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Natural Resources And Lands Management Division

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About The Moccasin Planning And Compliance Section Of NRLM

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Role Description

Role Description:

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.
Prepares or coordinates permit applications, right-of-way and special use authorization requests, and related submissions to local, state, and federal agencies.
Obtains authorizations under CWA

401/404, NPDES
402, Fish & Game Code

1602/1610, ESA/CESA, NHPA
106, ARPA, FLPMA, Raker Act, Wilderness Act, Wild & Scenic Rivers Act, and related federal/state authorities. Prepares, reviews, and coordinates CEQA, NEPA, NHPA, FLPMA, and related environmental review and compliance documentation.
Prepares and manages technical studies and reports concerning environmental, biological, cultural, land, and other natural resource matters.
Critically reviews and evaluates consultant work associated with planning, permitting, environmental review, technical studies, and compliance monitoring, and develops scopes of work and supports consultant contract administration, including schedules, budgets, deliverables, and fieldwork coordination.
Coordinates interdisciplinary review of project proposals, technical studies, and environmental documentation; performs environmental review of third-party applications for use of SFPUC lands.
Identifies environmental and regulatory risks, evaluates available information, and develops practical recommendations when requirements or project conditions are uncertain.
Represents SFPUC interests during interagency consultations, stakeholder meetings, public meetings, and field visits, and collaborates with multidisciplinary staff, consultants, regulatory personnel, Tribal representatives, and other parties.
Exercise sound and objective judgment, including when information is incomplete, requirements are uncertain, or competing priorities must be reconciled.
Manages competing priorities and communicates emerging issues, schedule risks, and recommended actions to project managers and supervisors.
Communicate complex legal, technical, and procedural information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

How To Qualify

Minimum Qualifications:

Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university AND four (4) years (8000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

OR

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in city/regional/urban planning, environmental studies, architecture, law, earth sciences, geography, economics, landscape architecture, civil engineering, urban studies or public administration AND two (2) years (4000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

AND

License:Possession of a current valid California Driver’s License.

Note:
One (1) year of full-time employment is considered equivalent to two thousand (2,000) hours. Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Desirable Qualifications:
The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring:

Experience interpreting or working with federal land management and permitting instruments including rights-of-way, special use authorizations, permits, easements, agreements, maps, land records, or historical authorizations.
Experience applying local, state, and federal environmental laws, regulations, and environmental review processes.
Experience with cultural resources identification, preservation, protection, consultation, and management practices.
Experience conducting environmental review and permitting for utility, infrastructure, operations, maintenance, or capital improvement activities.
Experience using GIS, databases, document management systems, or other tools to organize and analyze environmental, geographic, or regulatory information.
Experience developing scopes of work and supporting consultant contract administration, schedules, budgets, and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Experience coordinating with regulatory agencies, land management agencies, Tribal representatives, project managers, operations staff, consultants, attorneys, or other parties with differing responsibilities and perspectives.

for our location in Clearfield, UT. This position is onsite and will join a diverse team of engineers.

What You will do:

APIMS is a management tool used to comply with all aspects of the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Storage Tanks, and Refrigerant Management regulations at ~200 industrial facilities. Determines impact on company operations and publishes compliance strategies and requirements.

Department Information

This posting is only open to current residents of the State of Colorado.
