https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TvscsQSYIM

About Cdphe

At the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, we are charged with protecting Colorado’s health and

environment – a responsibility that affects every person and every community in the state. CDPHE is distinctive because we bring public health and environmental protection together under one agency, recognizing that healthy people depend on healthy places. Our teams prevent diseases and injury, respond to emergencies ranging from E.coli outbreaks to global pandemics, reduce air pollution, protect water quality, regulate health facilities, manage environmental hazards, perform advanced laboratory testing, provide birth and death records, and implement health promoting programs. We turn science and data into action, set statewide standards, and work alongside local public health agencies and community partners to meet Colorado’s most pressing health and environmental challenges. Working at CDPHE means applying your expertise to complex, consequential work that can improve lives across the state.

Our mission captures this broad portfolio of work: to advance Colorado’s health and protect the places we live, learn, work, and play. Our vision is a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations can thrive. Achieving the mission and vision takes bold action, talented people, broad partnerships, and a commitment to serving every Coloradan.

Important Information

This position will have hybrid workplace options available but will still be required to report to the listed address at the discretion of the supervisor and based on business needs.
The referral list generated by this position announcement may be used to fill multiple position vacancies and may be extended.

CDPHE offers:

CDPHE offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to build a meaningful career in public service. Benefits include:

Medical and dental plans.
Colorado PERA retirement options, including defined benefit plan or defined contribution plan.
Optional 401(K) and 457 retirement plans.
Employer-paid life insurance.
Short- and long-term disability coverage.
Potential flexible working arrangements
11 paid holidays per year and generous paid time off.
Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Tuition assistance.
Employee wellness programs.
Professional development opportunities.
Career opportunities throughout Colorado state government.
Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. For more information, go to: https://studentloans.gov/myDirectLoan/pslfFlow.action#!/pslf/launch

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Toxicology and Risk Assessment (TARA) Program is under the direction of the Division of Environmental Health and Sustainability Deputy Director and exists to provide epidemiologic research, surveillance data, toxicology and health risk assessment assistance, and consultation to CDPHE management, divisions and programmatic units; federal and local public health and environmental agencies and officials; and businesses and the public. Our programs span the topics of exposure to toxic substances (e.g., lead, mercury, carbon monoxide, and pesticides), cancer clusters, oil and

gas health impacts, and more.

TARA responds to community concerns about environmental exposures and disease clusters. Staff members provide expertise and oversight for state and community-based environmental health research, health surveillance, and biomonitoring.

The Regulatory Toxicology Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The Regulatory Toxicology Workgroup conducts health risk investigations and evaluates environmental exposures, hazards and health status of communities. The purpose of this workgroup is to (1) provide statewide consultation to the department's environmental programs other state agencies federal agencies (US EPA, ATSDR) local public health departments, and the general public and (2) conduct public health assessment to identify potential impacts from environmental chemical exposures. The work unit is responsible for reviewing, interpreting and presenting on the toxicological properties of chemicals as it relates to evaluating the public health risks from environmental chemical exposures.

The Emerging Issues Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The purpose of this work group is to: (1) be a resource on the relationship between PFAS/emerging issues exposure and public health for stakeholders including: TARA, DEHS, other CDPHE divisions, other state agencies, federal agencies, and the general public; (2) increase transparency and understanding of PFAS/emerging issue data and what it means for public health;

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to support science communication needs for the ECHO unit. This includes translating

complex technical information into understandable information for a variety of stakeholders through appropriate

methods. In addition, this position is responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of communications to different

stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Based on guidance and support from senior TARA staff, provides risk consultation and communication expertise on environmental health problems to local public health agencies, and other stakeholders as needed.
With support of senior outreach staff, educate communities, local public health partners, and local policymakers about environmental health risks and protective measures.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct data analysis, visualization, and interpretation to assist in data-driven decision making on environmental contaminants.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis on the effectiveness of communication and outreach methods for different stakeholders.
Participate in responding to technical inquiries from the public (i.e., Toxcall, PFAS TAP).
Assists with public workshops, seminars and other meetings.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

Residency Requirement
This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

I3B2T* Physical Science Researcher/Scientist I

Minimum Qualifications

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Natural Resources And Lands Management Division

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About The Moccasin Planning And Compliance Section Of NRLM

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Role description

Role Description

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.
Prepares or coordinates permit applications, right-of-way and special use authorization requests, and related submissions to local, state, and federal agencies.
Obtains authorizations under CWA

401/404, NPDES
402, Fish & Game Code

1602/1610, ESA/CESA, NHPA
106, ARPA, FLPMA, Raker Act, Wilderness Act, Wild & Scenic Rivers Act, and related federal/state authorities. Prepares, reviews, and coordinates CEQA, NEPA, NHPA, FLPMA, and related environmental review and compliance documentation.
Prepares and manages technical studies and reports concerning environmental, biological, cultural, land, and other natural resource matters.
Critically reviews and evaluates consultant work associated with planning, permitting, environmental review, technical studies, and compliance monitoring, and develops scopes of work and supports consultant contract administration, including schedules, budgets, deliverables, and fieldwork coordination.
Coordinates interdisciplinary review of project proposals, technical studies, and environmental documentation; performs environmental review of third-party applications for use of SFPUC lands.
Identifies environmental and regulatory risks, evaluates available information, and develops practical recommendations when requirements or project conditions are uncertain.
Represents SFPUC interests during interagency consultations, stakeholder meetings, public meetings, and field visits, and collaborates with multidisciplinary staff, consultants, regulatory personnel, Tribal representatives, and other parties.
Exercise sound and objective judgment, including when information is incomplete, requirements are uncertain, or competing priorities must be reconciled.
Manages competing priorities and communicates emerging issues, schedule risks, and recommended actions to project managers and supervisors.
Communicate complex legal, technical, and procedural information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

How to qualify

Minimum Qualifications

Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university AND four (4) years (8000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

OR

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in city/regional/urban planning, environmental studies, architecture, law, earth sciences, geography, economics, landscape architecture, civil engineering, urban studies or public administration AND two (2) years (4000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

AND

License: Possession of a current valid California Driver’s License.

Note:
One (1) year of full-time employment is considered equivalent to two thousand (2,000) hours. Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Desirable Qualifications:
The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring:

Experience interpreting or working with federal land management and permitting instruments including rights-of-way, special use authorizations, permits, easements, agreements, maps, land records, or historical authorizations.
Experience applying local, state, and federal environmental laws, regulations, and environmental review processes.
Experience with cultural resources identification, preservation, protection, consultation, and management practices.

Experience using GIS, databases, document management systems, or other tools to organize and analyze environmental, geographic, or regulatory information.
Experience developing scopes of work and supporting consultant contract administration, schedules, budgets, and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Experience coordinating with regulatory agencies, land management agencies, Tribal representatives, project managers, operations staff, consultants, attorneys, or other parties with differing responsibilities and perspectives.

Principal Environmental Consultant

About the Opportunity

A highly respected environmental consulting firm is seeking a seasoned environmental professional to join its Dallas office in a leadership capacity. This role offers the opportunity to work on some of the most technically challenging environmental projects in the country, partnering with experts across disciplines to develop practical, science-based solutions to complex environmental issues.
The successful candidate will serve as a senior technical leader, trusted client advisor, and mentor while helping expand the firm's presence across Texas and the broader region. This position is well suited for an experienced consultant who enjoys tackling difficult environmental problems, leading multidisciplinary teams, and building long-term client relationships.
Unlike many consulting environments that focus primarily on project volume, this role emphasizes technical excellence, critical thinking, and collaboration in support of complex site investigations, remediation programs, environmental risk evaluations, and strategic environmental decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Lead complex environmental consulting engagements involving site characterization, groundwater and soil impacts, remediation strategy development, risk evaluation, and regulatory negotiations.
Serve as a senior technical resource for multidisciplinary teams of engineers, geologists, hydrogeologists, environmental scientists, and risk professionals.
Provide technical direction on projects involving contaminant fate and transport, emerging contaminants, environmental forensics, corrective action programs, and redevelopment challenges.
Develop defensible technical approaches that help clients navigate environmental liabilities, regulatory requirements, and business objectives.
Build and maintain relationships with industrial, energy, manufacturing, legal, commercial, and public-sector clients.
Participate in business development efforts, including proposal preparation, client strategy discussions, and identification of new opportunities.
Review and oversee technical reports, investigation work plans, conceptual site models, risk evaluations, and remediation recommendations.

Collaborate with senior practitioners throughout the organization to solve complex environmental challenges and deliver high-quality client solutions.

Job Board Title

Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental Health

Post Date

9/28/2026

Expiration Date

10/28/2026

Details

Rice University invites applications for multiple tenured and tenure-track positions at the senior and junior levels in Environmental Health, with preferred focus areas in environmental and occupational epidemiology, environmental exposures and sustainability, environmental risk assessment, toxicology, infectious diseases, global environmental health, and climate impacts on health, as well as the intersection of these areas with environmental justice. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The ideal candidate(s) would bring an interdisciplinary approach, leveraging quantitative training in biostatistics, epidemiological modeling, spatial analytics (GIS), or AI/data science, with experience analyzing clinical (e.g., electronic medical records), registry (e.g., Texas Cancer Registry), or administrative (e.g., American Community Survey) health data.

Primary academic appointment will be in the Department of Kinesiology, ranked #1 nationally by the popular Niche™ rankings and home to Rice’s Public Health Sciences and Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology undergraduate degrees. These positions are part of an initiative to support interdisciplinary environmental health scholarship, including a new Climate + Health Excellence Center (FORECAST) funded by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund. They will come with robust joint appointments in Departments of BioSciences, Chemistry, and Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences as most appropriate.

The successful candidate(s) will be expected to establish a vibrant, externally funded research program, collaborate across disciplines, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. We especially encourage applications from scientists addressing climate impacts on human health and infectious disease, and contributing to broad themes of sustainability or One Health principles. Potential to connect to exercise science, the department’s other major intellectual theme, will also be explored, such as through interests in impacts of extreme heat, air quality, and toxicants on human physiology and performance.

Candidates must have a PhD, DrPH, or equivalent degree in public health science or a relevant field of natural science or engineering and have completed the requirements for the degree by July 1, 2027.

To apply, please submit the following materials online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193813: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research statement (3 pages max); (4) statement of teaching philosophy (3 pages max); and (5) contact information for three references. The research statement and statement of teaching philosophy may also include plans for building a diverse and inclusive research group and fostering equitable and inclusive classrooms. Applications that are received by November 16, 2026,
will receive full consideration, but we will continue reviewing applications until positions are filled. For additional information, please visit our department website or contact the search chairs, Dr. Cassandra Diep (csdiep@rice.edu) and Dr. Scott P. Egan (scott.p.egan@rice.edu).

Rice University is located in Houston, Texas, USA, and is a private, coeducational, nonsectarian university that aspires to path-breaking research, unsurpassed teaching, and contributions to the betterment of our world. **Location:** Remote

**Job Type:** Part\-Time

Southern Nevada Environmental, Inc. **(SNEI)** is seeking an experienced environmental technical writer with **prior experience on Mojave Desert projects** to prepare biological survey and environmental compliance reports for utility, renewable energy, and infrastructure projects. Much of our work involves **botanical and desert tortoise surveys**, so experience reporting on either or both is especially valuable.

SNEI needs someone who can take ownership of a report from first draft through final delivery. You will organize field data and project records, work with biologists and project managers to resolve questions, coordinate technical review, and produce clear, accurate documents for our clients.

**Responsibilities**

* Draft and edit botanical, desert tortoise, other biological survey, monitoring, environmental summary, and compliance reports.

* Develop reports using project templates, previous reporting periods, and project\-specific documentation.
* Identify missing information, conflicting figures, and unclear conclusions; work with technical staff to resolve them.
* Coordinate reviews, incorporate comments, and check consistency across report text, tables, figures, photographs, and appendices.
* Manage multiple assignments and communicate progress and deadlines to project managers.

**Required Qualifications**

* Prior experience working on Mojave Desert environmental or biological projects, including familiarity with the region’s habitats and sensitive species.
* Demonstrated experience preparing environmental or biological technical reports, preferably in an environmental consulting setting.
* Ability to interpret field data and accurately present survey methods, biological findings, and environmental compliance requirements.
* Strong writing, editing, proofreading, and organizational skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Word, including formatting complex documents and managing tables, captions, and cross\-references.
* Ability to work independently and communicate effectively with technical staff in a remote setting.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience writing botanical survey, rare plant, vegetation, habitat assessment, or desert tortoise survey reports.
* Experience with utility, renewable energy, transmission, pipeline, or other infrastructure projects.
* Familiarity with environmental and biological resource requirements of agencies such as BLM, USFWS, CDFW, or NDOW.

**Position Details**

This is a part\-time, remote role with regular weekly availability. Workload may vary with project schedules, and some reports will have firm client deadlines. **Starting pay is $40–$50 per hour, depending on relevant experience and writing samples.**

This position is part\-time and does not include benefits.

jobs.title: UAV Designer — Modelling, Simulation & Autopilot
jobs.description:
Company Description
SkyVector Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a fast-growing company based in Hyderabad, India, specializing in Advanced Electronics, Aerospace, Defence, and Electronic Warfare systems. The organization delivers cutting-edge solutions for defence and aerospace programs, combining deep engineering expertise with a strong culture of innovation. Teams at SkyVector work on indigenous product development across embedded systems, firmware, PCB design, and mission-critical electronic systems. The company is driven by precision, quality, and a passion for solving complex engineering challenges, and is actively expanding its engineering workforce. Applicants will join a collaborative environment focused on building technology that has real-world impact.

Role Description: 

UAV Designer — Modelling, Simulation & Autopilot

Hyderabad, Telangana | Fixed-Wing UAV Program | Full-Time | Defence, Aerospace & EW Electronics

Why Join Us

 Work on real, mission-critical hardware for defence and aerospace platforms — not simulations or academic exercises
 Direct exposure to founders on every major design call — this is not a siloed role several layers removed from decisions
 A genuine hand in a defence-relevant program from an early stage, including the IP and documentation that comes out of it
 We're a fast-growing company — compensation grows quickly with demonstrated performance, not just tenure

Compensation

As a startup, we're not able to match big-company salaries right now — but we're growing fast, and early team members get real ownership over what they build, faster growth in responsibility, and compensation that scales quickly with performance rather than waiting on annual cycles.

This is a hands-on flight-dynamics and autopilot role
, not a general software or coding role. You should be someone who has actually built 6-DOF dynamics models
and worked on real autopilot/GNC logic

— not just studied aerodynamics or written general-purpose code. If your background is in software development, computer science, or IT with no UAV, aircraft, or flight-dynamics project work, please do not apply.
This posting is exclusively for candidates with an Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering background and real UAV/aircraft-relevant project experience.

The Role

We're after someone who can sit across modelling & simulation, autopilot/GNC, and the aerodynamics-and-structures side of a fixed-wing airframe — not necessarily expert in all three on day one, but able to move between them without needing a translator. You'll build and maintain the 6-DOF dynamics model, help shape the autopilot logic that flies on it, and weigh in on airframe decisions (wing loading, control surface sizing, launch loads) that the model and the autopilot both depend on getting right.

Minimum Qualifications

 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering or Mechanical Engineering — aerospace is the closer fit, but a mechanical background with real aircraft or UAV project work is welcome (CGPA 7.5+ or equivalent — applications below this will not be considered)
 2–5 years working on UAV or aircraft flight dynamics, autopilot/GNC, or aerodynamics — industry, a research lab, or a genuinely serious student UAV/rocketry project all count

What You'll Be Doing

Building and maintaining 6-DOF flight dynamics models and using them to drive hardware/software-in-the-loop (HIL/SIL) testing before anything goes near a real airframe
Working on autopilot and guidance logic — L1/NLGL-style guidance, PID and lead-compensator loops, EKF-based state estimation — and tuning it against both simulation and flight-test data
Running aerodynamic analysis (stability derivatives, trim, control-surface sizing) so the airframe can actually fly the mission it's meant to
Sanity-checking structural and launch-load questions — canister-launch acceleration, wing-fold mechanisms, airframe weight budget

Debugging the gap between "works in simulation" and "works on the bench"
Writing up trajectory, launch-angle, and performance analysis clearly for the team and future reviewers

 Flight dynamics modelling (MATLAB/Simulink, Python, or equivalent) — able to build a 6-DOF model from equations of motion, not just run someone else's

 Aerodynamics background sufficient to reason about stability, trim, and control-surface authority
 Basic structural/load reasoning and airframe structural design fundamentals — load paths, material selection, basic sizing

Nice to Have

 Hands-on HIL/SIL experience, canister- or rail-launched airframe experience, familiarity with ArduPilot/PX4/custom FCS at code level, actuator control exposure, or a fly-off/competition track record (SAE Aero, DBF, or similar)

jobs.title: Senior Marine Ecologist, benthic and shellfish ecology
jobs.description:
Your job

As an experienced Senior Marine Ecologist at Wageningen Marine Research (WMR) in Yerseke, you will lead a team of dedicated researchers who are working together on a range of ecologically relevant issues of societal importance in the South-Western Delta.

As a Senior Marine Ecologist, specialized in benthic organisms and shellfish, you will use your knowledge and experience to carry out research in the South-Western Delta. You will lead a team of enthusiastic fellow ecologists with whom you will carry out research focusing on the effects of human activities such as fishing and sand replenishment, and the consequences of climate change on marine benthic fauna. You will contribute to nature conservation through the active restoration of shellfish beds in the North Sea and the Delta. You have an affinity for applied research and working in complex policy and stakeholder environments. You will initiate new research, including securing funding for it, and lead major projects.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

to act as a leading figure in the field of benthic ecology in contacts with (potential) clients and the media;
to manage and carry out large-scale and complex research projects;
securing new research and drafting multidisciplinary research proposals;
maintaining and expanding the national and international network in the field of delta- and benthic ecology and the restoration of shellfish beds;
presenting the research findings to the business community, sector organizations, civil society organizations, government bodies and fellow scientists.

Your team

Based at WMR’s site in Yerseke, you will work alongside various project teams of differing compositions. As a project leader, you will provide substantive and project-related guidance to field staff, junior and mid-level researchers, enabling them to carry out their work efficiently and thoroughly.

You will work here

Wageningen Marine Research (https://www.wur.nl/en/research/marine) (WMR) is one of the nine institutes that form part of Wageningen Research. WMR is a leading, independent research institute with sites in Yerseke, IJmuiden and Den Helder, which focuses on strategic and applied marine ecological research. Products and services are delivered on a project basis and are diverse in nature: field research, realistic-scale experiments, exploratory laboratory-scale studies, data management and modelling. The institute has modern research facilities and is ISO 9001 certified.

Your area of work will primarily be the south-western Delta, but other parts of the Netherlands, such as the North Sea and the Wadden Sea, as well as international projects, are also possibilities.

Your qualities

You are proactive, results-oriented and have excellent communication and organizational skills. You are able to maintain an overview of complex processes, work with precision and feel at ease in an environment where different interests and disciplines come together.

You Also Possess

relevant university degree and PhD in Marine Ecology;
extensive work experience as a researcher and project leader in the field of benthic ecology;
entrepreneurial spirit, decisiveness, the ability to take the initiative, good teamwork skills, and a customer- and results-oriented approach;
a good command of the Dutch language is a strong advantage.

In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) B2. If you haven’t yet reached this level, we will of course help you, and you are welcome to visit our language centre, Wageningen in’to Language (https://www.wur.nl/en/education/into-languages).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
there is a strong focus on vitality;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 4,938.- and € 7,337.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 12). Additionally, for this role a contract for 24 to 36 hours hours can be discussed. As for your contract, we initially offer a one-year contract that can be extended. Of course, we are happy to have a conversation with you if you have any questions about this.

Wageningen University & Research offers plenty of opportunities for growth and development, with a strong internal recruitment policy and excellent training programmes.

If you are an internal employee, your current contract serves as the starting point; please ask your HR Business Partner about your specific situation. We encourage development and mobility within our organization. Our recruitment and selection policy outlines the specific conditions that apply to you as a (former) employee.

Coming from abroad

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/) can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Jeroen Wijsman, Researcher Marine Ecologist, via phone number: +31 317-487114 or via email: jeroen.wijsman@wur.nl (mailto:jeroen.wijsman@wur.nl).

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Dax Teunissen, Corporate Recruiter, via email: recruitment.asg@wur.nl (mailto:recruitment.asg@wur.nl).

Ready to apply?

Click on the application button next to the vacancy on our website. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

You can apply up to and including Monday 26 October 2026.
Internal candidates are preferred to apply before 1st October 2026
.

Applications are reviewed regularly. Therefore, the position may be filled before the stated closing date.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

Wageningen Marine Research

Wageningen Marine Research (WMR) is a leading independent research institute with locations in IJmuiden, Den Helder and Yerseke. The institute focuses on strategic and applied marine ecological research. Its products and services are delivered on a project basis, with more than 400 research projects carried out annually, ranging from field studies and full-scale experiments to exploratory laboratory studies, data management and modelling. The institute is equipped with modern research facilities and is ISO 9001 certified. Wageningen Marine Research is organisationally part of Wageningen University & Research. Research within our institute focuses on understanding the spatial and temporal dynamics of individuals, populations, ecosystems and socio-ecological systems. This includes accounting for changing environmental conditions, climate change and human activities in marine and freshwater environments. We work with a wide variety of species, ranging from corals and fish to marine mammals and birds, across both benthic and pelagic ecosystems. In addition, we investigate human behaviour, for example that of fishers. To achieve this, we make use of experimental field and laboratory data, mathematical models and computer simulations.

We are

The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines.

jobs.description:
À propos

SkyVisor est une entreprise technologique qui fournit des solutions logicielles aux exploitants de centrales de production d’énergie renouvelable comme les éoliennes et panneaux solaires.

Fondée en 2018, SkyVisor permet à ses clients de digitaliser et d'optimiser la maintenance des infrastructures énergétiques afin de démocratiser la maintenance prédictive.

Grâce à ses solutions qui reposent sur des technologies de rupture comme les drones autonomes ou le machine learning, SkyVisor est devenu en peu de temps un acteur clé de l’inspection des éoliennes et parcs photovoltaïques avec une présence internationale dans plus de 30 pays.

L’entreprise cherche maintenant à accélérer sa croissance à l'international, développer de nouvelles solutions digitales et accroitre ses avancées technologiques.

Descriptif du poste

Acteur reconnu de l'inspection automatisée d'éoliennes et de centrales photovoltaïques par drones, SkyVisor recherche un Lead Android / Application
Drone
pour renforcer son équipe R&D et relever les challenges de croissance de l'entreprise.

Vous souhaitez développer des applications Android de pilotage de drones
en conditions réelles, où chaque évolution est validée aussi bien par des tests automatisés que par des campagnes d'essais sur le terrain ? Vous aimez construire des logiciels robustes, fiables et maintenables, capables de fonctionner dans des environnements exigeants ? Cette opportunité est faite pour vous !

En lien direct avec le responsable technique de SkyVisor
et en collaboration étroite avec les équipes Produit et Opérations, vous serez responsable de notre solution drone innovante afin de capturer les données et l'imagerie des infrastructures energétiques renouvelables.

Concrètement Les Missions Consistent à

Prendre le leadership technique de l'application droneApp SkyVisor et faire évoluer son architecture dans une logique de qualité, de robustesse et de pérennité.
Développer les composants logiciels et missions embarquées nécessaires au besoin des nouvelles fonctionnalités de l'application mobile, adapter l'application pour de nouveaux modèles de drones/cameras
Contribuer techniquement aux spécifications et à l'architecture, un apprentissage du métier éolien et solaire sera nécessaire
Définir et mettre en œuvre une véritable stratégie de qualité logicielle : tests unitaires, tests d'intégration, tests instrumentés Android, automatisation des tests et validation continue.
Être garant de la stabilité de l'application, de la gestion des régressions et de la fiabilité des versions livrées.
Organiser très régulièrement des essais terrains sur des éoliennes et parcs solaires (nombreux déplacements à prévoir)
Concevoir des algorithmes de plan de vol du drone et de computer vision (reconnaissance d'objets en temps réel)
Effectuer une veille permanente sur l'industrie afin de proposer des solutions innovantes et pragmatiques

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons avant tout un ingénieur qui apprécie autant le développement logiciel que la validation sur le terrain. Chez SkyVisor, un développement n'est réellement terminé que lorsqu'il a démontré sa robustesse en conditions réelles.

Vous Aimez

développer des applications Android complexes ;
concevoir des architectures maintenables et évolutives ;
automatiser les tests pour fiabiliser les livraisons ;
comprendre le comportement d'un système complet, de l'implémentation jusqu'au vol du drone ;
confronter vos développements aux essais terrain afin d'améliorer continuellement la qualité du produit.

Master, école d'ingénieurs
+3 ans d'expérience dans le développement mobile Android
Vous êtes parfaitement à l'aise avec les environnements et langages associés aux technologies Android: Kotlin, Java, Compose, Android Studio, gradle, git...
Connaissances dans le domaine des drones DJI (MSDK, PSDK), robotique/code embarqué (C/C++), la vision par ordinateur (openCV) ainsi que la photographie seraient un plus mais non obligatoire

jobs.description:
BEFORE YOU APPLY:
Please read the compensation information at the bottom of the page!

OVERVIEW

We are currently looking for concept artists for our ongoing comic book development that we are running similarly to a TV show/movie (Art Directors, Producers, Concept Art before “shooting it” (pencilling, inking etc.)).

ABOUT THE COMPANY

We are creating films, games, and comics - stories with soul - for our own fantasy universe (think Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, etc., but smaller - for now hehe). We started 4 years ago as a small team of folks who were initially supposed to package a TV show. Finding ourselves unwilling to sign away our IP, we decided to build out the universe ourselves to retain (creative) control. Now, 4 years later, our rag-tag band of pirates has grown to over 150 members (far over 200 depending on how you count).
Our current slate includes 3 short films (2 in active development, 1 in post production, 30min each), a comic book series (9 issues of Season 1, 45 pages/issue), and two games (one Card Game online and offline version featuring our characters and factions, and one TTRPG with one shots, campaign rules, and region expansions). We also produce music, art, and have our own in-house media marketing element and ops.
We have been working on getting greenlight, production up, worldbuilding ready, and marketing infrastructure set up. Now our task is mostly about improving the existing processes and bringing us into our first launches with financial implications (thus far, we took on some investment but have not made revenue yet - you first have to make a film to make box office).

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

Create concepts within a team for various projects, working under the guidance of the Worldbuilding team and Advisors
Gather references and create mood boards to convey ideas prior to design execution
Conduct research to understand the complexity of concepts in order to design them believably
Work comfortably in a grounded, realistic fantasy art style
Create concept art for characters, creatures, environments, and props
Work from structured briefs with worldbuilding and creative leadership

YOU

Proactive attitude toward skill development and growth
Experienced in background or environment design
Transparent and responsive communication
Professional working proficiency in English
Ability to adapt artistic style to the project’s aesthetic
Strong grasp of artistic fundamentals, including color, composition, value, form, anatomy, brushwork, and perspective
Bonus: Knowledge of 3D software for blockouts

COMPENSATION DETAILS

Time Investment:
Part-time. Approximately 5-15 hours/week (flexible week on week, as we understand you may have other commitments) - you set your own boundaries and communicate your availability.

Salary :
At this point, there is no salary for anyone in our team (from the CEO to the producers to the set runner, nobody draws a salary). We instead give parts of the profit away:

Profit Participation:
We are currently in the development of a profit share/royalty system that will award everyone who is part of the project a piece of the pie without causing any upfront taxation. Upon request for an interview, we will send you a detailed breakdown so you can make a decision on whether or not you want to continue with the application. This is fundamentally an investment contract (time invested, profit participation/royalties gained), and as a result, we are happy to support any due diligence you want to undergo ahead of joining.
Thank you very much for considering the collaboration.
We hope to see you on the other side and that we grow together on these exciting projects!

All the best,
Your Soul Atlas Team

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Land
jobs.description:
$85,000+ Super + Paid Overtime / TOIL

Around 2 Days Fieldwork Per Week – Mostly Sydney & Surrounds

Clear Progression into Project Ownership & PM-Level Responsibility

As an Environmental Scientist in Contaminated Land, this is a good time to join a young consultancy that has moved beyond the start-up phase and is now winning the sort of larger projects that create genuine room for people to grow with it.
They don't need another graduate, and they don't need a finished Project Manager. They need the person in between.
Someone with around 2–3 years' consulting experience who understands PSI/DSI work, can handle themselves in the field, writes a decent report and is ready to start taking greater ownership, while still having experienced PMs around them to review, guide and teach.
The business is currently tendering for larger infrastructure and contaminated land projects, while already delivering substantial investigations across industrial sites, renewables and commercial developments. As that pipeline grows, so should your role.

The Role

You'll sit between the junior field team and senior PMs, combining hands-on investigation work with reporting and gradually increasing project responsibility.

You'll:
Deliver PSI, DSI, validation and Acid Sulfate Soil investigations.
Undertake soil and groundwater sampling and broader environmental field investigations.
Work on larger contaminated land programs rather than being stuck doing endless small one-off jobs.
Contribute to investigations involving soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water.
Write PSI/DSI reports, with senior review and technical support available.
Gain exposure to RAPs and waste classifications where projects require it.
Gradually take ownership of defined pieces of work and smaller projects as your capability develops.
Spend around two days per week in the field, occasionally three depending on the project.

Current and recent work includes a 5-hectare industrial DSI covering soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water, a major renewable energy project moving into remediation, larger PSI/DSI programs and further infrastructure projects currently being tendered.
Most fieldwork is around Sydney and surrounding areas. Some sites can mean roughly two hours' travel each way, but there isn't an expectation of constant regional or overnight travel. Where practical, you can travel directly from home to site.

The Team

This is a small, growing consultancy where your contribution will be visible.
You'll have experienced contaminated land people above you for technical support, alongside junior consultants who are earlier in their careers. That puts you in a useful position: experienced enough to get on with the work, but with plenty of room to keep learning.
They're looking for someone independent without pretending you should know everything already. Take a brief, have a crack, research what you don't know and ask sensible questions when you need to.
The business backs that up with professional development, industry training and support toward relevant accreditations and memberships.
Hybrid working is available, along with company vehicles, fuel cards, full PPE, field equipment, laptop and phone. Overtime is paid and TOIL is available, with no regular weekend-work expectation.

Experience

Around 2–3 years' environmental consulting experience, predominantly in contaminated land.
Practical PSI/DSI, soil sampling, environmental investigation and reporting experience.
Some groundwater knowledge plus exposure to Acid Sulfate Soils and validation work.
Most importantly, enough initiative to take ownership of your work while still being comfortable learning from experienced PMs.

This isn't a PM job dressed up as a Scientist role. It's the step before it, with the project exposure and support to help you get there.

Salary starts from $85,000 + super, with paid overtime / TOIL available.

-------------------------------------------------

jobs.title: Senior Geospatial Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
We are looking for someone who already does production geoprocessing in Python - rasterio, geopandas, numpy - and wants the geospatial layer to be the product rather than a chore buried under someone else's roadmap.

M33 is building iris
. You can ask a spatial question in plain language - "vegetation change along this corridor over the last three years" - and iris composes a real, inspectable pipeline against satellite imagery and open vector data, which you can open, change and re-run. All orchestrated with trusted tools, with transparency and provenance about what’s happening all the way through.

We are a small but growing team. You would be joining as our second engineer, and as another geospatial specialist - so we need someone who can function as a subject-matter expert as much as a developer.

The engagement

Independent contract, not employment. Remote, anywhere you can legally invoice as a business. Up to 40 hours a week at your own schedule, with at least 8 overlapping North American hours.

US$45-55/hour
, depending on depth and location.

What you would own

Our Python processing engine - the catalog of composable geoprocessing tasks iris builds pipelines from.
Making a wrong answer hard to ship quietly. Nodata that survives masking, resampling and band maths. Reprojection that does not silently degrade. Pipelines that don’t run green if they’re returning a plausible but wrong number.
Letting someone bring their own data into a pipeline, validating it, and refusing it loudly when it cannot be trusted.
Cloud-native formats and access: COGs, STAC, GeoParquet, PostGIS, DuckDB spatial, dynamic tile serving.
New data sources and connectors - satellite collections, global vector sources, disaster-event feeds.

What we need to see

Production
experience with rasterio, geopandas and numpy. (This one is non-negotiable - substantial real work, not passing familiarity.)
A spatial problem you took end-to-end into production. Any industry: agriculture, disaster response, urban planning, logistics, environmental monitoring. What matters is that you worked through the geoprocessing and shipped something that ran.
Depth underneath those libraries - GDAL internals, coordinate systems and reprojection, raster and vector operations, STAC.
Python you would be happy for someone else to maintain, and comfort working in Docker.
The independence to set technical direction rather than wait to be told what to build.

Nice to have:
SAR or optical remote sensing, spectral indices, change detection, terrain and hydrology. Performance tuning of large raster reads. Knowing how you would prove a server does what it says it does.

How to apply

Use the link to access our (short!) application form. Tell us who you are, and one spatial problem you took into production. If you look like you might be a good fit for M33, we’ll reach out for an interview.

jobs.title: Reality Capture Technician (Entry-Level LiDAR Support)
jobs.description:
What You Will Do

Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is seeking a skilled professional to join our Engineering Services (ES) Division as a Reality Capture Technician within our Weapons Facilities Operations (ES-WFO) Group. This team supports the development of digital representations of facilities through terrestrial laser scanning and building information modeling. The program focuses on delivering accurate and reliable building data to support operations, planning, and engineering efforts across Laboratory facilities.

As a Reality Capture Technician at the entry level, you will support field scanning operations and structured data workflows. This includes assisting with scan setup, organizing collected data, and performing initial quality checks to ensure completeness and accuracy. You will work closely with engineers and designers while developing foundational skills in laser scanning, data processing, and digital modeling workflows.

Designer/ Drafter 1 ($49,600 - $76,700)

Assist with terrestrial LiDAR scanning operations using Leica systems
Set up tripods, scanners, targets, and field equipment
Support control point setup and scan logistics
Ingest, organize, and maintain scan data and metadata
Prepare scan data for processing in appropriate software tools
Perform initial quality checks such as coverage validation and file integrity
Follow established procedures, safety protocols, and structured workflows
Collaborate with engineers and designers to support facility documentation efforts

Designer/Drafter 2 ($54,900 - $84,300)

In addition to the responsibilities outlined at the lower level, you will:

Perform more advanced quality assurance and quality control checks, including basic error evaluation and validation of datasets.
Independently support portions of field data collection and processing workflows
Help define data organization standards and improve workflow efficiency
Participate in coordination with stakeholders to support project requirements and data deliverables
Apply working knowledge of design and drafting principles to support downstream modeling and engineering use

This position will be filled at either the Designer/Drafter 1 or 2 level, depending on the skills and experience of the selected candidate. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if the

candidate is hired at the higher level.

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements

Experience (0-2 years) in field data collection, surveying, GIS, facilities documentation, or related technical work
Ability to learn and apply laser scanning, Revit, and building information modeling workflows
Strong attention to detail and ability to follow structured processes and procedures
Ability to work in field environments and comply with safety and security requirements
Basic experience with computer-based tools for data handling and organization
Foundational understanding of design/drafting or engineering concepts
Ability to work both independently on routine tasks and collaboratively in a team environment
Exposure to technical standards, structured workflows, or data management practices

Additional Job Requirements for Designer/ Drafter 2:

Working-level experience supporting technical data collection, drafting, or design workflows
Ability to apply drafting or modeling principles to support engineering-related deliverables
Experience performing quality checks and resolving basic technical/ data issues
Ability to work with minimal direction on non-routine tasks and contribute to problem solving
Familiarity with Revit tools or product/ data management systems
Working knowledge of technical standards and ability to support more complex assignments

Education/Experience for Designer/Drafter 1:
Position requires a High School diploma or equivalent and 1 year of related experience.

Education/ Experience for Designer/Drafter 2:
Position requires a High School diploma or equivalent and 3 years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Desired Qualifications:

Experience with terrestrial Laser scanning system (Leica BLK360 and RTC360)
Familiarity with Autodesk ReCap, Revit, CloudCompare, or similar tools
Exposure to CAD and 3D modeling environments
Experience working in controlled or secure environments
Understanding of industry standards (such as ASME or related drafting standards)
Exposure to point cloud processing or digital twin workflows

Work Location:
The work location for this position is hybrid and is located in Los Alamos, NM. Hybrid is defined as working partially onsite/partially offsite but within 2 hours ground commute of this location. All work locations are at the discretion of management and can change at any time with appropriate notice.

Position Commitment:
Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 1 year.

Note to Applicants:
Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China - including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau - as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Where You Will Work

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network
Dental and vision insurance
Free basic life and disability insurance
Paid childbirth and parental leave
Award-winning 401(k) (6% matching plus 3.5% annually)
Learning opportunities and tuition assistance
Flexible schedules and time off (PTO and holidays)
Onsite gyms and wellness programs
Extensive relocation packages (outside a 50 mile radius)

Additional Details

Directive 206.2:
Employment with Triad requires a favorable decision by NNSA indicating employee is suitable under NNSA Supplemental Directive 206.2. Please note that this requirement applies only to citizens of the United States. Foreign nationals are subject to a similar requirement under DOE Order 142.3A.

Clearance:
Q (Position will be cleared to this level). Selected applicants will be subject to a background investigation conducted by or on behalf of the Federal Government, and must meet eligibility requirements* for access to classified matter. This position requires a Q clearance. and obtaining such clearance requires US Citizenship except in extremely rare circumstances. Dependent upon the position, additional authorization to access classified information may be required, which may or may not be available to dual citizens. Receipt of a Q clearance and additional access authorization ultimately is a decision of the Federal Government and not of Triad.

Eligibility requirements: To obtain a clearance, an individual must be at least 18 years of age; U.S. citizenship is required except in very limited circumstances. See DOE Order 472.2 for additional information.

New-Employment Drug Test:
The Laboratory requires successful applicants to complete a new-employment drug test and maintains a substance abuse policy that includes random drug testing. Although New Mexico and other states have legalized the use of marijuana, use and possession of marijuana remain illegal under federal law. A positive drug test for marijuana will result in termination of employment, even if the use was pre-offer.

Regular Position:
Term status Laboratory employees applying for regular-status positions are converted to regular status.

Ability to connect complex technical capabilities to practical client and business needs

Experience integrating geospatial data with engineering, asset management, digital delivery or BIM workflows

jobs.description:
The Role – What You’ll Do

Barr is seeking an environmental scientist to join our New Mexico team. In this hybrid role, you will support our environmental group in the characterization of environmental resources, conducting wetland delineations and interpreting permitting requirements, reporting, and supporting other project permitting and compliance.

A successful person in this role is intrinsically driven and collaborative. They will have strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills. They possess exceptional organizational skills, can work in a fast-paced environment, and have a flexible working style. They are also willing to occasionally modify their schedule to meet deadlines and/or client needs.

Your Impact – Key Responsibilities

Wetland delineations: conducting wetland delineations, inventories, and functional assessments.
Field support: conducting baseline biological surveys and other ecological field investigations.
Reporting: completing and reviewing written reports based on field findings.
Regulatory knowledge: communicating with regulatory agencies and clients and developing and reviewing environmental permit applications.
Project and task management: assisting in planning, coordinating, and executing projects. Helping ensure project milestones are met and providing regular updates to project managers and clients.

About The Opportunity

Hybrid: A hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position is based out of Barr's Albuquerque or Farmington, New Mexico, offices.
Work environment: some fieldwork locations include difficult terrain typical of backcountry (e.g., dense vegetation, fallen timber, poor footing soils, streams), roadway, and construction sites. Work may also require entering and working in facilities that include limited accessibility, moving machinery, and other conditions typical of construction or industrial facilities. Safety training will be provided.
Physical requirements: walking up to 10 miles per day in extreme temperatures of up to 90+ degrees Fahrenheit.

About You – Required Core Competencies

Education: bachelor’s degree in environmental science, studies, or policy; ecology; natural resources management; biology; botany; or a related natural resources field.
Experience: 7 years of relevant experience related to the job responsibilities described above.
Regulatory knowledge: working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act, National Environmental Policy Act, as well as state and municipal regulatory expertise in New Mexico.
Travel: ability and willingness to travel to site and client locations about 25% of the time. Time spent traveling will vary based on office location and client needs.
Driver's license: must possess a valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.

Helpful Additional Experience (not Required)

Experience with arid west geographies, bird identification, and plant identification.
Experience with renewable energy siting and permitting.
Experience with public engagement.

Compensation

Anticipated range of $80,000–$100,000 annual salary. Compensation will vary based on relevant experience, education, skill level, and other compensable factors. Employees in this position may also be eligible for a discretionary cash bonus based on team and individual performance. This position is classified as Exempt (salaried) under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

We are committed to providing an employee experience that attracts and retains top talent. That's why we offer a competitive package of employee benefits - including some unique offerings not found at other companies. At Barr, we also believe that learning doesn't stop when you get your degree, which is why we provide coaching, mentoring, and support for ongoing educational opportunities to foster professional development at every stage of your career.

Competitive, affordable insurance plans: Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, accidental death insurance, and flexible spending accounts for medical and dependent care

Profit distribution: Barr has a "no retained earnings" model and distributes all profit to our employees through our annual bonus distribution plan, ESOP, and dividends to shareholders
Professional development benefits: Annual time and expense allowances, mentorship program, and many internal training opportunities
Work/life balance: Paid time off, holidays, overtime for non-exempt/hourly staff, and compensatory time for exempt/salaried staff (time off or pay for extra time worked), paid family leave
Wellness focus: Ergonomic analysis and equipment, Personal Protective Equipment allowance, wellbeing-focused educational opportunities

At Barr, you'll join a community of engineers, scientists, and professionals who will help you achieve your ambitions and build a meaningful, rewarding career. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to clients who value Barr's tailored solutions and commitment to exceptional service.

As part of our employee-owned firm, you'll contribute to a culture of commitment and camaraderie where staff can thrive as professionals. We value diverse perspectives and experiences and believe an inclusive workplace is critical to our success.

jobs.description:
The Leibniz Centre for Tropical Marine Research (ZMT) GmbH (www.leibniz-zmt.de) is an independent research and teaching institute that provides scientific knowledge for the protection and sustainable use of tropical coastal ecosystems. To this end, we work in an inter- and transdisciplinary manner with our partners in the tropics. The ZMT is a member of the Leibniz Association.

Climate change is a well-established scientific fact, multiple lines of evidence prove that it is caused by human activities. While consensus among scientists on the role of humans as drivers of climate change is overwhelming, the public opinion remains fractured along political, generational and ideological lines. Different factors concur to maintain these fractures, including cognitive biases and the way information is produced, distributed, and accessed. In societies affected by various forms of inequalities (economical, educational, etc.), access to reliable, verified information is not distributed evenly, creating and maintaining opinions that may not conform with scientific facts. The lack of consensus in this context paralyses legislative action, fuels public polarisation, and creates legal uncertainties that prevent effective climate mitigation and adaptation strategies. By building on our previous work on opinion dynamics, we plan to develop Agent-Based Models of social influence rooted on network theory to investigate the dynamics of opinions in societies affected by cognitive biases and subject to different information structures. We are particularly interested to study three factors determining how information shapes opinion dynamics: (1) the structure of information, especially in relation to the divide between wealthy groups (which can afford premium subscriptions to high-quality factual information) and disadvantaged groups (which rely often on algorithmically driven, low-quality sources); (2) the role of inequality in voices dictating who gets a voice and who is ignored; and (3) media with agendas, involving both the broadcasting of certain stories repeatedly, while starving others of attention, and how certain stories are framed. Using computational modelling, we intend to understand how various characteristics of information may impact opinion dynamics and the formation of consensus or divides on existential matters like climate change. This research will be undertaken in close collaboration with Professor Paul E. Smaldino (from University of California Merced and Santa Fe Institute).

The working group Systems Ecology is seeking to fill an opening for a doctoral candidate (subject to release of funds).

Doctoral candidate (gn)

(Reference: 27-SE-PhD)

Your Tasks

- Investigate how cognitive biases influence opinion dynamics
- Investigate how information and media influence opinion dynamics
- Develop computational models of opinion dynamics
- Apply network theory to models of opinion dynamics
- Produce results publishable in peer-reviewed journals
- Produce and defend a PhD thesis

Requirements

Applicants must hold a Master degree in one of the following disciplines: mathematics, physics, computational sciences, social modelling, or in similar quantitative or numerical disciplines.
Knowledge or a keen interest in behavioral economics, psychology, sociology, and data science will represent an advantage.
Candidates should possess very good programming skills, possibly in python, and should have a keen interest in developing a research career focused on the mathematical modelling of social problems.
We are looking for highly motivated students with an interest in interdisciplinary studies and good communication and scientific writing competences.
The working language is English.
This study is undertaken in close cooperation with Prof. Paul E. Smaldino (from University of California Merced and Santa Fe Institute) and, pending funding availability, short visits to the University of California Merced may be required.

Further Information

For questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Agostino Merico, email: agostino.merico@leibniz-zmt.de

Remuneration is based on Pay Group 13 of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States (TV-L). The gross monthly salary is determined in accordance with the provisions of the TV-L and currently ranges from 4759.37 EUR to 6764.69 EUR employees gross salary per month, depending on the candidate’s recognized relevant professional experience. The gross salary listed here applies to a full-time position. For part-time employment, this amount should be adjusted proportionally. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the National Security Space enterprise. The Space Environment and Weather Programs (SEWP) Department directly supports USSF System Delta 810 in providing mission assurance and technical acquisition expertise for all space environment and weather programs. The SEWP Department is in need of a Space Based Environmental Monitoring Systems Engineer
. The successful candidate will support current major programs, including the Weather System Follow-On - Microwave (WSF-M) and the Electro-Optical and Infrared (EO/IR) Weather System (EWS), as well as planned prototypes and future programs.

Battelle delivers when others can’t. We conduct research and development, manage national laboratories, design and manufacture products and deliver critical services for our clients—whether they are a multi-national corporation, a small start-up or a government agency.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Summary

The Environment and Agriculture (E&A) Business Line is part of the Environment and Infrastructure Business Unit in Battelle’s Applied Science & Technology Organization. E&A is responsible for delivering strategic growth and business priorities focused on a wide range of environmental and agriculture crop protection services.

The Environmental Solutions Division is responsible for developing and delivering environmental services for contaminated sites from assessments through remediation, natural resource management, environmental data management, and general environmental support. The Environmental Solutions Division Manager will have operational responsibility for approximately 100 staff and over $50 million in revenue from Government and Commercial clients. The Environmental Solutions Division Manager is responsible for the implementation of the environmental portion of the E&A annual growth and business plan, including managing relationships with clients and other stakeholders. Specific responsibilities include.

This position is located in Columbus, OH.

Leads the Division to achieve growth year/year and profitable performance.

Responsible for the overall financial performance of the assigned group including attaining gross business volume, net income, and intellectual property goals as well as maximizing profitability, cost control, and investment decisions. Manages human resource activities such as developing recruiting strategy and hiring staff, establishing performance goals and appraising performance, and providing opportunities for career development. Manages relationships of staff and other groups.

For brilliant minds in science, technology, engineering and business operations, Battelle is the place to do the greatest good by solving humanity’s most pressing challenges and creating a safer, healthier and more secure world.

Support and participate in Management of Change (MOC) processes to ensure environmental impacts, permitting requirements, regulatory obligations, and sustainability considerations are appropriately evaluated and addressed prior to implementation.

Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered.

Demonstrated experience managing environmental permitting programs, regulatory reporting, and agency interactions.
Working knowledge of RCRA hazardous waste regulations, air permitting, water permitting, stormwater compliance, and environmental auditing practices.
Experience participating in or leading Management of Change (MOC) processes.
Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple projects, and effectively communicate across all levels of the organization.

Experience supporting Process Safety Management Programs
Knowledge of ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems
Experience with SharePoint and enterprise EHS management systems.

jobs.title: SCI Seasonal Restoration Technician
jobs.description:
Overview

SERG seeks two (2) Seasonal Restoration Technicians for habitat restoration, rare plant surveys, and other botany-related projects on San Clemente Island, a Naval installation on the southernmost of California’s Channel Islands. The Seasonal Restoration Technician position requires arduous manual labor, working outdoors in all weather, heavy lifting and carrying, and hiking on rugged terrain. This position will report to and work directly with the Crew Lead or Botany Project Manager, along with a crew of up to two other Seasonal Technicians and five other permanent staff members. The Seasonal Restoration Technician position will start on February 2, 2027, and end in May 2027. This is a full-time, hourly position. Compensation will be $23.31/hour plus a full benefits package. Housing is provided while working on San Clemente Island. The work schedule will be 10 days working on-island and 4-day weekends off-island. Housing is not provided during the 4-day weekends off-island. Transportation to and from the island is provided from the San Diego area by means of a twin engine 19-seater plane. Relocation benefits will not be offered.

All work will be conducted on San Clemente Island, which is owned and operated by the U.S. Navy as an active training site, as part of the Navy’s Natural Resources Program. San Clemente Island has a particularly unique flora, hosting 2 federally listed plants, 18 plants that are known from nowhere else in the world, and an additional 26 plants that are only known from islands off the coast of southern California or Baja. The program also supports an extensive community of biologists and researchers. Applicants should enjoy living as part of a small and remote community, and be able to maintain a professional, positive attitude at all times.

Responsibilities

The SCI Seasonal Restoration Technician is responsible for, but not limited to:

Field Work 80%

Monitor rare plant populations
Monitor vegetation cover
Maintain and monitor native species outplantings
Collect native plant propagules
Propagate native plants

Data Entry and Other Office Work 15%

Use GPS in the field and GIS software
Enter data and maintain databases

Other Duties and Responsibilities as assigned 5%
